### TD-297: Layer `update_weights()` Steps a Shared Optimizer Once per Layer

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Attention / CrossAttention | October 10, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [CrossAttention.md](../reference/source/CrossAttention.md) and confirmed by running the real
class. `CrossAttention::update_weights()` calls `optimizer->step()`, but `Optimizer::step()` steps
**every** parameter group ever registered with it, not just this layer's.
`DecoderBlock::register_parameters_with_optimizer()` registers every sub-layer with one shared
optimizer, and `DecoderBlock::update_weights()` then calls each sub-layer's `update_weights()` in
turn. With two `CrossAttention`s sharing an SGD optimizer, the second layer's weights moved a full
step on the first layer's call and again on its own: two steps. A full decoder block makes 6–10
`step()` calls per update (each also advancing Adam's step counter). `MultiHeadAttention`,
`FeedForward`, `LayerNorm`, `TokenEmbedding` and `LanguageModelHead` follow the same pattern.
Calling `set_optimizer()` twice with the same optimizer also registers the groups twice (verified:
8 groups instead of 4), doubling every update.

The shipped trainers (`ChatbotTrainer`, `RLHFTrainer`) call `optimizer->step()` once directly and
are unaffected, but the public `EncoderDecoderModel::train_step()`/`update_weights()` path
over-steps whenever an optimizer is registered. `LeJEPAEncoder` hit and fixed exactly this
(TD-178).

Action Items:

- [x] Apply TD-178's fix at the model level: when an optimizer is registered, `EncoderDecoderModel`/`LLMDecoder`/`DecoderBlock` `update_weights()` call `step()` once at the top and only zero grads below; or have layers skip `step()` when the optimizer is shared.
- [x] Make `set_optimizer()`/`register_parameters()` idempotent for the same optimizer (or dedupe in `Optimizer::add_parameter_group()`).
- [x] Test: two layers on one optimizer each move by exactly one step per `EncoderDecoderModel::update_weights()`.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-346/TD-360).** TD-178's fix is now applied at every composite level.
- **One step.** `EncoderDecoderModel`, `LLMEncoder`, `LLMDecoder`, `EncoderBlock` and `DecoderBlock` remember the optimizer they were registered with. `update_weights()` calls its `step()` once, then zeroes the gradients. Before, every sub-layer's `update_weights()` stepped the shared optimizer again. `register_lora_parameters()` also sets the model's optimizer, so `update_weights()` steps the adapters rather than running SGD on the frozen base.
- **Registration.** `Optimizer::add_parameter_group()` ignores a matrix that is already registered (and throws if it comes with different gradients), so registering twice no longer doubles updates.
- **Unchanged.** Leaf layers still call `step()` in their own `update_weights()`; that is correct for a layer with an optimizer of its own.

Test: `EncoderDecoderModelTest.OneUpdateIsOneStepWithOrWithoutAnOptimizer`: two copies of a 2+2-layer model, one with an SGD optimizer registered (twice) and one without, take one `train_step()`. The encoder's weights and the decoder's final norm must move, and the two models must give the same logits (within 1e-4). On the old code the encoder and the final norm didn't move, and the logits differed by up to 4.65.

Location in code: `src/CrossAttention.cpp` (`update_weights()`, `register_parameters()`), `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`update_weights()`); no longer tagged.

Files to Modify:

- `src/CrossAttention.cpp`
- `src/DecoderBlock.cpp`
- `src/Decoder.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `src/Optimizer.cpp`
- `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp`

|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Attention / CrossAttention | October 10, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-297 and confirmed by running the real class. `load()` pre-sets each value to
`NAN` and never checks the stream, so a file cut off after `W_k` loaded **without error** with all of
`W_v`/`W_o` NaN. `learning_rate` is read into the member before the dimension check, so a rejected
(mismatched) file still changes the layer's learning rate. `save()` doesn't check its writes. This

checkpoint path is SafeTensors (`ModelSerializer`).

- [x] Read the header into locals and assign `learning_rate` only after validation; check `save()`'s stream before returning.
- [x] Test: truncated and empty files throw and leave the layer unchanged.

**Load/save checks (October 26, 2026, with TD-423).** `save()`/`load()` reads and writes through `adai::binio` (`src/BinaryIO.{hpp,cpp}`): a short or over-long file throws `std::runtime_error`, the file is read into temporaries before anything changes, and a failed write or flush throws. Covered by `EncoderDecoderModelTest.EveryCheckpointFileIsCheckedOnLoad` and `CrossAttentionPersistenceTest.TruncatedOrEmptyFileThrowsAndLeavesTheLayerUnchanged`; `learning_rate` is assigned only after the whole file is read and validated.

| LOW | Open | Attention / CrossAttention | October 10, 2026 | 1 hour |

Description:
Found alongside TD-297 and confirmed by running the real class. The constructor validates
`d_model % num_heads` in its body, but the initializer list has already computed
`d_k(d_model / num_heads)`, so `CrossAttention(8, 0)` kills the process with SIGFPE instead of
throwing. A negative `num_heads` that divides `d_model` is accepted with a negative `d_k`.

no MNS crashes the process. `MultiHeadAttention` should be checked for the same pattern.

### TD-302: LoRA Adapters Aren't Persisted or Counted in Gradient Norms

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Attention / CrossAttention | October 10, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-297, by inspection. Neither `CrossAttention::save()` nor SafeTensors
(`ModelSerializer`) stores LoRA adapters, so unmerged LoRA training is lost on save unless
`merge_lora()` is called first. `get_gradient_norm()` covers only the base weights' gradients, so
gradient clipping and norm reporting ignore adapter gradients, which matters most when only the
adapters are trained. `MultiHeadAttention` has the same shape. LoRA has no production caller yet

### TD-304: Session Counters Can Be Duplicated and `DaemonConfigStore` Has No Busy Timeout

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open | Core / DaemonConfigStore | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DaemonConfigStore.md](../reference/source/DaemonConfigStore.md) and confirmed by running the real
class. `DaemonConfigStore` never sets `sqlite3_busy_timeout()`, so any write while another
connection holds the write lock fails immediately: with a second connection in a write
transaction, `set()` threw `database is locked` after 0.1 ms.

`LocalTransport::next_session()` (standalone trainers, no `REGISTRY_SERVER_URL`) allocates session
numbers as `load_all()` → `+1` → `set()` with no transaction and no lock. Two processes each doing
200 such increments against one `session_counters.db`:
- 284 of 400 calls **threw** (`database is locked`);
- the counter ended at **113** although 116 calls reported success, so 3 increments were lost (two
  callers handed the same session number).

`IncrementalTrainer::begin_run()` catches the throw and continues with an **empty** session ID.
`registry_server`'s `handle_session_next` is safe within one process (it holds
`g_session_store_mtx`) but would race the same way across processes. `trainer_service` and its child
also share `TRAINER_ADMIN_DIR/daemon_config.db`, so a write overlapping a child's start or exit
fails instead of waiting.

Action Items:

- [ ] Set `sqlite3_busy_timeout()` (e.g. 5 s) in the constructor.
- [ ] Add an atomic `increment(key)` (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` read-modify-write, or `UPDATE … RETURNING`) and use it in both `next_session()` implementations.
- [ ] Tests: two connections writing concurrently both succeed; concurrent increments are never lost or duplicated.

Location in code: `src/DaemonConfigStore.cpp` (constructor, `set()`), `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport::next_session()`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_session_next`); tagged `TODO: See TD-304`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DaemonConfigStore.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryTransport.cpp`
- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/daemonconfigstore_test.cpp`

### TD-305: A Rejected or Failed `PUT /admin/config` Still Partly Applies

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — trainer validate-first part fixed October 19, 2026 (with TD-519) | Admin config API | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-304, by inspection. Two problems:

- **Trainer PUTs apply keys before validating later ones.** Both `TrainerAdminAPI::handle_put_config()`
  and `TrainerServiceProxy::handle_put_config_idle()` apply the body key by key and return 400 at the
  first invalid value. `{"auto_save_enabled":false,"auto_save_every_samples":-5}` is rejected with 400,
  but auto-save is already off:
  - in a live child, in memory only, so live state and `daemon_config.db` disagree;
  - in the idle proxy, already written to the DB, so the next pass starts with auto-save off.
- **Multi-key persistence isn't atomic in any daemon.** `TrainerAdminAPI`, `ModelNameService`,
  `TrainingMetricsAPI` and `registry_server` call `DaemonConfigStore::set()` once per key with no
  transaction, after the in-memory state is already updated. If one `set()` throws (e.g. locked,
  TD-304), earlier keys are persisted and later ones aren't, and the exception escapes the handler,
  so the client sees an error for a change that partly applied and will partly revert on restart.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate every key in the body before applying or persisting any of them. Done October 19, 2026 for both trainer handlers with TD-519's
  shared `parse_trainer_admin_config()`; the tests now include a body whose third key is invalid, which changes nothing.
- [ ] Add `DaemonConfigStore::set_many()` (one transaction) and persist before (or atomically with) updating in-memory state; return a clear 500 when persistence fails.
- [ ] Tests: a body with one invalid key changes nothing; a persistence failure leaves memory and DB consistent.

Location in code: `src/TrainerAdminAPI.cpp` (`handle_put_config()`), `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp` (`handle_put_config_idle()`), `src/DaemonConfigStore.hpp`; tagged `TODO: See TD-305`.

### TD-307: `DaemonConfigStore::load_all()` Hides Read Errors

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Core / DaemonConfigStore | October 11, 2026 | 1 hour |

Description:
Found alongside TD-304, by inspection. `load_all()` stops at the first non-`SQLITE_ROW` step result
without checking whether it was an error, so a mid-scan failure returns a partial map with no
warning. The `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` result is ignored: on filesystems without shared memory,
SQLite falls back to rollback journalling where readers can be blocked, so a daemon's startup
overlay can silently drop persisted overrides.

Action Items:

### TD-309: Gutenberg Sentence Splitting Can Crash `registry_server`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / DataFetcher | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DataFetcher.md](../reference/source/DataFetcher.md) and confirmed by running the real
code. `DataFetcher::extract_sentences()` matches `std::regex("[^.!?]+[.!?]+")` over the whole cleaned
book. libstdc++'s regex engine recurses per character, so a long run with no `.`, `!` or `?` overflows
the stack: 20,000 characters was fine, but **100,000 and 400,000 characters died with SIGSEGV**.
Realistic triggers include a book in a script without ASCII sentence punctuation (e.g. Chinese, which
uses `。`), a long poem, or a large index or table.

`registry_server`'s `POST /registry/<group>/fetch/gutenberg` runs `ensure_gutenberg_cached()` →
`extract_sentences()` in its request thread, so **one fetch request kills the registry daemon**. No
sentence cache is written on the way, so every retry of the same book crashes it again.
`dataset_manager`'s local `gutenberg` command crashes the same way.

Action Items:

- [x] Replace the regex with a linear hand-written scanner (also the natural place for TD-311's abbreviation handling).
- [x] Cap the length of a candidate sentence span, and treat a book with no usable sentences as a clean failure.
- [x] Test: a 1 MB unpunctuated input returns without crashing.

Location in code: `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (`extract_sentences()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-309`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataFetcher.cpp`
- `tests/DataFetcherTests.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **Sentence splitting:** `extract_sentences()` is one linear pass with the regex's rules: a run of non-terminators plus its
  terminators; text after the last terminator dropped; a `.` between digits isn't a boundary; whitespace collapsed; 21–499 characters
  kept. A candidate stops being built once it reaches 500 characters.
- **Other whole-text regexes:** three more could overflow the same way, and are now linear loops too:
  - `clean_gutenberg_text()`'s `[ \t]+` and `\n{3,}` collapses (a long run of spaces or newlines);
  - `strip_illustration_markers()`' `\[(Illustration|…)[^\]]*\]` (an unclosed `[Illustration` before a long text).

  The per-line marker regexes only see short trimmed lines and stay.
- **Not done:** a book with no usable sentences still yields an empty list, which the existing callers already report.
- **Not changed:** TD-311's abbreviation splitting.

Tests (`DataFetcherTests.cpp`):
- `MegabyteInputsWithoutBoundariesReturnNormally`: 1 MB unpunctuated, 1 MB of words with no terminators, a 1 MB space run, a 1 MB
  newline run, and an unclosed `[Illustration` before 1 MB, through `clean_gutenberg_text()` and `extract_sentences()`. The old code
  segfaults on it (exit 139).
- `SentenceScannerMatchesTheOldRegexOnProse`: the old regex pipeline, kept in the test as a reference, gives the same sentences on
  prose with decimals, `!?` runs, line breaks, stray leading terminators and a trailing fragment.

### TD-310: HuggingFace `split` Can Write Outside the Registry Data Directory

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / DataFetcher | October 11, 2026 | 1 hour |

Description:
Found alongside TD-309 and confirmed by running the real code. `registry_server`'s
`fetch/huggingface` allow-lists `dataset_id` and `split` to `[A-Za-z0-9._-/]+`, which permits `..`
and `/`. `DataFetcher` flattens `/` in `dataset_id` but concatenates `split` into the cache path
as-is (`<dir>/<safe_id>_<split>/`), and the registry builds the training-file path from `split` the
same way. `split = "x/../../../../ESCAPED"` made `ensure_huggingface_cached()` create `ESCAPED/`
outside the group's data directory. With a real download, `parquet_info.json`, `parquet/` and
`full_dataset.jsonl` would be written there, and the produced training file and pending entry would
point there too. Any client that can reach the registry's fetch endpoint can do this.

Action Items:

- [x] Reject `..` path components (or any `/`) in `split` in the registry allow-list, and flatten `split` in `DataFetcher` like `dataset_id`.
- [x] Test: the endpoint rejects a `split` containing `..`, and `DataFetcher` never creates paths outside its output dir.

Location in code: `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (`ensure_huggingface_cached()`, `fetch_huggingface()`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`kSafeHfIdentifier`); tagged `TODO: See TD-310`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataFetcher.cpp`
- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **Registry allow-list:** `fetch/huggingface` replaces its `[A-Za-z0-9._-/]+` allow-list with `is_safe_hf_component()` (one
  `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` name, never `.` or `..`) for `split`, and `is_safe_hf_dataset_id()` (`name` or `org/name`, every component
  safe, no leading, trailing or doubled `/`) for `dataset_id`. Anything else gets 400 before any fetch.
- **Registry training-file name:** built with `flatten_for_path(split)`.
- **`DataFetcher`:** `fetch_huggingface()` and `ensure_huggingface_cached()` build the per-dataset directory with
  `hf_dataset_dir_name()`, which flattens `/` and `\` in both `dataset_id` and `split`. That also protects `dataset_manager`'s
  local `huggingface` command, which doesn't go through the registry check.

Tests:
- `DataFetcherTests.cpp`'s `SplitIsFlattenedIntoTheOutputDirectory`: split `x/../../ESCAPED` resolves inside the output directory,
  and nothing named `ESCAPED` is created outside it (offline, with a pre-created cache).
- `dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`'s `TraversalInDatasetIdOrSplitIsRejected`: nine traversal cases get 400. 90/90 live tests pass
  against a fresh server.

`"<template>" + s[i]` with `s[i+1]` and `"Summarize: " + s[i] + s[i+1]` with `s[i+2]`. The
"answer" is just whatever the author wrote next, and the "summary" is the following sentence, so the
model is trained to answer "Can you explain: X" with an unrelated continuation. `extract_sentences()`
also splits on abbreviations: `Mr.`, `Mrs.` and `Dr.` end a "sentence", so `"Mr."` is dropped and
the rest is split mid-clause (verified on Pride-and-Prejudice-style text). The template comes from
unseeded `rand()` (same sequence every run), and every pair is tagged `language="en"` regardless of
the book. Every Gutenberg fetch produces this data.

Action Items:

- [ ] Decide the intended task (the user's call). Options: plain continuation/completion pairs labelled as such (`task_type="completion"`), real QA from a better source, or dropping the QA/summary templates.
- [ ] Handle common abbreviations in sentence splitting (fold into TD-309's scanner).
- [ ] Use a seeded RNG (or no templates), and set `language` from the book's metadata or leave it empty.

|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open | Data / DataFetcher | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-309, by inspection. `download_hf_full_dataset()` logs and skips any Parquet part
that fails to download or convert, and succeeds if one part converted. `ensure_huggingface_cached()`
then treats any non-empty `full_dataset.jsonl` as complete, so the missing parts are never retried.

indefinitely. Two concurrent `fetch/huggingface` requests for the same dataset (different models, or a
retry) download into the same `parquet/part_<i>.parquet` and `full_dataset.jsonl` at once, and the
second request may see the first's half-written cache as complete.

- [ ] Download into a temp directory and rename into place only when every part succeeds; write a completion marker and check it instead of file size.
- [ ] Serialize fetches per dataset in `registry_server` (a per-dataset mutex or lock file).

parsers. `parse_assign_args()` and `parse_migrate_args()` accept any integer for `--count`, and a
value ≤ 0 with no file targets selects **everything**:
- `LocalTransport::assign()` and `registry_server`'s assign handler both treat "no paths and
  `count <= 0`" as `assign_all`.

So `dataset_manager assign my-model --count -2` (or `--count 0`) assigns **every pending file** to
`my-model`, and `migrate chatbot --count 0` migrates every legacy entry. Assigning everything is
only documented as "omit `--count`", so a typo silently turns "first N" into "the whole pool".

Action Items:

- [ ] Reject `--count` values < 1 in both parsers (keep "omit `--count`" as the only way to say all).
- [ ] Optionally have the transports/server treat `count <= 0` with an explicit count parameter as an error rather than `assign_all`.
- [ ] Tests: `--count 0` and `--count -2` are usage errors.

### TD-326: `dataset_manager migrate` Duplicates Segmented Data Across Pools

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DatasetManagerTool.md](../reference/source/DatasetManagerTool.md) and confirmed by running the real
binary against a scratch local pool. `migrate` copies each legacy entry with
`dest.add_pending_path_unchecked(entry.path)`, which **drops `segment_start`/`segment_count`**
(TD-205), then calls `source.delete_entries({entry.path}, …)` and `dest.assign_model(…)` **without
checking either result**.

Migrating a 30-pair file split into 3 segments:
- the `chatbot` pool got the **whole file** (all 30 pairs);
- the other two segments failed ("already pending");
- the source delete matched nothing (segment-aware identity), so **all 3 segments stayed in the
  legacy pool**;
- it printed "Migrated 1/3".

Training both pools trains every pair twice. Any failed source delete (e.g. a remote error) also
leaves an entry in both pools, and a failed `assign_model()` silently loses the model assignment.
`migrate` is TD-202's one-time upgrade path, so operators run it over their whole legacy pool.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 19, 2026:** `migrate` now moves each entry exactly.
- A file target takes every entry of that file.
- Each entry is added with its segment range, its model assignment is restored by segment, and the source entry is deleted by
  `(path, segment_start, segment_count)`.
- If the assignment or the source delete fails, the destination copy is rolled back and the entry isn't counted, so nothing is left in both pools.
  The result line counts entries.

Checked with the real binary on a scratch local pool holding a 30-pair file's whole-file entry and its 3 segments: all 4 moved with their ranges
(`Migrated 4/4 entries`), and the legacy pool ended empty.

There are still no command-level unit tests (TD-331). The run also showed TD-542: `segment` keeps an already-queued whole-file entry.

- [x] Carry `segment_start`/`segment_count` into `add_pending_path_unchecked()` and match/delete source entries by `(path, segment_start, segment_count)` (TD-205's `SegmentTarget`).
- [x] Check `delete_entries()`/`assign_model()` results; on failure, roll back the destination add (or report clearly) and don't count the entry as migrated.
- [x] Test: migrating a segmented file moves exactly its segments and leaves the source empty. (Checked end to end with the real binary; no unit test, TD-331.)

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`migrate`); the `TODO: See TD-326` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`
- `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`
- tests (new CLI-level test)

**Android follow-up (October 19, 2026).** The dashboard's `RegistryRepository.migrateToKind()` already carried the segment range but still ignored
its assign and delete results and returned success. It now checks both like the CLI and removes the destination copy on failure. New unit tests:
`migrateToKind removes the destination copy and fails when the legacy delete fails` and `… keeps the source when the assign fails`.

### TD-333: Segment Claims Aren't Released on Failure and Trained Records Ignore Segments

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Data / DatasetRegistry | October 11, 2026 | 4-8 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DatasetRegistry.md](../reference/source/DatasetRegistry.md) and confirmed by running the real class
against a scratch `LocalTransport` pool (one 30-pair file split into three TD-205 segments).
`acquire_pending()` hands out segments correctly, but every production caller
(`IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`'s train/resume/retrain/LeJEPA paths and
`IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()`) then calls `mark_trained()`/`release_pending()` with
**bare paths** (`resp.registry_paths()`):

- **Failure doesn't release segments.** Since TD-205, a bare path releases only whole-file entries.
  `release_pending("run-A", {path})` left the segment **claimed by `run-A`**, and a pass with a
  different `run_id` couldn't acquire it. The same `run_id` can reclaim its own claims, so an MNS
  `resume` recovers. But after a `retrain` (new MNS run), or in standalone mode (run ID from
  hostname + PID, new every pass), the segment stays stuck until released by hand.
- **Success is recorded per path.** Training two segments of one file produced **one** trained
  file with 10 samples (`build_new_versions()` skips a path already in `trained_set_`), and the whole
  path now counts as trained, so re-queuing any segment of it is **rejected**. Segments trained in
  separate passes can't all be recorded.

`registry_server`'s release/trained handlers follow the same path-keyed rules.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 19, 2026:**
- **Record format:** `DataVersion` has `segment_start`/`segment_count` (-1 = whole file). `trained_matches()` is its identity check. The local
  registry file gains two trailing columns, and older lines without them still load as whole-file records. `GET …/registry` adds two JSON fields,
  and an absent field means whole file.
- **Registry API:** `DatasetRegistry` has `mark_trained(run_id, units, counts)` and `release_pending(run_id, units)` overloads taking the
  acquired `PendingFileRange`s. Every production caller (train, retrain, LeJEPA, failure releases, `resume_last_session()`) now passes
  `resp.file_ranges()`.
  - `build_new_versions()` records one entry per unit, so segments trained in separate passes each keep their sample count.
  - `is_trained(path, seg…)` is segment-aware. A whole-file query is still true if any part was trained.
- **Releasing:** `LocalTransport::release()` and `registry_server`'s release apply whole-file paths and segments together. They used to do one or
  the other.
- **Committing:** `commit_trained()` takes an optional segment list (exact mode). `RemoteTransport` sends aligned `segment_starts`/`segment_counts`,
  and `registry_server` records per unit and removes exactly those pending entries. Requests without the arrays keep the old path-wide behaviour,
  for older clients.
- **Delete and re-queue:** a whole-file target removes every record of the path, and a segment target removes just its record. `requeue_trained()`
  restores each trained segment as that segment (TD-540's last limitation).
- **Startup sweep:** it keeps the download of a file that is trained in part but still has pending segments.
- **Empty checksums:** the registry file writes `-` for an empty checksum, so the later columns can't shift.

Tests:
- `ReleasingAnAcquiredBatchFreesItsSegments`;
- `SegmentsTrainedSeparatelyAreEachRecorded` (two records, 10 + 7 samples, per-segment `is_trained`, segment-preserving re-queue);
- `LocalTransportSegmentRecordTest` (format round trip and legacy lines);
- `LiveRegistryTest.RemoteTransportCommitsAndReleasesExactSegments`, run against a real `registry_server` (all 87 live tests pass).

These tests need the new overloads, so they couldn't be run on the old code; the old behaviour was measured when this entry was filed.

- [x] Pass `FileToken` segment ranges through as `SegmentTarget`s to `release_pending()`/`mark_trained()` from every caller.
- [x] Key trained records by `(path, segment_start, segment_count)` (local registry format, `DataVersion`, `registry_server`), and make `is_trained()` segment-aware.
- [x] Tests: acquire → fail → release frees the segment for another run; training two segments records both, with their sample counts.

Location in code: `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`, callers in `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` and `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`, `src/StartupSweep.hpp`; the `TODO: See TD-333` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`

### TD-337: `DataTransport` Names Downloads by Basename, So Segments and Same-Named Files Collide

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Data / DataTransport | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DataTransport.md](../reference/source/DataTransport.md) and confirmed end-to-end on loopback
(local `registry_server` with FTP enabled, a 15.8 MB file split into three TD-205 segments).
`fetch()` saves to `download_dir / filename(token.ftp_path)`:

- **Segments download the whole file N times, concurrently, to one path.** All three segment tokens
  had the same `ftp_path` and full-file `size_bytes`; `fetch_all()` sent all three to `dl/big.jsonl`
  in parallel, transferring the full 15.8 MB three times. The file was intact in 20 runs (identical
  bytes), but each thread opens with `trunc` and **deletes the file on a size mismatch**, so one
  thread's final check can delete another's in-progress download and fail the pass.
- **Different files with the same basename collide**, e.g. `<group>/uploads/x.jsonl` vs
  `<group>/datasets/x.jsonl`, or two kinds' sub-pools sharing one `download_dir`.

The `UsesBasenameOfFtpPath` test pins the basename behaviour.

Action Items:

- [x] Name local files from the full `ftp_path` (or a hash of it).
- [x] Deduplicate tokens by `ftp_path` in `fetch_all()` (download once, return the path for each segment token).
- [x] Tests: three segment tokens of one file trigger one download; same-basename files in different directories don't collide.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Naming:** a download is named `download_file_name(registry_path)` (`RegistryTransport.hpp`): a 16-hex-digit FNV-1a hash of the full
  registry path, then `_` and the basename. The registry path is used rather than `ftp_path` because it is all `startup_sweep()` knows, so
  the sweep matches downloads by the same name, which also fixes TD-513's basename matching.
- **One download per file:** `fetch_all()` downloads each distinct local file once and returns that path for every token of it.
- **Cleanup:** the trainer's `cleanup_downloads()` tolerates the repeated path and removes TD-338's sidecar.
- **Upgrade:** downloads made under the old basename names look orphaned to the first sweep after an upgrade, and are deleted and fetched
  once more.

Verified against a real `registry_server --ftp-enabled`, with a 13 MB file queued as three segments:
- the old `DataTransport` made 3 `RETR`s into one `big.jsonl`;
- the new one made 1 `RETR`, and all three tokens got `909f16ee7ce07427_big.jsonl`.

Unit tests:
- `SegmentTokensOfOneFileDownloadOnce` (with no server listening, only a single shared request can succeed);
- `SameBasenameInDifferentDirectoriesDoesNotCollide`;
- the updated Condition B and `fetch_all()` tests (the pinned `UsesBasenameOfFtpPath` test is replaced).

Location in code: `src/DataTransport.hpp` (`fetch()` local path, `fetch_all()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-337`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataTransport.hpp`
- `tests/DataTransportFtpTests.cpp`

### TD-338: `DataTransport` Reuses Same-Size Stale Files Without Checking the Checksum

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Data / DataTransport | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-337 and confirmed end-to-end. "Condition B" returns an existing local file
whenever its size equals `token.size_bytes`, without downloading. A planted same-name, same-size file
of different content (all `Z` bytes) was returned and would have been trained, although the token
carried `checksum = "15769547_<mtime>"`, which would have caught it. The trainer's startup sweep
keeps non-empty files, so a stale copy survives across passes. Triggers include a dataset re-uploaded
under the same name with a size-preserving edit, and TD-337's basename collisions.

Action Items:

- [x] Store the token checksum alongside each download (e.g. a sidecar file) and skip only when it matches; otherwise re-download.
- [x] Test: same-size different-checksum file is re-downloaded.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Sidecar:** `fetch()` writes the token checksum to `<download>.checksum` before the transfer starts.
- **Reuse check:** when the token has a checksum, an existing file (complete or partial) is reused or resumed only if its sidecar holds
  that same checksum. A missing or different sidecar deletes the file and downloads it again. A token without a checksum keeps the old
  size-only check.
- **Removal:** failed and mismatched downloads remove the sidecar too. `startup_sweep()` removes a sidecar with its download, or on its own
  once the download is gone.

Verified against the real `registry_server`:
- **New code:** a rerun reused the download (`[CLEANUP-B]`, no connection). After a same-size edit to the server's file, the next fetch
  logged "doesn't match the registry's checksum" and downloaded the new content.
- **Old code:** with a locally edited same-size copy, it skipped the download for all three tokens and kept the edited bytes.
- **Tests:** `SameSizeFileWithDifferentChecksumIsDownloadedAgain`, and the sweep's sidecar cases in
  `TrainedFileWithSameBasenameDoesNotDeleteAPendingDownload`.

Location in code: `src/DataTransport.hpp` (`fetch()` Condition B); tagged `TODO: See TD-338`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataTransport.hpp`
- `tests/DataTransportFtpTests.cpp`

### TD-339: FTPS Downloads Don't Verify the Registry's Certificate

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / DataTransport | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-337, by inspection. With FTPS enabled, `fetch()` sets `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER`
and `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST` to 0 to accept the registry's self-signed certificate. The control
channel is encrypted, but anyone able to intercept the connection can impersonate `registry_server`,
serve arbitrary training data, and collect the one-time credentials. There's no option to pin the
server certificate or trust a private CA. This pairs with TD-284 (`registry_server` ignores the
config file's FTPS keys).

Action Items:

- [x] Add a trainer config option for a CA bundle or pinned certificate (`CURLOPT_CAINFO` / `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY`), enable verification when set, and warn loudly when FTPS runs unverified.

Location in code: `src/DataTransport.hpp` (`fetch()` FTPS options); tagged `TODO: See TD-339`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataTransport.hpp`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `DataTransport` takes an `FtpsVerification` (`ca_file`, `pinned_public_key`). The trainer fills it from
two new `config.trainer.conf` keys, also read from the environment and carried through `DatasetConfig` to `resolve_pass_files()`:
- **`FTPS_PINNED_PUBLIC_KEY`:** curl's `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY` (`sha256//<base64>` or a public-key file), checked on its own, so it
  authenticates the default self-signed certificate. `registry_server` now logs its pin at startup (`[FTP/TLS] Certificate public-key
  pin …`, `FtpDataServer::public_key_pin()`). A generated certificate's key changes on every restart, so a pinned deployment should give
  `registry_server` `--ftp-cert`/`--ftp-key`.
- **`FTPS_CA_FILE`:** a PEM CA bundle (or the registry's own certificate). It turns on peer and hostname verification
  (`VERIFYPEER`/`VERIFYHOST 2`), so the certificate must name the host `registry_server` advertises.

With either key set:
- a registry that offers plain FTP is refused before any credentials are sent;
- a missing CA file fails before connecting.

With neither set, FTPS works as before and logs one loud warning per process.

**Found while testing:** `FtpDataServer` survived a client that dropped a TLS session only because `httplib::Server`'s constructor
ignores SIGPIPE process-wide; OpenSSL writes with plain `write()`. In the test process the wrong-pin case killed the server with SIGPIPE
(exit 141). `FtpDataServer::start()` now ignores SIGPIPE itself. The shipped `registry_server` was not affected (30 wrong-pin `curl`
connections against the real binary, which survived).

Tests:
- `DataTransportFtpsTests` (new; a real `FtpDataServer` with FTPS serving a real libcurl `DataTransport` on loopback):
  - the server publishes a well-formed pin;
  - the matching pin downloads;
  - a different pin is refused (the impersonation case, which the old code accepted);
  - a CA file must sign the server's certificate (generated with SAN `IP:127.0.0.1`; a different self-signed certificate is refused);
  - a missing CA file fails before connecting;
  - configured verification refuses plain FTP;
  - unverified FTPS still downloads;
  - the keys reach `DatasetConfig`.
- `config_test`: `FtpsVerificationKeysLoad`.
- The new tests can't build against the old code, which had no verification API. Its `fetch()` set both checks to 0 and no pin, which
  is the path `UnverifiedFtpsStillDownloads` covers.

### TD-341: World-Model and Hippocampal Gates Never Train in Production

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 20, 2026 | Transformer / DecoderBlock | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DecoderBlock.md](../reference/source/DecoderBlock.md) and confirmed by running the real class.
`DecoderBlock`'s TD-180 gates (`gate`, `gate_h`) are plain floats updated only by plain SGD inside
`DecoderBlock::update_weights()`; `register_parameters_with_optimizer()` doesn't register them
(`Optimizer` takes only `Matrix` groups). `ChatbotTrainer` never calls `update_weights()`: it
registers the model with one optimizer and calls `optimizer->step()` directly (which is also how it
avoids TD-297). So **nothing ever updates the gates**.

A block with the world-model path enabled, trained 50 steps the way `ChatbotTrainer` does, ended at
`gate = 0.000000` (gradients up to 34 were computed, then zeroed). With `tanh(gate) = 0` the gated
cross-attention's own gradient is also zero, so its weights didn't change at all. The same 50 steps
via `update_weights()` moved the gate to −1.04. World-model injection (TD-180/181/186) and
hippocampal memory (TD-185/194) therefore remain exact no-ops in every trained model, whatever MNS
links. Nothing reads `get_gate()` outside tests, so no metric reveals it.

Action Items:

- [x] Make each gate a 1×1 `Matrix` (value + gradient) and register it in `register_parameters_with_optimizer()`; drop the plain-SGD gate step from `update_weights()` (or keep it only for the no-optimizer case).
- [ ] Push per-layer `tanh(gate)`/`tanh(gate_h)` as a training metric so a stuck gate is visible. (Partly: logged per epoch; a metrics-pipeline series still needs a reporter method, server storage and a dashboard view.)
- [x] Test: training via the trainer's optimizer-only path moves a gate off zero.

Location in code: `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`update_weights()`, `register_parameters_with_optimizer()`), `src/DecoderBlock.hpp` (gate members); tagged `TODO: See TD-341`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DecoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (metrics)
- `tests/decoderblock_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Registered gates:** `gate`/`gate_h` (and their gradients) are 1×1 `Matrix` members.
  `register_parameters_with_optimizer()` adds each as a parameter group when its path is allocated, so
  `ChatbotTrainer`'s `optimizer->step()` moves them. `update_weights()` keeps its plain-SGD gate step only when no
  optimizer is registered (`gate_optimizer_`). The accessors and the checkpoint format (one float per gate) are
  unchanged.
- **Visibility:** at the end of each epoch, `ChatbotTrainer` logs per-layer `tanh(gate)`/`tanh(gate_h)`
  (`Epoch N gates tanh(gate): L0 world=… L0 memory=…`), only for a model with gated paths. A stuck gate now shows in
  the trainer log and `/admin/logs`.
- **Optimizer state:** a gated model has two more parameter groups per gated block, so a `<checkpoint>.optimizer`
  saved before this fix no longer matches. `Optimizer::load_state()` warns and keeps fresh moments once (TD-269's
  existing mismatch handling). AdamW's global weight decay (TD-469) also applies to the gates.
- **GPU training:** the gated paths still don't run there (TD-342), so the gates get no gradient and stay at 0 on a
  GPU pass. They are host groups of `GPUOptimizer`. This fix makes them learn in CPU training.

Tests:
- `decoderblock_test.cpp`:
  - `OptimizerOnlyTrainingOpensBothGates`: 30 optimizer-only steps open both gates, and the gated inputs then change
    the output.
  - `UpdateWeightsStillStepsGatesWithoutAnOptimizer`.
- `encoderdecoder_test.cpp`:
  - `TrainerStyleOptimizerStepsOpenTheGates`: a model with a `LeJEPAEncoder` attached, trained the way
    `ChatbotTrainer` does, opens every block's world-model gate.

The first and third fail on the old code (gates exactly 0, output unchanged).

**Follow-up (October 20, 2026, TD-342).** The gates now train on the GPU too, as device parameters, and the per-epoch log
reads their live device values.

### TD-342: KV-Cached Generation and the GPU Path Skip the Gated Paths

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 20, 2026 | Transformer / DecoderBlock | October 11, 2026 | 4-8 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-341, by inspection (documented in the class header). `forward_with_cache()` has no
world-model or memory parameters, and its no-cache fallback calls `forward()` without them, so every
KV-cached generation strategy (greedy, sampling, …) ignores an attached world model and hippocampal
memory; only the non-cached beam branch passes them (TD-186). `gpu_forward()`,
`gpu_forward_with_cache()` and `gpu_backward()` implement only the core sub-layers, and the GPU
upload/download/zero helpers skip the gated sub-layers, so GPU training never trains them either.
Once TD-341 is fixed, inference behaviour will differ by generation strategy and device.

Action Items:

- [x] Thread `world_model_output`/`memory` (and the hippocampal knobs) through `forward_with_cache()` and `LLMDecoder::forward_with_cache()`, caching the world-model K/V like the encoder's.
- [x] Add the gated paths to the GPU forward/backward and the upload/download/zero helpers, or refuse to enable them on GPU with a clear error.

Location in code: `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`forward_with_cache()`, GPU functions); tagged `TODO: See TD-342`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DecoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/Decoder.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).** The owner chose the full GPU scope.
- **CPU cached generation:**
  - `DecoderBlock::forward_with_cache()` and `LLMDecoder::forward_with_cache()` take the world-model output, memory and
    hippocampal settings. Both forwards share one helper, `apply_gated_paths()`.
  - The KV-cached `model_fn` in `generate_response()`/`generate_response_with_strategy()` passes them, so greedy and sampling
    decoding use the world model and memory like beam search.
  - The world-model K/V are recomputed each step rather than cached; the sequence is short.
- **Gate kernels:** `gated_residual_add_gpu()`/`gated_residual_backward_gpu()`, in CUDA and SYCL. They read `tanh(gate)` from
  a 1×1 device parameter and accumulate the gate gradient on the device.
- **Decoder block on the GPU:**
  - `gpu_forward()`/`gpu_forward_with_cache()` run both gated paths after the cross-attention residual, and `gpu_backward()`
    backpropagates them in reverse order.
  - The upload, download, collect and zero helpers include the gated sub-layers and both gates. `GPUOptimizer` therefore steps
    them on the device: a gated model has no host groups.
  - `current_gate()`/`current_gate_h()` read the live device values. `ChatbotTrainer`'s per-epoch gate log (TD-341) uses them,
    since the host copies are refreshed only at checkpoints.
- **Hippocampal path on the GPU:**
  - `CrossAttention::gpu_forward()` takes an optional score bias (added after scaling, before the mask, as
    `forward_with_scores()`), and `gpu_last_mean_attention_weights()` downloads the mean attention weights.
  - The coverage and association state stays in `HippocampalMemory` on the host. Each call uploads the keys and score bias
    and downloads the weights; both are small.
  - The bias and the update are shared with the CPU path (`hippocampal_score_bias()`, `update_hippocampal_memory()`).
- **World model on the GPU:** `LeJEPAEncoder::gpu_encode()` runs the frozen world model on the device. Its weights are
  uploaded on first use and again after `load()`. `EncoderDecoderModel` uses it for GPU training (on the decoded input, as
  `forward()`), for GPU generation, and for memory writes when the GPU is active.
- **Memory writes:** GPU generation now writes the response to the memory, as the CPU paths do (TD-185); it never did.

Tests:
- **CPU:** `decoderblock_test.cpp`'s `CachedForwardAppliesTheGatedPaths` (cached equals full forward with both gates open).
- **GPU** (`gpu_optimizer_test.cpp`, on the oneAPI CPU device):
  - the gate kernels against the host formula;
  - the GPU score bias against `forward_with_scores()`;
  - a block's GPU gated forward and backward against the CPU (output, input gradient, both gate gradients, memory coverage);
  - `gpu_encode()` against `encode()`;
  - a gated model training on the device with 0 host groups and opening both gates of every block.
- **Real binaries** (SYCL, CPU device): a LeJEPA pass, then a chatbot pass with the world model and memory attached. All 84
  groups were stepped on the device and the world-model gates opened across two resumed passes.

The memory gates stayed at 0 in that run, because training never writes the memory (only generation does). With nothing to
attend to, the hippocampal path is inactive. That run also found TD-548.

CUDA is compile-checked only.

### TD-343: Hippocampal Memory Is Updated on Every Forward Pass

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 21, 2026 | Transformer / DecoderBlock | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-341, by inspection. When `memory` is passed, `forward()` decays and accumulates
coverage and Hebbian associations on **every** call: training forwards, validation forwards, and one
call per hypothesis in beam search (the only generation branch that passes memory). The design
("called once per decode step") assumes one update per generated token, so coverage and associations
build up several times faster than intended, strengthening the repetition penalty and cross-reference
pull, and training passes pollute the persistent memory state that's saved on shutdown.

**Update (October 11, 2026, from [Decoder.md](../reference/source/Decoder.md)):** `LLMDecoder` passes the
same `memory` to every block with the gated path, and each block updates it, so one forward applies
one decay-and-accumulate round **per injected layer** (6 with `WORLD_MODEL_INJECT_EVERY_N_LAYERS = 1`
and 6 layers). The fix should update memory once per forward, at the decoder or model level.

**Update (October 11, 2026, from [EncoderDecoderModel.md](../reference/source/EncoderDecoderModel.md)):**
`generate_response()` writes the response into hippocampal memory after every CPU generation, including
`ChatbotTrainer`'s label-backfill and generation-quality calls on the live model, so training-time
evaluation also writes episodic memories. Only serving generations should write.

Action Items:

- [x] Separate scoring from state update: let the caller commit coverage/association updates once per decode step (and never during training/validation unless intended).
- [x] Test: beam search with width k updates coverage once per step.

Location in code: `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`forward()` hippocampal coverage/association update); tagged `TODO: See TD-343`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DecoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `src/HippocampalMemory.{hpp,cpp}`

**Note (October 20, 2026, TD-342).** The GPU forward and KV-cached generation now update the memory too, through the same
shared `update_hippocampal_memory()`, so this per-forward update also happens there.

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Forwards only read the memory:** `DecoderBlock`'s forwards (CPU, KV-cached and GPU) read the memory for scoring and never
  update it.
  - `last_hippocampal_attention()` returns the last forward's mean attention weights. On the GPU they are downloaded only when
    asked, so GPU training no longer downloads them every forward.
  - `LLMDecoder::last_hippocampal_step_weights()` averages the newest token's row over the blocks whose path ran: one update per
    step, not one per injected layer.
- **One commit per step:** the update moved to `HippocampalMemory::commit_attention()`. Every generation path (CPU and GPU, beam and
  cached) commits it through a `HippocampalStepCommitter`, once per decode step.
  - A step is a token length, and beam hypotheses at the same step are averaged.
  - The pending step is flushed when generation ends.
  - All hypotheses in a step now see the same coverage, from the end of the previous step.
- **Training and validation:** teacher-forced forwards never commit.
- **Training-time generation:** `EncoderDecoderModel::set_hippocampal_updates_enabled(false)` stops step commits and response writes.
  `ChatbotTrainer::train()` sets it for its whole run (restored on exit), so quality and backfill generations no longer pollute the
  serving memory.
- **Diagnostics:** `HippocampalMemory::committed_steps()` counts committed steps.

Tests:
- `encoderdecoder_test.cpp`:
  - `BeamSearchCommitsOncePerDecodeStep`: beam width 3, two injected layers, at most 10 tokens → at most 10 commits. Before,
    about width × layers per step.
  - `CachedDecodingCommitsOncePerToken`.
  - `TrainingForwardsAndDisabledUpdatesLeaveTheMemoryAlone`.
- `decoderblock_test.cpp`: `CommittedStepStrengthensAssociationBetweenAttendedSlots` (a forward alone leaves coverage and
  associations at 0). The coverage and association bound tests commit after each forward.
- `gpu_optimizer_test.cpp`: the GPU block test commits from both paths and compares coverage.

### TD-346: `LLMDecoder::update_weights()` Never Updates the Final Norm

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Transformer / Decoder | October 11, 2026 | 1 hour |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [Decoder.md](../reference/source/Decoder.md) and confirmed by running the real class.
`update_weights(float lr)` calls the token embedding's and every block's `update_weights()`, but the
final norm's update is commented out ("For now, we'll skip if the method doesn't exist"), although
`LayerNorm::update_weights()` exists; the `lr` argument is ignored. Twenty steps through this path
moved the token embeddings (L1 0.22) while the final norm's gamma and beta stayed exactly unchanged.
`EncoderDecoderModel::update_weights()`/`train_step()` use this path; the shipped `ChatbotTrainer`
calls `optimizer->step()` and is unaffected.

Action Items:

- [x] Call `final_norm->update_weights()` (in the no-optimizer case; with an optimizer, fold into TD-297's single top-level `step()`); remove or honour the unused `lr` parameter.
- [x] Test: `update_weights()` changes the final norm's parameters.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-297/TD-360).** Without an optimizer, `LLMDecoder::update_weights(lr)` applies `lr` to every sub-layer (`set_learning_rate()`) and updates the token embedding, every block and the final norm. With one, it steps it once (TD-297). Test: `EncoderDecoderModelTest.OneUpdateIsOneStepWithOrWithoutAnOptimizer`: two copies of a 2+2-layer model, one with an SGD optimizer registered (twice) and one without, take one `train_step()`. The encoder's weights and the decoder's final norm must move, and the two models must give the same logits (within 1e-4). On the old code the encoder and the final norm didn't move, and the logits differed by up to 4.65.

Location in code: `src/Decoder.cpp` (`update_weights()`); no longer tagged.

### TD-347: Cached and Full Decoder Forwards Diverge Past `max_seq_length`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Transformer / Decoder | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-346 and confirmed by running the real class. Within `max_seq_length` the KV-cached
incremental forward matches the full forward (|Δ| = 0.000002). Past it they split:
`PositionalEncoding::forward()` leaves rows beyond `max_len` without positional encoding (stderr
warning), while `forward_with_cache()` and `gpu_decode_step()` compute positional encoding inline for
any position. With `max_seq_length = 4` the last token of a length-6 sequence differed by 13.6 (L1 over
`d_model = 16`). Over-length generation therefore produces different hidden states depending on the
strategy (KV-cached greedy/sampling vs full-recompute beam), and neither has positions the model was
trained on.

Action Items:

- [x] Cap decoder input + generated length at `max_seq_length` in generation (truncate the oldest context or stop), and make the cached paths refuse or clamp positions ≥ `max_seq_length` consistently with `PositionalEncoding`.
- [x] Test: generation never exceeds `max_seq_length`; cached and full forwards agree at the boundary.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Cached forward.** The CPU `forward_with_cache()` takes its positional rows from `PositionalEncoding`'s table and adds none at or past
  `max_seq_length`, like the full forward; the GPU cached path already did so (TD-547). This also removes one of TD-478's inline copies
  of the formula.
- **Generation cap.** Every generation entry point (`generate_response()`, `gpu_generate_response()`, and both
  `*_with_strategy()`) caps the length at `max_seq_length` through `capped_generation_length()`, so the decoder never sees
  positions the model has no encoding for. Generation stops there.

Tests:
- `CachedMatchesFullPastMaxSeqLength` (`inference_optimization_test.cpp`): 6 tokens at `max_seq_length = 4`, cached vs full within
  1e-3 at every step. The old code diverged by 4.0 and 7.7 L1 at positions 4 and 5.
- `GenerationNeverExceedsMaxSeqLength` (`encoderdecoder_test.cpp`): `max_length = 100` at `max_seq_length = 8` stays within 8
  tokens for plain, greedy, sampling and beam generation. The old code produced 92–99.

Location in code: `src/Decoder.cpp` (`forward_with_cache()`, `gpu_decode_step()` positional encoding); tagged `TODO: See TD-347`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Decoder.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `src/PositionalEncoding.cpp`

**GPU follow-up (October 19, 2026, TD-547).** `LLMDecoder::gpu_decode_step()` now takes positional rows from the shared table, adding none past
`max_seq_length`, like the full forward. So the GPU cached path no longer diverges this way; the CPU `forward_with_cache()` still does.

### TD-349: RAG Indexes Whole Files but Embeds Only Their First `max_seq_length` Tokens

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open | RAG / DocumentStore | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DocumentStore.md](../reference/source/DocumentStore.md) and confirmed by running the real class.
`chatbot_api_server` adds each top-level `.txt` file under `RAG_DOCS_PATH` as **one** `DocumentStore`
document (no chunking), and `LLMEncoder::encode()` truncates input to `max_seq_length` tokens before
embedding. A long document is therefore represented by its opening only. With `max_seq_length = 16`,
two documents sharing their first 16 tokens got **bit-identical embeddings** and tied on every query,
including one matching the tail of one of them exactly. At the default `MAX_SEQ_LENGTH = 512`,
content past roughly the first page of each file is unretrievable, yet the whole file text is what
`RAGInference` puts in the prompt.

| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 27, 2026 | RAG / DocumentStore | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-349, by inspection. `retrieve()` is `const` but calls `encoder->encode()`, which
mutates the encoder's caches (`requires_grad` defaults to true) and prints `Encoding N tokens...` to
stdout on every query; `DocumentStore` has no lock. Today RAG generation runs under
`ChatbotAPI::config_mutex_` (TD-230), so requests are serialized and there's no race. Fixing TD-230
by releasing that lock, as its own action item suggests, would expose concurrent `retrieve()` calls
to data races inside the encoder.

Action Items:

- [x] Before (or with) TD-230: give `DocumentStore` a mutex around encode+score, or put the RAG encoder in inference mode (`set_requires_grad(false)`) and make `encode()` side-effect free; drop the stdout print.
- [x] Test: concurrent `retrieve()` under TSan.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `DocumentStore` has a mutex held by every method, so a query is encoded and scored under it and
documents can be added while others retrieve. `LLMEncoder::encode()` logs its token count at debug level instead of printing to
stdout on every call (the constructor and save/load prints stay with TD-367). Tests: `ConcurrentRetrieveMatchesSerialResults` (four
threads get the same hits and scores as serial queries) and `AddDocumentWhileRetrieving`. Under TSan (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`) the old
code reported 74 data races and 4 heap-use-after-frees in these two tests; the fixed code reports none. Pointers `retrieve()` returns
are still valid only until the next add/remove/clear, as documented.

Location in code: `src/DocumentStore.cpp` (`retrieve()`); tagged `TD-350`.

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [EncoderBlock.md](../reference/source/EncoderBlock.md), by inspection. `get_gradient_norm()`

### TD-358: GPU Training Feeds Unshifted Targets, Teaching the Model to Copy Instead of Predict

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours (plus retraining every GPU-trained checkpoint) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [EncoderDecoderModel.md](../reference/source/EncoderDecoderModel.md). `EncoderDecoderModel::gpu_forward()`
calls `decoder->gpu_decode(target_tokens, …)` with the **unshifted** targets as decoder input, then
`matrix_cross_entropy_loss_gpu()` scores row *t* against `targets[t]`. Under the causal mask,
position *t* sees `targets[t]` itself, so the loss is minimized by copying the current input token.
The CPU `forward()` correctly feeds `[BOS] + target[:-1]`. `gpu_backward()` and `gpu_evaluate()` use
the same misalignment, so training and validation loss look excellent.

`ChatbotTrainer` uses this path whenever `ADAI_ENABLE_GPU` is set, i.e. every `incremental_trainer`
pass on ai-machine (SYCL). **Reproduced on the CPU** with the same model classes and the GPU path's
exact decoder input, on a tiny echo task (150 epochs each):

| Decoder input during training | Final loss | Greedy generation exactly right |
|---|---|---|
| `[BOS] + target[:-1]` (CPU `forward()`) | 0.0008 | 12 / 12 |
| `target` unshifted (GPU `gpu_forward()`) | 0.0006 | **0 / 12** (`2 2 2 17 17 17 …`) |

The GPU-style model reaches equally low loss but can't generate: it learned "output the token I was
given". Every checkpoint trained on the GPU path needs retraining after the fix.

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** `EncoderDecoderModel::make_decoder_input()` builds `[BOS] + target[:-1]` and both `forward()` and
`gpu_forward()` use it (`target_tokens` stay the labels, so `gpu_backward()` needed no change); `gpu_forward()` now throws
`invalid_argument` for an empty target. Verified on the oneAPI CPU SYCL device (scratch build with CPU devices enabled): pre-fix
`gpu_forward()` loss matched the unshifted CPU reference exactly (4.879566, against the shifted 4.751482); post-fix it matches the CPU
`forward()` loss exactly on three pairs. New tests `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.GpuForwardLossMatchesCpuForwardTeacherForcing` (failed
before the fix, passes after) and `GpuForwardRejectsEmptyTarget` run on any GPU build with a device; the first also fails while the
TD-384 kernel race is present, so the two land together. Remaining: run the tests on ai-machine, then retrain.

Action Items:

- [x] In `gpu_forward()`, build the decoder input exactly as `forward()` does (`[BOS] + target[:-1]`, via one shared helper) while keeping `targets` as the labels.
- [x] Add a CPU-vs-GPU equivalence test (same weights → same logits and loss for `forward()` and `gpu_forward()`).
- [ ] Run it on ai-machine (with TD-384's fix); until GPU CI exists, ship a run package for the remote host.
- [ ] Retrain affected models; consider bumping the checkpoint format version so GPU-trained pre-fix checkpoints are flagged.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`gpu_forward()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-358`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp`

### TD-359: `generate_response()` and `gpu_generate_response()` Ignore `max_length`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | October 11, 2026 | 1 hour |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358 and confirmed. Neither method forwards its `max_length` argument to
`TextGenerator`, which uses its stored `max_length` (initially `max_seq_length`):
`generate_response("hello world", 5)` produced 9 tokens with the generator at 64. The GPU version
documents it ("kept for interface parity"). `ChatbotTrainer`'s generation-quality metrics
(`generation_quality_max_tokens = 50`) and label backfill call `generate_response()`, so their
generations can run to `max_seq_length`, slowing metric computation. The `_with_strategy` variants do
honour `max_length`.

Action Items:

- [x] Apply `max_length` for the call (temporarily set it on the generator config and restore it, or pass it through), on both CPU and GPU.
- [x] Test: `generate_response(…, 5)` returns at most 5 new tokens.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `generate_response()` and `gpu_generate_response()` apply their `max_length` for the call through a scoped
override (`ScopedMaxLength`, under the model lock), and the generator's stored value is put back afterwards. `max_length <= 0` keeps
the stored value. `ChatbotTrainer`'s generation-quality and backfill calls now stop at `generation_quality_max_tokens` (50) and
`generation_backfill_max_tokens` instead of running to the stored length. (The count still includes BOS, TD-516.)

Tests:
- `GenerateResponseHonoursMaxLength` (CPU): three inputs at `max_length = 5` stay within 5 tokens with the generator at 64, a limit of
  40 gives longer output, and the stored 64 is unchanged. The old code returned 10, 12 and 14 tokens.
- `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.GpuGenerateResponseHonoursMaxLength`: the same on the GPU path, run on the oneAPI CPU device
  (`ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`, `build/sycl-cpudev`).

**Test update (October 26, 2026).** `GenerateResponseHonoursMaxLength` and its GPU twin failed about 1 run in 15: the untrained, unseeded model (TD-368) sometimes stopped before 6 tokens, and re-encoding the decoded answer doesn't count tokens exactly. Both now decode greedily with the special tokens ruled out, and check that the 5-token answer is a strict prefix of the 40-token one (40 of 40 runs pass).

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`generate_response()`, `gpu_generate_response()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-359`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp`

### TD-360: `EncoderDecoderModel` No-Optimizer Path Never Updates the Encoder

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358 and confirmed. `update_weights()` and `set_learning_rate()` skip the encoder
(the calls are commented out: "LLMEncoder doesn't have this method"), and the LM head's LR isn't set
either. **Corrected October 11, 2026** ([LLMEncoder.md](../reference/source/LLMEncoder.md)): that
comment is stale for `set_learning_rate()`, which `LLMEncoder` has had since the TD-093 fix; only
`LLMEncoder::update_weights()` is missing. Ten `train_step()` calls with no optimizer left the encoder's weights exactly unchanged while
the decoder's moved. Combined with TD-346 (final decoder norm), `train_step()` trains only the decoder
blocks, embeddings and head. `ChatbotTrainer` registers an optimizer and is unaffected.

Action Items:

- [x] Add `LLMEncoder::update_weights()`, call it and the existing `LLMEncoder::set_learning_rate()`; set the head's LR; fold into TD-297's single-step design for the optimizer case.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-297/TD-346).** `LLMEncoder::update_weights()` is new: it steps a registered optimizer once, or runs plain SGD in the token embedding, every block and the final norm. `EncoderDecoderModel::set_learning_rate()` reaches the encoder and the LM head. The no-optimizer `update_weights()` updates the encoder, the decoder (final norm included) and the head; with an optimizer it steps once. Test: `EncoderDecoderModelTest.OneUpdateIsOneStepWithOrWithoutAnOptimizer`: two copies of a 2+2-layer model, one with an SGD optimizer registered (twice) and one without, take one `train_step()`. The encoder's weights and the decoder's final norm must move, and the two models must give the same logits (within 1e-4). On the old code the encoder and the final norm didn't move, and the logits differed by up to 4.65.

### TD-361: Training Targets Get a Double `BOS`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358 and confirmed. Targets are tokenized with `encode(response, true)` =
`[BOS, w1…wn, EOS]` (in `train_step()` and `ChatbotTrainer`'s tokenization), and `forward()` prepends
another `BOS`, so the decoder input is `[BOS, BOS, w1…wn]` and position 0 is trained to predict `BOS`
from `BOS`. Generation follows suit: from `[BOS]`, a trained model first emits a second `BOS`
(`2 2 12 23 …` in the TD-358 experiment), wasting a step and a `max_length` slot.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** chose the first option. `EncoderDecoderModel::strip_leading_bos()` drops the tokenizer's leading `BOS`
from training targets, so targets are `[w1…wn, EOS]` and `make_decoder_input()` supplies the only `BOS`. It's used in `train_step()`,
`evaluate()`, `gpu_evaluate()` and `ChatbotTrainer::preprocess_data()` (training and validation). CPU and GPU share `make_decoder_input()`,
so both are consistent. `truncate_target_keep_eos()` now keeps the first `max_seq_length − 1` content tokens plus `EOS`.

`kPreprocessFormatVersion` was bumped to 3, and the `SpecialTokens.hpp` example was updated.

New tests:
- `StripLeadingBosOnlyRemovesALeadingBos`.
- `TrainedModelsFirstPredictionIsTheFirstWordNotBos`: after 300 `train_step()` rounds on three pairs, the first prediction after `[BOS]` is each
  target's first word on 6/6 runs. With the old targets it was `BOS` (token 2) on 3/3 runs.

RLHF's own response encoding (TD-500) is unchanged; that subsystem is deferred.

- [x] Either tokenize targets without the leading `BOS` (keeping `EOS`) or stop prepending in `forward()`/the GPU fix, consistently for CPU and GPU; this changes training alignment, so do it together with TD-358's retraining.
- [x] If targets are tokenized differently, bump `ChatbotTrainer::kPreprocessFormatVersion` (TD-409) so cached token IDs are rebuilt; `truncate_target_keep_eos()` (TD-275) assumes a target ends with `EOS`.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`strip_leading_bos()`, `make_decoder_input()`, `train_step()`, `evaluate()`, `gpu_evaluate()`), `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`preprocess_data()`); the `TODO: See TD-361` tags are now fix comments.

### TD-362: CPU and GPU Generation Paths Behave Differently

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358, by inspection. The four generation entry points diverge:
- Invalid-vocab masking (IDs ≥ the tokenizer's vocab) happens only in the CPU strategy path and the
  CPU beam paths; the CPU plain cached path and every GPU path don't mask.
- Only CPU paths write hippocampal memory or attach the world model (beam only).
- An unknown strategy goes to `generate()` on CPU but to nucleus sampling on GPU.
- `num_beams > 1` forces beam on CPU (TD-261) but is ignored by the GPU non-beam strategies.

The same request can therefore produce different output depending on whether the server runs on a
GPU build.

Action Items:

- [x] Factor one shared model_fn/strategy-dispatch for CPU and GPU (masking, defaults, beam handling, memory write), differing only in the forward call.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** By then TD-342/343 had already given the GPU paths the world model and the hippocampal writes, and TD-261
had fixed `num_beams` on the CPU. The remaining differences now go through shared members of `EncoderDecoderModel`:
- `normalize_strategy()` (public, static): `temperature`→`sampling`, `top_k`/`top-k`→`topk`, `top_p`/`top-p`→`nucleus`. The CPU
  strategy path used to accept only the hyphenated forms.
- One beam decision on both: "beam", or an unrecognized strategy with `num_beams > 1`.
- `sync_generation_config()`, which stores the beam width only when beam search runs. The GPU path used to store it for every
  strategy, so a later plain call could switch to beam search.
- `mask_unknown_ids()`, now used by every CPU and GPU model callback. The CPU plain cached path and all four GPU callbacks didn't
  mask IDs beyond the tokenizer's vocabulary.
- `run_single_hypothesis()`, which runs `TextGenerator::generate()` on the configured filters for an unrecognized strategy. The GPU
  path used nucleus sampling.

`ChatbotAPI`'s CPU fallback (no GPU) now calls `generate_response_with_strategy()`, as its GPU branch calls the GPU version. It used to
run its own `TextGenerator` loop over `next_token_logits()` (TD-506), re-running the encoder and the whole decoder every step, with no
hippocampal commits and no `max_seq_length` cap. Generation therefore tokenizes with the model's tokenizer on both paths. When no
checkpoint loads, `chatbot_api_server` gives that tokenizer `VOCAB_PATH`.

Tests:
- `NormalizeStrategyAcceptsEverySpelling`.
- `PlainCachedPathMasksIdsTheTokenizerLacks`: with the logits favouring an ID the tokenizer lacks, the plain call must equal greedy. On
  the old code it returned "" against "worlhellod worl amm".
- `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.GpuAndCpuGenerationAgree` (oneAPI CPU device): GPU greedy, plain, beam and "other" with 3 beams equal the CPU
  greedy/beam output, and an explicit greedy call doesn't store its `num_beams`. On the old code every GPU result was "".
- The `ChatbotAPIEchoTest` paths, with the fixture's model given the API's vocabulary.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}` (`normalize_strategy()`, `sync_generation_config()`, `mask_unknown_ids()`,
`run_single_hypothesis()`, all four generation entry points), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`generate_response()`), `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`

### TD-363: `EncoderDecoderModel` Clone, Load and World-Model Input Gaps

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358, by inspection:
- `clone()` round-trips `save_model()`/`load_model()`, so the copy lacks the world model, hippocampal
  memory, generation config, repetition params and LoRA adapters. `ChatbotTrainer`'s async BLEU/ROUGE
  snapshots therefore generate differently from the live model.
- `load_model()` doesn't check its config reads, and restores special-token IDs onto the model but not
  into the generator's config until `sync_special_tokens()` runs.
- `forward()` re-derives the world model's input by decoding token ids back to text, which is lossy
  under the tokenizer's normalization (TD-224).

Action Items:

- [x] Copy the extra state in `clone()` (or document the snapshot's scope); check reads and sync the generator in `load_model()`; pass the original text to the world model where available.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **`clone()`.** The copy is built with the original's `world_model_inject_every_n_layers`, now kept on the model. It used to be built
  without the gated decoder paths, so for any world-model-enabled model `load_model()` threw on the gated-path flag and the per-epoch
  quality snapshot failed. The copy also gets:
  - an independent world model, through the new `LeJEPAEncoder::clone()` (temp save/load, tokenizer, SIGReg settings);
  - a snapshot of the hippocampal memory;
  - the repetition and cross-reference parameters, the hippocampal-updates flag, the generation config and the learning rate.
- **`load_model()`.** Reads were already checked (TD-423), and it now calls `sync_special_tokens()`, so the generator's BOS/EOS/PAD
  follow the loaded tokenizer immediately.
- **World-model input.** The world model encodes the caller's text where one exists: `train_step()`, and the new `input_text`
  argument of `next_token_logits()`, which `ChatbotAPI`'s speculative, batched and `/chat/batch` callbacks pass. The token-only
  `forward()` still decodes.

Not covered: LoRA adapters aren't saved (TD-302), so a clone has none. The copied memory keeps the original's swap file path;
`ChatbotTrainer`'s copy has hippocampal updates off, so it never writes.

Tests:
- `CloneCopiesGatedPathsAttachmentsAndSettings`: on the old code `clone()` throws.
- `LoadModelSyncsTheGeneratorsSpecialTokens`: on the old code the generator kept 57.
- `WorldModelSeesTheOriginalInputText`: with an open gate, "hello jazz" (whose letters the model's vocabulary lacks) changes the
  logits; without the text, the decoded tokens are used.

### TD-364: `LLMEncoder::encode()` Input Doesn't Match the Model's Encoder Input

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Transformer / LLMEncoder | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `LLMEncoder` and verified. `encode(text)` tokenizes with the encoder's own
tokenizer and `add_special_tokens = true`, so `"hello world"` becomes `[BOS, 80, 77, EOS]`.
`EncoderDecoderModel` always tokenizes encoder input with `encode(input_text, false)` (`[80, 77]`), in
training and in generation, so the trained encoder has never seen `BOS`/`EOS` at its input and every
real token sits one position later under `encode()`. The first output row differed (1.398 vs 0.980).
`PipelineInferenceEngine`'s encoder stage calls `encode()` on the trained chat encoder and hands the
result to the decoder, so pipeline-mode answers come from out-of-distribution encoder input. For RAG
(`DocumentStore`) it only needs to be consistent, which it is.

Also verified: when `encode()` truncates to `max_seq_length` it uses `resize()`, dropping the `EOS` it
just added (32 ids cut to 8, last id no longer `EOS`).

Action Items:

- [x] Give `encode()` an `add_special_tokens` parameter (default matching the model: `false`), or have `PipelineInferenceEngine` tokenize with the model's tokenizer and call `encode_with_mask()`.
- [x] When truncating with special tokens, keep the final `EOS`.
- [x] Add a test that pipeline and plain generation produce the same encoder output for the same text.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-365).** `encode(text, add_special_tokens = false)`: the default gives what `EncoderDecoderModel` feeds
the encoder, so `PipelineInferenceEngine`'s encoder stage is in distribution. With special tokens, BOS and EOS are kept at the ends
when the input is truncated (TD-365's tail rule). RAG (`DocumentStore`) re-embeds its documents and queries with `encode()` on every
start and saves nothing, so it stays consistent. Without special tokens it now embeds the last `max_seq_length` tokens of a long
document instead of the first (TD-349 still applies).

Tests (`llmencoder_test.cpp`):
- `EncodeMatchesTheModelsEncoderInput`: `encode(text)` equals `encode_with_mask(tokenize(text, false))`.
- `OverLongInputKeepsTheTail`: covers the special-token case (BOS + last 6 + EOS at `max_seq_length = 8`).

Location in code: `src/LLMEncoder.cpp` (`encode()`), `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (encoder stage); tagged `TODO: See TD-364`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`
- `src/encoder.hpp`
- `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp`
- `tests/llmencoder_test.cpp`
