### TD-365: Encoder Input Is Never Truncated to `max_seq_length` When Serving

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Transformer / LLMEncoder | October 11, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `LLMEncoder` and verified. Only `encode(text)` truncates. `encode_with_mask()` and
`gpu_encode()` take any length, and neither `EncoderDecoderModel`'s generation entry points nor
`ChatbotAPI` truncate the input. A 60-token input on a `max_seq_length = 16` model completed generation
after `PositionalEncoding` warned *"Positions beyond max_len will not receive positional encodings"*, so
44 positions had no order information. Attention cost also grows as O(n²) with no bound, so a long chat
message costs more CPU or GPU time than the configured model size suggests. Related: TD-347 (decoder
side past `max_seq_length`) and TD-294 (the conversation token budget isn't tied to `max_seq_length`).

Action Items:

- [x] Decide on keep-the-tail truncation or rejection, and apply it once where `EncoderDecoderModel` tokenizes encoder input (CPU and GPU, training and generation).
- [x] Add a `max_seq_length` check (assert or throw) in `encode_with_mask()`/`gpu_encode()`.
- [ ] Coordinate with TD-294 so the conversation context fits the encoder. (Left with TD-294: the encoder now keeps a conversation's
  last `max_seq_length` tokens, but the context's own token budget is still unrelated to it.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Policy.** Keep the tail: the rule `ChatbotTrainer` already applies to training inputs (`truncate_tokens_tail()`), so serving now

### TD-366: Serving Encoders Cache Activations for Backward; Dead State and Duplicate API

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Transformer / LLMEncoder | October 11, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `LLMEncoder`, by inspection. `requires_grad` defaults to `true` and nothing clears it
for the serving encoders (the chat encoder in `chatbot_api_server` and the RAG encoder). So every
inference `encode*()` call copies `(num_layers + 1) × seq × d_model` floats into
`cached_encoder_outputs`, which `backward()` never reads (it relies on each block's own caches).
`cached_embeddings` and `cached_pos_encoded` are declared and never used.
`get_sentence_embedding()` and `get_sentence_embedding_trainable()` are identical, and neither has a
production caller (`DocumentStore` pools for itself).

Action Items:

- [x] Remove `cached_encoder_outputs`, `cached_embeddings` and `cached_pos_encoded`, or at least stop filling the first.
- [x] Clear `requires_grad` for serving instances (`EncoderDecoderModel::set_training(false)` already forwards it; make the server and RAG setup call it).
- [x] Merge the two sentence-embedding functions.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- `cached_encoder_outputs`, `cached_embeddings` and `cached_pos_encoded` are removed, along with the per-call copies into the first.
  That was `(num_layers + 1) × seq × d_model` floats per encode, never read.
- The serving model is put in inference mode with `set_training(false)`: `chatbot_api_server`'s model and draft model, and
  `chatbot_gui`'s. The RAG encoder calls `set_requires_grad(false)`.
- `get_sentence_embedding_trainable()` now calls `get_sentence_embedding()`; the name is kept as the pair of
  `backward_sentence_embedding()`.

Test: `LLMEncoderTD366Test.SentenceEmbeddingFunctionsAgreeInEitherMode` (both functions, and `encode()` with `requires_grad` on and
off, give the same result). The removed state had no reader, so the change is otherwise behavior-neutral.

### TD-371: Residual-Branch Output Isn't Scaled for Depth

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — owner decision | Transformer / FeedForward | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `FeedForward` and measured. With unit-variance input (what `LayerNorm` produces),
a freshly initialized FFN's output has a standard deviation of about 1.35 (1.38 at d=64, 1.32 at
d=256, 1.37 at d=512, `d_ff = 4·d_model`). Every Pre-LN block adds this, plus its attention output,
to the residual stream unscaled, so the stream's variance grows with depth from the first step.
GPT-2-style models initialize the residual branch's output projections (`W2` here, the attention
`W_o`) with an extra `1/√(2·num_layers)` factor to keep it bounded. This isn't a bug; it's an
initialization choice that bears on the open hypothesis that Pre-LN residual growth caused the
epoch-5 divergence on ai-machine.

Action Items:

- [ ] Decide whether to scale `W2` (and the attention output projections) by `1/√(2·num_layers)` at initialization, which needs the layer count passed down.
- [ ] If adopted, compare a short training run against the current initialization before switching, since it changes training dynamics (existing checkpoints are unaffected).

Location in code: `src/FeedForward.cpp` (constructor `W2` init); tagged `TODO: See TD-371`.

### TD-372: FTP Data Connections Are Accepted From Any Host, So Files Can Be Stolen

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 21, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | October 12, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer` and verified against a live server. `cmd_retr()` calls
`accept()` on the PASV socket and takes the **first connection from any address**; it never checks
that the peer matches the control connection's client IP. A third socket that connected to the
advertised data port before the real client received the entire file (300,000 of 300,000 bytes), and
the server logged `226 Transfer complete` and marked the token consumed. **The same worked under FTPS
with `PROT P`**: the data-channel `SSL_accept()` accepts any TLS client (no session-reuse or peer
binding), so a TLS-capable thief also received all 300,000 bytes. PASV ports come lowest-first from a
small fixed range (default 50000–50099), so an attacker on the network only has to keep connecting
to them. Consequences: dataset confidentiality is lost, and the real trainer's download fails while
its token is consumed, so every download can be denied as well. The per-file token and TLS design is
bypassed entirely at the data channel.

Action Items:

- [x] Record the control connection's peer address; after `accept()` on the PASV socket, compare the data peer's address and reject (close, keep listening until the timeout) any mismatch.
- [ ] Under `PROT P`, additionally require TLS session resumption (The peer-IP check is done; session reuse is TD-549.) from the control channel (as vsftpd's `require_ssl_reuse` does) or at least the peer-IP check above.
- [x] Don't consume the token unless the transfer went to the authenticated peer.
- [x] Add a live-session test: a foreign connection to the PASV port gets nothing and the real client still succeeds.

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`cmd_retr()`, `ConnState`); tagged `TODO: See TD-372`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/FtpDataServer.hpp`
- `tests/FtpDataServerTests.cpp`

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Peer check:** `cmd_retr()` accepts through `accept_from_client()`, which takes only a connection from the control connection's
  client IP. Any other peer is logged (`[AUDIT] Data connection refused`) and closed while it keeps waiting, within the same 30 s.
- **Backlog:** the PASV listen backlog is now 4 (was 1), so a squatter can't block the real client.
- **Token:** consumed only after a transfer to that peer.
- **Not done:** requiring TLS session reuse on the data channel, the stronger binding, is TD-549.

Tests:
- `FtpDataServerTests.cpp`'s `ForeignDataConnectionGetsNothingAndTheClientStillDownloads`: a socket bound to 127.0.0.2 connects to
  the PASV port before `RETR`. It receives nothing, and the client gets all 300,000 bytes. On the old code the foreign socket took
  the data connection and the client couldn't connect.
- End to end, with the real `registry_server --ftps` and `curl --ssl-reqd --ftp-method nocwd` (the trainer's libcurl options), the
  download still completes (226, contents match).

### TD-373: `--ftps` Doesn't Require Encryption

|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 21, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer` and verified. With `--ftps` enabled, nothing requires
`AUTH TLS` before `USER`/`PASS` or `PROT P` before `RETR`: a plaintext client logged in and downloaded
the full file from the FTPS server. Credentials and data can therefore cross the network unencrypted
on a server operators believe is "FTPS". `DataTransport` requests TLS (`CURLUSESSL_ALL`), so today's
trainer is protected unless the connection is downgraded or a client is misconfigured.

Action Items:

- [x] When FTPS is enabled, refuse `USER`/`PASS` with `530`/`534` until `AUTH TLS` has completed, and refuse `RETR` unless `PROT P` is set.
- [ ] Do this together with TD-339 (client certificate verification) and TD-284 (FTPS keys from config).

- `tests/FtpDataServerTests.cpp`

**Fix (October 21, 2026).** With FTPS enabled:
- **Login:** `USER` and `PASS` get `530 TLS required` until `AUTH TLS` has completed, and are logged (`[AUDIT] Plaintext login refused`).
- **Download:** `RETR` gets `521` (RFC 4217) unless `PROT P` is set.

TD-339 (client certificate checks) and TD-284 (FTPS keys from config) remain open.

### TD-374: FTP Re-Login Leaks Rate-Limit Slots

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open | Data / FtpDataServer | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer` and verified. `PASS` claims a per-`run_id` rate-limit slot,
but `USER` resets the connection's login without releasing it, and the end-of-session cleanup releases
only the latest `run_id`. After one connection logged in twice and quit, a run with
`max_sessions_per_run = 2` and **one** open session was refused a second (`421 Too many concurrent
sessions`). Each such connection leaks a slot until `registry_server` restarts; after
`max_sessions_per_run` leaks, that `run_id` can't download anything. libcurl doesn't re-login on one
connection, so this takes a misbehaving or hostile client.

Action Items:

- [ ] In `cmd_user()` (and before a second successful `PASS`), release the held slot and clear the login.
- [ ] Test: repeated `USER`/`PASS` on one connection, then quit, leaves no slots held.

### TD-375: `FtpDataServer` Has No Connection Limits or Timeouts

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open | Data / FtpDataServer | October 12, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer`; the read behaviour was verified, the rest is by inspection.
`listener_loop()` spawns one **detached** thread per connection with no cap. `read_line()` reads a byte
at a time with **no idle timeout and no length limit**: a 2 MB line with no newline was accepted and
the connection stayed open. So any client that can reach the control port can exhaust
`registry_server`'s threads and memory before logging in. The detached threads aren't tracked, so
`stop()` (and the destructor) can't end them; a connection open at shutdown keeps running against a
destroyed `FtpDataServer` (use-after-free).

Action Items:

- [ ] Cap concurrent connections (reply `421` beyond the cap); set a control-socket receive timeout (for example 60 s pre-auth, a few minutes after login); limit command lines to 512 bytes as RFC 959 implementations commonly do.
- [ ] Track connection threads (or their sockets) so `stop()` can shut them down and join before destruction.

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`listener_loop()`, `read_line()`, `stop()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-375`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/FtpDataServer.hpp`

  `registry_server` can't tell whether FTP came up.

### TD-378: BLEU Smoothing Inflates Unrelated Answers and Zeroes Correct Short Ones

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / GenerationQuality | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `GenerationQualityMetrics` and verified against a textbook (Papineni et al.)
BLEU. `compute_corpus_bleu()` uses `(matches + 1) / (hypothesis n-grams + 1)` for **every** order,
including unigrams, and a fixed `log = -20` when the hypothesis has no n-grams of some order. The
header labels this "add-1 smoothing (Lin & Och 2004, method 1)", but Lin & Och's add-one smoothing
applies only to n ≥ 2. Single-pair results:

| Case | This code BLEU-4 | Textbook BLEU-4 |
|---|---|---|
| Unrelated 5-word answer (no words in common) | 0.230 (BLEU-1 0.167) | 0 |
| Same 5 words, scrambled | 0.359 | 0 |
| Exactly correct 3-word answer | 0.0067 | 0 (no 4-grams) |

So an unrelated answer's BLEU-4 exceeds its BLEU-1, and a correct short reply scores far below an
unrelated long one. The per-epoch metric (10 pairs by default) is less distorted (0.015 for fully
unrelated output) but still biased against short targets, which dominate conversational data such as
daily_dialog. The per-sample backfill (TD-273) gets the full sentence-level distortion. The tests
(`CompletelyDifferentHypothesisScoresNearZero`, `BLEU1AtLeastBLEU2AtLeastBLEU4`) pass only on their
particular examples.

Action Items:

- [x] Use unsmoothed corpus BLEU for the per-epoch metric, or a documented standard smoothing (Chen & Cherry 2014 method 1 — epsilon for zero-match orders — or add-1 for n ≥ 2 only); keep sentence-level BLEU only behind an explicitly smoothed function.
- [x] Handle hypotheses shorter than `n` the standard way, and fix the header's citation.
- [x] Add tests against known reference values (for example, sacreBLEU/NLTK outputs recorded as constants): unrelated → 0, scrambled → low, short exact match.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Per-epoch score.** `evaluate()` reports unsmoothed corpus BLEU (Papineni et al.). Matches and n-gram counts are summed over every
  pair, and an order with no matches makes the score 0. For a single pair, the textbook value of a 3-word answer's BLEU-4 is 0. With
  the default 10 pairs that only happens when the model gets no 4-gram right anywhere.
- **Per-sample score.** The new `sentence_bleu()` is the explicitly smoothed single-pair score, used by the per-sample backfill
  (TD-273). It follows sacreBLEU's sentence settings: Chen & Cherry (2014) method 1 (an order with no matches counts 0.1 matches,
  `smooth_method="floor"`) and effective order (orders the hypothesis is too short for are left out). An exactly correct 3-word answer
  scores 1, and 5 unrelated words score 0.025.
- The header's citation is corrected.

Tests (`generation_quality_test.cpp`). sacreBLEU and NLTK aren't installed here, so the reference values come from an independent
Python implementation of the published formulas, recorded as constants. The partial-match value, 0.537285, matches a hand
calculation.
- Corpus: an unrelated answer → 0, scrambled words → BLEU-4 0 (BLEU-1 1), partial match, brevity penalty, a corpus summed across
  pairs, and a short exact match (BLEU-2 1, BLEU-4 0).
- Sentence: reference values, and a correct short answer outranking an unrelated long one.

The old code fails 5 of the 6 new corpus tests: unrelated BLEU-4 0.188, scrambled 0.359, short exact match 0.0067.
`IdenticalReferenceShouldScoreOne` now expects exactly 1.

Per-epoch BLEU-4 values from before this fix aren't comparable with later ones. The old numbers were inflated for poor outputs and
deflated for short correct ones.

**Superseded (October 25, 2026, TD-380).** The scores now follow sacreBLEU's defaults (13a tokens, `exp` smoothing) on 0–100. Corpus
BLEU is no longer unsmoothed, and `sentence_bleu()` uses `exp` instead of floor smoothing. The fix against the add-1 distortion
stands.

### TD-380: Generation-Quality Scores Aren't Comparable or Well-Sampled

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / GenerationQuality | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `GenerationQualityMetrics`, by inspection:
- `tokenize()` drops punctuation and keeps internal apostrophes, unlike sacreBLEU's `13a` tokenizer
  (punctuation as separate tokens) and `rouge-score` (non-alphanumerics as spaces), so these numbers
  can't be compared with published BLEU/ROUGE.
- Scores are on a 0–1 scale, while the lesson [Reading BLEU and ROUGE Results](../../lessons/reading-bleu-rouge.md)
  gives interpretation ranges on the 0–100 scale for standard corpus BLEU-4.
- `generation_quality_sample_size` defaults to 10 pairs, which makes BLEU-4 very noisy from epoch to
  epoch.

Action Items:

- [x] Document the tokenization and scale in the header, metrics API and dashboards (or report 0–100).
- [x] Add a note to the lesson that the training metric isn't standard corpus BLEU.
- [ ] Raise the default sample size (or report a confidence interval) once TD-359 makes generation length bounded. (TD-359's fix
  landed October 26, 2026; this can now be done.)

**Owner decision (October 25, 2026).** Standard tokenizers and the 0–100 scale.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **BLEU.** `GenerationQualityEvaluator` follows sacreBLEU's defaults: the 13a tokenizer (`tokenize_13a()`: punctuation as tokens,
  `.`/`,` kept between digits, `-` split after a digit, entities unescaped, case kept), and sacreBLEU's `compute_bleu()`. That means
  `exp` smoothing, 0 when no unigram matches, and an order with no hypothesis n-grams giving about 0 at corpus level.
  `sentence_bleu()` is sacreBLEU's `sentence_bleu()` (adds effective order). This replaces TD-378's unsmoothed corpus and
  floor-smoothed sentence scores.
- **ROUGE.** rouge-score's defaults (`tokenize_rouge()`: lowercase, `[a-z0-9]` runs, no stemming); the F1 math was already the same.
- **Scale and consumers.** Every score is on 0–100. The per-sample backfill stores `sentence_bleu() / 100` in `SampleMeta::quality`,
  which stays [0, 1]. The Tizen dashboard colors at 30/10 (was 0.3/0.1) and shows 2 decimals, the Android ops dashboard shows 2
  decimals, and the lesson notes the change.

Tests (`generation_quality_test.cpp`, rewritten): tokenizer outputs and every score are checked against sacreBLEU 2.6.0 and
rouge-score, installed in a scratch directory to produce the values. All 16 tests match within 0.001, including:
- punctuation, case and number handling;
- `exp`-smoothed zero-match orders;
- the corpus/sentence effective-order difference.

Stored generation-quality values before this date are on 0–1 with the old tokenization.

### TD-382: GPU Work From Any Thread Shares Unsynchronized `GPUManager` State

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 | GPU / GPUManager | October 12, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `GPUUtils.hpp`, by inspection. `GPUManager`'s state is process-wide
`inline static` with no locking: `allocated_bytes_` is a plain `size_t`, and there's one cuBLAS handle
and one stream. `Matrix::operator*` sends every product with inner dimensions of at least 32 to
`multiply_gpu()` whenever `GPUManager::is_available()`, **from any thread**. `ChatbotTrainer`'s async
BLEU/ROUGE path is commented as "deliberately still CPU-only" because it calls `generate_response()`
on a `clone()`d model, but that model's `Matrix` products still go to cuBLAS on the shared stream,
concurrently with the training thread's own GPU work. That means unsynchronized updates to the budget
counter (lost updates, wrong refusals) and one cuBLAS handle used from two host threads at once, which
NVIDIA advises against. The same applies to any other thread doing large `Matrix` multiplies while a
model runs on the GPU. CUDA-side analysis only; the SYCL manager will be checked in its own reference.

Action Items:

- [x] Decide on the threading model: either a mutex (or atomic counter plus a per-thread cuBLAS handle) in `GPUManager`, or a thread-local "CPU only" override that the async quality thread sets so its `Matrix` math really stays on the CPU.
- [x] Correct the async-path comment in `ChatbotTrainer::compute_generation_quality_metrics()`.
- [x] Test (on a GPU host): concurrent `Matrix` multiplies from two threads keep the budget counter exact. Covered by `ConcurrentReserveReleaseKeepsCounterExact`, verified on the oneAPI CPU device; a CUDA run is still pending.

**SYCL amendment (October 12, 2026, [GPUUtils_SYCL.md](../reference/source/GPUUtils_SYCL.md)):** the
SYCL manager already guards `max_memory_bytes_`/`allocated_bytes_` with `memory_mutex_`, and
`sycl::queue` is thread-safe for submission, so on SYCL (ai-machine) this item reduces to the
cross-thread GPU use itself (the async quality thread sharing the training queue), not a counter race.

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** both options, since they address different threads.
- `adai::gpu::ScopedCpuOnly` (in `GPUUtils.hpp`, defined in every build) is a per-thread, nestable
  opt-out that `Matrix::operator*` and `multiply_gpu()` check before dispatching. The async quality
  thread holds one for its whole run, so its clone's products stay on the CPU and its comment is now
  true.
- The CUDA manager guards `max_memory_bytes_`/`allocated_bytes_` with `memory_mutex_`, like SYCL.
- Both cuBLAS call sites hold `GPUManager::cublas_mutex()` while enqueuing, which covers any other
  thread (e.g. `chatbot_api_server` request threads) that still multiplies on the GPU.

Verified on the oneAPI CPU device (scratch build, device selection widened):
- the new `GPUManagerTest.ConcurrentReserveReleaseKeepsCounterExact` (8 threads × 20,000
  reserve/release pairs) passes;
- the new `MatrixTest.ScopedCpuOnlyMultiplyMatchesUnscoped` passes, and a temporary probe in
  `multiply_gpu()` showed exactly one GPU dispatch (the unscoped product), none from the scoped thread.

`ScopedCpuOnlyIsPerThreadAndNestable` also runs in the debug build. The CUDA changes compile
(`cuda-gputest`) but haven't been run, since no CUDA device is available.

Location in code: `src/gpu/GPUUtils.hpp` (`GPUManager` state), `src/Matrix.cpp` (`operator*` dispatch), `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (async quality comment); the `TODO: See TD-382` tags are now `TD-382:` fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/gpu/GPUUtils.hpp`
- `src/gpu/sycl/GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp`
- `src/Matrix.cpp`
- `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp`

### TD-383: `GPUManager` Lifecycle Gaps (`set_device`, `cleanup`, `initialize`)

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | GPU / GPUManager | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `GPUUtils.hpp`, by inspection:
- `set_device()` says it "also resets the memory budget", but it only calls `cudaSetDevice()`; the
  stream and cuBLAS handle stay bound to the old device. No caller exists, so it's a latent trap.
- `cleanup()` sets `allocated_bytes_` to 0 while layers' persistent `GPUState` buffers still exist,
  so after a re-`initialize()` the budget undercounts.
- `initialize()` returns true without applying new arguments once initialized, and leaks the stream
  if the cuBLAS step throws.
- `probe_diagnostic()` discards the CUDA error, so a driver failure reads as "0 device(s)".
- `GPUMemory`'s `count × sizeof(T)` isn't overflow-checked.

Action Items:

- [ ] Make `set_device()` rebuild the stream, handle and budget (or remove it); have `cleanup()` refuse or warn while allocations are live; apply or reject differing arguments on repeat `initialize()`; free partial state on failure; include the CUDA error text in `probe_diagnostic()`.

**SYCL amendment (October 12, 2026, [GPUUtils_SYCL.md](../reference/source/GPUUtils_SYCL.md)):** the
SYCL `set_device()` does recreate its queue, but allocations made on the old queue are later freed
with `sycl::free(ptr, new_queue)` (undefined across contexts) and the budget isn't recomputed;
`cleanup()` zeroes the counter and live buffers are then never freed (by design, TD-096); repeat
`initialize()` also ignores new arguments. Tagged in `src/gpu/sycl/GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp` too.

Location in code: `src/gpu/GPUUtils.hpp` (`initialize()`, `cleanup()`, `set_device()`, `probe_diagnostic()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-383`.

### TD-384: Shared-Memory Race in GPU Softmax, LayerNorm and Cross-Entropy Kernels (CUDA and SYCL)

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 | GPU / Kernels | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `MatrixGPU.cu`, by inspection (a definite race under the CUDA and SYCL memory
models). `softmax_rows_kernel`, `layer_norm_fwd_kernel`, `cross_entropy_loss_kernel` and
`cross_entropy_grad_kernel` each run two tree reductions through the same shared `scratch` buffer.
After the first reduction's final barrier, every thread reads `scratch[0]` (the row max or the mean),
computes its next partial, and writes `scratch[lid]`, with **no barrier between the read and
thread 0's write to `scratch[0]`**. Warps (CUDA) or sub-groups (SYCL) of a 256-thread block aren't
scheduled in lockstep, so a lagging warp can read thread 0's partial sum instead of the max or mean.
The result for that row is silently wrong: softmax `exp(x − wrong_max)` can overflow to `inf`/`NaN`,
LayerNorm centres on a variance partial, and the loss and gradient for that position are wrong.

It's likely rare, since thread 0 must finish a full loop pass before the lagging warp's single load,
but it's intermittent, data-dependent and affects attention, every LayerNorm and the loss in GPU
training. **`MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp` has the identical pattern in the same four kernels**, and ai-machine
trains on SYCL (Intel Arc), so its runs are exposed too.

**Verified October 12, 2026** ([MatrixGPU_SYCL_cpp.md](../reference/source/MatrixGPU_SYCL_cpp.md)):
contrary to the original note here, it **does** reproduce on the oneAPI CPU device, deterministically
(the CPU runtime runs a work-group's sub-groups in turn, so sub-group 0 always overwrites
`scratch[0]` first). Wrong results: softmax rows (2.5×10⁻² relative error), LayerNorm forward
(0.32), cross-entropy loss (4×10⁻³) and grad (2×10⁻³), identical over five runs. Adding one
`item.barrier(local_space)` after each of the four reads made all of them pass (≤ 2×10⁻⁷; LayerNorm
backward 6.6×10⁻⁵ vs. finite differences). On a GPU it's timing-dependent rather than certain.

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** all eight sites now wait after reading `scratch[0]`
(`__syncthreads()` in CUDA, `item.barrier(local_space)` in SYCL). These are the only `scratch[0]`
reads followed by another reduction; the rest are each kernel's last use of the buffer. Verified on
the oneAPI CPU device (scratch build with device selection widened to `device_type::all`):
- new tests `MatrixGPUTD003Test.SoftmaxWideRowsMatchHost` (64 × 300) and `LayerNormWideRowsMatchHost`
  (32 × 768, 5 trials each) pass, and so does `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.GpuForwardLossMatchesCpuForwardTeacherForcing`;
- all three fail on every run without the barriers, even with TD-393 fixed.

The CUDA change compiles (`gpu` preset) but hasn't been run, since no CUDA device is available.
Remaining: a racecheck on real hardware, and the on-device run on ai-machine together with TD-358.

Action Items:

- [x] Add a barrier (`__syncthreads()` / `item.barrier(local_space)`) after each `scratch[0]` read that's followed by another reduction, in all four kernels in both backends (or reduce into a second buffer).
- [ ] On a GPU host, run `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck` (CUDA) over a training step to confirm no other shared-memory races remain.
- [x] Do this with TD-358, before the retraining runs.

Location in code: `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu` and `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp` (softmax rows, LayerNorm forward, cross-entropy loss and grad); previously tagged `TODO: See TD-384` at all eight sites; now marked with `TD-384:` fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu`
- `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp`

### TD-387: GPU Generation Fails on Input Longer Than `max_seq_length`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 (with TD-365) | GPU / GPUMatrix | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `MatrixGPU.hpp`, by inspection (definite). `gpu_generate_response()` and
`gpu_generate_response_with_strategy()` build a `GPUDecoderKVCache(decoder_layers, max_seq_length,
d_model)`, whose cross-attention caches hold at most `max_seq_length` rows. On the first decode step,
`CrossAttention::gpu_forward_with_cache()` appends the **entire encoder output** to that cache, but
encoder input is never truncated to `max_seq_length` (TD-365). So any chat input longer than
`max_seq_length` tokens makes `GPUKVCache::append()` throw `out_of_range`, and the request fails on a
GPU server (the TD-033 serving path), while the CPU path answers the same request (with the TD-365
positional-encoding gap). The self-attention cache has the same cap but isn't reachable today:
`TextGenerator` stops at `max_length = max_seq_length` generated tokens, which fills it exactly.

Action Items:

- [x] Truncate encoder input once where the model tokenizes (TD-365), which removes the overflow; or size the cross-attention caches from the actual encoder length.
- [ ] Test (on a GPU host): an over-length prompt generates without throwing and matches the CPU path. (Run on the oneAPI CPU
  device, not a GPU host. The CPU-match part is not checked.)

**Fixed by TD-365 (October 26, 2026).** Both GPU generation paths now keep the encoder input's last `max_seq_length` tokens, so the
encoder output fits the cross-attention cache. Test `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.GpuGenerationAcceptsOverLongInput`: a 480-character input
on a `max_seq_length = 16` model goes through `gpu_generate_response()` and `gpu_generate_response_with_strategy()` without throwing,
on the oneAPI CPU device (`build/sycl-cpudev`, `ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`).

**Verified October 12, 2026** ([MatrixGPU_SYCL.md](../reference/source/MatrixGPU_SYCL.md)): on the
oneAPI CPU device, appending a 12-row encoder output to a `GPUDecoderKVCache(2, max_seq_length = 8,
4)` cross-attention cache throws `"GPUKVCache::append: exceeds max_seq_length capacity"`.

Location in code: `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.hpp` (`GPUDecoderKVCache` constructor), `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (both GPU generation paths); tagged `TODO: See TD-387`.

### TD-388: `GPUKVCache` Copies the Whole Cache Every Decode Step

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | GPU / GPUMatrix | October 12, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `MatrixGPU.hpp`, by inspection. `GPUKVCache::get_keys()`/`get_values()` allocate a
new `GPUMatrix` and copy the whole populated prefix on every call. Cached self-attention and
cross-attention call them once per layer per decode step, so a generation of `n` tokens copies
O(n²·d_model) floats per layer and performs two allocations per layer per step. That works against
TD-050's goal (no per-step device malloc/free churn) and will show up in TD-033/TD-050's still-open
GPU latency benchmark.

Action Items:

- [x] Return a non-owning view (pointer, rows, cols) of the populated prefix and have attention consume it directly (cuBLAS/oneMKL take a leading dimension, so no copy is needed).

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Cache view.** `GPUKVCache::get_keys()`/`get_values()` (and `materialize()`) are replaced by a view: `keys_data()`,
  `values_data()` and `leading_dimension()`.
- **Strided GEMM.** The new `matrix_gemm_strided_gpu()` is a row-major `C = alpha·op(A)·op(B)` with leading dimensions:
  `cublasSgemm` in CUDA and oneMKL `gemm` in SYCL, using `matrix_multiply_gpu()`'s column-major trick.
- **Cached attention.** `MultiHeadAttention::gpu_forward_with_cache()` and `CrossAttention::gpu_forward_with_cache()` compute each
  head as `scale·Q_h·K_hᵀ` straight from the cache, and write `scores·V_h` into that head's columns of the output.
- **Removed per step.** Each layer used to copy the whole cache prefix twice (two allocations), copy every head's Q/K/V columns out
  one row at a time (about `total_len × heads` device copies), transpose, scale into a new matrix and scatter the head output back.
  All of that is gone.

Measured on the oneAPI CPU device, with d_model 128, 8 heads and 2+2 layers: a 100-token GPU greedy decode took 6.6 s before and
1.4 s after (4.6× faster). On a real GPU the removed per-row copies were separate device calls, so the gain should be larger;
measuring it is part of TD-033/TD-050's benchmark. The CUDA backend is compile-checked only.

Tests:
- `MatrixGPUTD388Test.StridedGemmMatchesHostReference`: all four transpose combinations, offset views and wider leading
  dimensions, and the columns outside the view are untouched.
- `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.CachedGpuDecodeMatchesCpuOverALongGeneration`: 4 heads, 2+2 layers, 20 greedy tokens, equal to the CPU
  output.
- The existing GPU generation tests.

Location in code: `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.hpp` (`GPUKVCache`, `matrix_gemm_strided_gpu()`), `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu`,
`src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp`, `src/CrossAttention.cpp`
(`gpu_forward_with_cache()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.hpp`
- `src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp`
- `src/CrossAttention.cpp`

### TD-389: `GPUMatrix` Shape Checks, Uninitialized Memory and Untested GPU KV Caches

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | GPU / GPUMatrix | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `MatrixGPU.hpp`, by inspection:
- `GPUMatrix::add_inplace`, `softmax_backward`, `gelu_backward`, `add_row_bias`,
  `masked_fill_inplace`, `layer_norm` and `layer_norm_backward` don't check shapes (the arithmetic
  operators do), so a caller's shape bug becomes silent device memory corruption or a fault.
- `GPUMatrix(r, c)` leaves device memory uninitialized (unlike CPU `Matrix`), and a short `upload()`
  leaves the rest as garbage; `r × c` is unchecked.
- `count_below_threshold()` on an empty matrix returns `NaN`.
- `GPUKVCache` validates its sizes only after allocating, and `GPUDecoderKVCache` doesn't
  bounds-check layer indices.
- **`GPUKVCache`/`GPUDecoderKVCache` have no tests at all**, not even GPU-gated ones.

Action Items:

- [ ] Add shape checks to the unchecked operations; zero (or document) new allocations; validate before allocating; check layer indices.
- [ ] Add GPU-gated tests for the KV caches (append, capacity, materialize, clear) mirroring `KVCache`'s CPU tests.

**Verified on SYCL, October 12, 2026** ([MatrixGPU_SYCL.md](../reference/source/MatrixGPU_SYCL.md)):
on the oneAPI CPU device, `big(4×4).add_inplace(small(2×2))` was accepted with no error (reading past
`small`'s buffer), and a fresh `GPUMatrix` held garbage (`6.6×10⁻³⁷`). The `GPUKVCache` itself ran
correctly (offsets, materialize, clear), its first run anywhere; the tests above should still be added

### TD-390: SYCL Deferred Frees and Blocking Copies Stall the In-Order Queue

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 20, 2026 | GPU / GPUManager | October 12, 2026 | 4-8 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp`; the pattern was verified on a CPU queue, and the GPU
magnitude is unmeasured. `GPUMemory`'s destructor and move assignment call `defer_free()`, which
submits a `host_task` on the in-order queue to run `sycl::free` and release the budget. That's correct
for ordering, but on an in-order queue a `host_task` waits for every earlier command to finish, and
nothing after it starts until the host callback returns: a device→host→device round trip with the
device idle, **for every `GPUMatrix` temporary destroyed**. `copy_from_host`/`copy_to_host` also
`.wait()` on the whole queue, so every upload drains it.

A standalone `icpx -fsycl` program reproducing the pattern on the oneAPI CPU device (allocate, small
kernel, `host_task` free) took **1.35 ms per iteration**, against **0.051 ms** for a blocking `wait()` +
`free` and **0.014 ms** for the kernel alone with a reused buffer. `MultiHeadAttention.cpp` and
`CrossAttention.cpp` alone have about 50 `GPUMatrix` uses each, so ai-machine's SYCL training and
generation likely spend a large share of their time in these bubbles. The `allocated_bytes_` lag that
`ChatbotTrainer` works around with periodic `gpu_synchronize()` calls is the same mechanism.

Action Items:

- [ ] Measure first on ai-machine: time one training step, and count `host_task`s per step (or use `onetrace`/`unitrace`).
- [x] Replace per-free `host_task`s with a caching allocator: keep freed blocks in a size-bucketed pool tied to the in-order queue (safe to reuse immediately, since later kernels on the same queue run after earlier ones), and return memory to USM only at `cleanup()` or under budget pressure.
- [ ] Make uploads asynchronous where the host buffer outlives the copy (or stage through a pinned buffer), keeping `.wait()` only on downloads.

Location in code: `src/gpu/sycl/GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp` (`GPUMemory::defer_free()`, `copy_from_host()`/`copy_to_host()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-390`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/gpu/sycl/GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp`
- `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (remove the accounting workaround syncs afterwards)

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Caching allocator:** `GPUMemory` takes its blocks from `GPUManager::allocate_block()` and returns them with
  `release_block()`, which puts the block in a size-bucketed pool: no `host_task` and no wait. Sizes are 512-byte
  steps up to 1 MiB, then an eighth of the next power of two, at most 12.5% over (`pool_size()`). Reuse is safe at
  once on the in-order queue: commands still using a released block were submitted earlier, so they run before
  anything its next owner submits.
- **Budget:** live and cached bytes both count against `GPU_MEMORY_FRACTION`. An allocation that doesn't fit
  waits for the queue and returns the pool to USM (`trim_pool_locked()`) before refusing. `cleanup()` and
  `set_device()` trim too, and a block from before them is never pooled (generation counter).
- **No accounting lag:** the budget counter now drops when a `GPUMemory` is destroyed, rather than when a
  `host_task` runs. `get_used_memory_bytes()` reports live blocks at their pool size, and
  `get_cached_memory_bytes()` reports the pool.
- **Trainer:** `ChatbotTrainer`'s six workaround `gpu_synchronize()` calls are gone (after each training and
  validation sample, both catch blocks, and the two generation-quality loops). Each sample's own uploads and loss
  download still order the work. One side effect: the per-sample compute-time metric now counts the backward's
  submission, not its device time, which moves into the next sample's upload wait. Per-epoch throughput is
  unchanged.
- **Uploads:** deliberately still `.wait()`. Callers pass host temporaries that may not outlive an asynchronous
  copy, and every training sample downloads its loss anyway, so asynchronous uploads would need staging buffers
  for little gain.

Measured on the oneAPI CPU device (`ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`):
- **Per temporary:** allocate + small kernel + free went from 1.25 ms to 0.0145 ms (86×). This used the real
  `GPUMemory`, built once with the old header and once with the new.
- **Real pass:** the same SYCL `incremental_trainer` pass (d_model 128, 2+2 layers, 120 samples, 1 epoch) went
  from 69.4 s to 38.4 s.

New tests (`gpuutils_test.cpp`, SYCL only):
- a released block is reused and counted at once, without `synchronize()` (the old header still counted it);
- reuse keeps queue order (a copy queued before the release still reads the old data);
- budget pressure returns the pool to the device;
- a block from before `cleanup()` isn't pooled;
- `pool_size()` rounding.

Still open: measuring on ai-machine.

**CUDA follow-up (October 20, 2026).** CUDA's `GPUMemory` called `cudaMalloc()`/`cudaFree()`, and `cudaFree()` synchronizes
the device: the same stall, once per temporary. It now goes through `GPUManager::allocate_block()`/`release_block()`,
which use `cudaMallocAsync()`/`cudaFreeAsync()` on the ADAI stream, the stream-ordered allocator `MatrixGPU.cu`'s batched
paths already used. Every ADAI kernel, copy, memset and cuBLAS call runs on that one stream (checked), so a freed block's
earlier uses complete before it is reused.
- **Pool:** the device's default memory pool keeps freed memory up to the ADAI budget (its release threshold) instead of
  returning it to the driver at each synchronization.
- **Allocation failure:** a failed allocation retries once after `cudaMemPoolTrimTo()`.
- **Teardown:** `cleanup()` trims the pool. A block destroyed after `cleanup()` falls back to `cudaFree()`, which also frees
  pool memory.
- **Fallback:** devices without memory-pool support (`cudaDevAttrMemoryPoolsSupported`) keep `cudaMalloc()`/`cudaFree()`.
- **Budget:** the counter is unchanged; it already dropped at release.

Compile-checked only (no CUDA device here). New CUDA-only tests, which skip without a device:
- `CudaUsesTheStreamOrderedPoolWhenSupported`;
- `CudaFreeKeepsStreamOrder`: a copy queued before its source is freed still reads the old data.

### TD-391: SYCL Lists the Same GPU Once per Platform and Doesn't Log the Backend

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|

Description:
Found while tracing `GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp`, by inspection. `enumerate_gpu_devices()` collects
`device_type::gpu` devices from **every** SYCL platform. With both the Level Zero and OpenCL runtimes
installed (the usual oneAPI setup, and what ai-machine's driver packages provide), one Intel Arc card
appears once per platform, so `device_count()` is 2 and `GPU_DEVICE_ID=0` means "whichever platform
enumerates first". The startup log prints the device name via `get_device_info()`, but not the
platform or backend, so nobody can tell whether training runs on Level Zero (the expected, faster path
for oneMKL) or OpenCL. Given ai-machine's driver-instability history (SIGSEGV in `libigc`, see
[ONEAPI_SYCL_DRIVER_SEGFAULT.md](../../operations/guides/troubleshooting/ONEAPI_SYCL_DRIVER_SEGFAULT.md)), knowing the backend matters for diagnosis too.

- [ ] Log the platform and backend in `get_device_info()`/the startup line.
- [ ] Ask the user to check ai-machine's current selection (`sycl-ls`, or the new log line).

### TD-393: SYCL Sub-Group Reduction Is Wrong When the Sub-Group Size Is 8

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 | GPU / Kernels | October 12, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp` and verified on the oneAPI CPU device.
`workgroup_reduce_sum()` (used by `matrix_sum_gpu` and `matrix_count_below_threshold_gpu`) reduces
within each sub-group, stores one partial per sub-group, and then has **only sub-group 0** combine the
`256 / S` partials. That's correct only if `S ≥ 16`. No `reqd_sub_group_size` is set, so the compiler
chooses `S`; the CPU device chose 8, so 8 of 32 partials were summed per level: 256 ones → 64,
1,000 → 256, 1,000,000 → 65,536; the saturation count came out 427 instead of 1,667. The
cross-entropy loss also goes through `matrix_sum_gpu`, so it's wrong once `seq_len > 64`.

ai-machine's Arc B60 (Xe2/Battlemage) supports only sub-group sizes 16 and 32, so it's probably
latent there, but nothing in the code guarantees it. Arc A-series (Alchemist) and CPU devices can use
8, and the CUDA version (warp 32) is unaffected.

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** sub-group 0 now loops over all partials
(`for (i = lane; i < num_subgroups; i += S)`) before its final sub-group reduction, so the sum is
exact for any `S`. Verified on the oneAPI CPU device (`S = 8`):
- the new `MatrixGPUTD003Test.SumIsExactAcrossWorkGroupBoundaries` (1 to 100,000 ones, including
  255/256/257) and `CountBelowThresholdIsExactForFullWorkGroup` pass;
- the existing `CountBelowThresholdLargeMatrixMultiBlock` now passes too (it failed before).

These tests skip without a device, so CI coverage still depends on TD-394.

Action Items:

- [x] Have sub-group 0 loop over all partials (`for (i = lane; i < num_subgroups; i += S)`), or pin `[[sycl::reqd_sub_group_size(16)]]` (or 32) on the reduction kernels.
- [ ] Cover it with TD-394's CPU-device test mode (sizes 255, 256, 257, 1e6). The tests exist in `tests/matrixgpu_td003_test.cpp`; only the device-less CI mode is missing.

Location in code: `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp` (`workgroup_reduce_sum()`); previously tagged `TODO: See TD-393`, now a `TD-393:` fix comment.

Files to Modify:

- `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp`

### TD-395: `GPUMatrix` Is Duplicated Between the CUDA and SYCL Headers

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |

| LOW | Open | GPU / GPUMatrix | October 12, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `MatrixGPU_SYCL.hpp`, by inspection. `GPUMatrix` is defined twice: in the CUDA
block of `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.hpp` and again in `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.hpp`. The two are the same
member for member except `copy()` (CUDA: async device copy; SYCL: `q.memcpy(...).wait()`) and `zero()`
(`cudaMemsetAsync` vs. `q.memset`). Every `GPUMatrix` change has to be made twice, and a missed one
makes the backends diverge silently. `GPUKVCache` already shows the alternative: one definition after
the backend split, using only the shared API. The SYCL `copy()`'s `.wait()` is also an unnecessary
full-queue drain on an in-order queue, against CLAUDE.md's "no `.wait()` on intermediate work" rule
(compare TD-390). The SYCL header's status note ("capped by TD-050") is stale, since TD-050 is mostly
resolved.

- [ ] Drop the `.wait()` from `copy()`; refresh the SYCL header's status note.

Location in code: `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.hpp` and `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.hpp` (`GPUMatrix`); tagged `TODO: See TD-395`.

### TD-396: Hippocampal Memory Eviction Starves New Memories

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 21, 2026 | Memory / HippocampalMemory | October 13, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `HippocampalMemory` and verified by simulation with the real class. TD-193's
least-used eviction removes the slot with the lowest `coverage_`, but a newly written slot starts at
coverage 0, while every older slot carries accumulated, decayed coverage. Under `DecoderBlock`'s
bookkeeping (each forward step: `decay_coverage(0.95)`, then add each slot's mean attention weight),
a new slot needs about `1/(1 − γ)` = 20 steps to approach the others. With near-uniform attention it
never catches up before the next write, so it is the slot evicted next. Simulation (capacity 8, one
write per "response" followed by 50 forward steps, 40 responses): with uniform attention the
survivors were writes **0–6** plus the newest, so the first `capacity − 1` memories are permanent and
nothing new persists. With peaked random attention turnover was normal (20, 22, 26, 33, 35, 37, 38,
39). Near-uniform attention is the likely case in shipped models: the hippocampal cross-attention gets
no gradient while its gate is stuck at 0 (TD-341), and keys are mean-pooled world-model embeddings of
whole responses. The failure is masked today only because TD-341 zeroes the path's output.

Action Items:

- [x] Give new slots a protection window (not evictable for N steps/writes), or start them at the current mean coverage, or evict by `coverage / age` (or LRU on last significant attention).
- [x] Add a test that simulates the decay-and-accumulate bookkeeping under uniform attention and asserts recent writes survive.
- [x] Do this together with TD-341.

Location in code: `src/HippocampalMemory.cpp` (`evict_least_used()`, `insert_slot()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-396`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/HippocampalMemory.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/hippocampalmemory_test.cpp`

**Note (October 20, 2026, TD-341).** The hippocampal gate now trains on the CPU path, so this eviction behavior is now
reachable in training, not only in theory.

**Fix (October 21, 2026).** Of the options above, a new slot (from `write()` or `recall_from_swap()`) now starts at the
**mean coverage of the slots it joins**, 0 when it's the first. Eviction ties go to the oldest.
- **Uniform attention:** every slot stays level, so eviction becomes FIFO.
- **Peaked attention:** usage decides as before.
- **Why not a protection window:** it doesn't fix exactly uniform attention. A slot leaving the window is still the youngest,
  so it's still the least covered.
- **Repetition penalty:** at the mean coverage, it adds the same bias to every slot under uniform attention, which doesn't
  change the softmax.
- **Format:** the saved file format is unchanged.

Tests (`hippocampalmemory_test.cpp`):
- `RecentWritesSurviveUnderUniformAttention`: the TD's own simulation (capacity 8, 40 writes, 50 committed steps each). The
  survivors are writes 32–39; the old code left {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 39}, as described above.
- `BufferTurnsOverUnderPeakedAttention`.
- `NewSlotsStartAtTheMeanCoverageOfTheOthers` replaces the test that asserted the old zero start.
- Two coverage expectations in the eviction and recall tests were updated to the mean.

TD-341 (the gates) and TD-343 (one update per decode step) landed first, so the simulation uses the real per-step bookkeeping.

interface's methods (`update_advanced_epoch_metrics`, both adaptive-clip methods,
`update_activation_saturation`, `update_attention_entropy`, `update_padding_efficiency` and both
LeJEPA methods) only store a value; it's sent inside the next `end_epoch()` payload, and
`start_epoch()` resets those buffers. So they must be called between `start_epoch()` and `end_epoch()`
of the same epoch. Both callers do this today, but the rule appears only in a call-site comment in
`IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`; the interface's doc comments don't say which methods are buffered or
that ordering matters, so a new implementation or a reordered caller would lose or misattribute
values silently. Separately, `AbnormalSample` carries full, untruncated `input_text`/`target_text` into
the push queue and the metrics DB (capped only by `max_abnormal_samples` per epoch).

Action Items:

- [ ] Document per method whether it's pushed immediately or included in the next `end_epoch()`, and the ordering rule, in the interface.
- [ ] Optionally truncate `AbnormalSample` texts (for example to 1 KB) before queuing.

and `resolve_dataset_kind()` returns it unchanged. With `RemoteTransport` it becomes a URL segment,

`LocalTransport`, `DatasetRegistry` joins it as `session_dir + "/" + kind`, so a typo silently selects
a new, empty sub-pool ("no pending data") and a value containing `..` or `/` puts the local registry
files outside `session_dir`.

Action Items:

- [ ] Validate the value against the four kinds (shared with `dataset_manager --kind` and `DATASET_KIND`) and reject anything else.

### TD-405: Each Training Pass Restarts From the Best-Ever Checkpoint, Not the Latest

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | October 13, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer` and verified with the real class. All three constructors,
and `resume_last_session()`, load the session with the **lowest `final_validation_loss` across the
whole history**. But each pass's validation loss comes from a validation split of that pass's own
files, so losses from different passes aren't comparable. When a later pass trains on new data whose
validation loss is higher, the next pass starts from the older checkpoint again and the later
learning is discarded, while the registry has already marked those files trained. Verified: with
session 0 (val 1.20) and a newer session 1 (val 2.00), construction logged `Best checkpoint:
…/session_0_checkpoint.bin` and loaded it. In incremental training over a stream of datasets, the
model can stay pinned to one old checkpoint indefinitely; this could explain apparent lack of
progress across ai-machine passes.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `select_resume_checkpoint()` returns the most recent completed session whose checkpoint passes
`is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()`. The new `RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT` key (`config.trainer.conf`, env, `IncrementalConfig`; default false)
selects the lowest-validation-loss session instead.

The constructors (through `init_from_session_history()`) and `resume_last_session()` both use it, and log the chosen checkpoint and the reason.
`best_checkpoint_path` is still tracked for the best symlink. Two more bugs turned up while testing, both fixed in the same change:
- [TD-539](#td-539-incrementaltrainer-constructors-never-load-a-checkpoint): the constructors never actually loaded any checkpoint.
- [TD-538](#td-538-encoder-token-embedding-and-final-norm-are-overwritten-in-every-checkpoint): checkpoints lost the encoder's embedding and final norm.

New test `ResumesFromMostRecentSessionNotLowestValidationLoss` uses real `save_model()` checkpoints. Session 1 is newer with validation loss 2.0,
session 0 older with 1.2; a new trainer matches session 1's weights by default and session 0's with the option set. On the old code it matched
neither.

- [x] Resume from the most recent completed session by default; keep "best" selection as an explicit option (or compare losses only on a fixed, shared validation set).
- [x] Apply the same rule in `resume_last_session()`, and log which checkpoint was chosen and why.
- [x] Test: two sessions where the newer has higher validation loss → the newer is resumed.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`select_resume_checkpoint()`, `init_from_session_history()`, `resume_last_session()`), `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}` (`RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT`); the `TODO: See TD-405` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/incrementaltrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-406: A Paused or Crashed Pass's Checkpoint Is Deleted on the Next Start

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | October 13, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer` and verified with the real class. `perform_auto_save()` (sample
cadence, forced `/admin/checkpoint`, and the `/admin/pause` drain path) writes `auto_save_session_N.bin`
and persists session N to `session_history.txt` with `final_validation_loss = 0`. On the next
construction:
1. `current_session_id` becomes N+1, so the in-progress check looks for `session_<N+1>_best.bin`
   and misses session N's best snapshot.
2. `cleanup_dead_sessions()` deletes session N's auto-save as an "orphaned snapshot from a
   crashed/superseded session".
3. It drops session N from the history ("Removing broken session") because its val loss is 0.

Verified: history with session 0 complete and session 1 paused (auto-save plus `session_1_best` on
disk) → the restart loaded session 0, removed session 1 and its auto-save, and left `session_1_best`
on disk unused forever. So TD-173's "pause drains the pass and checkpoints it" produces a checkpoint
the next pass deletes; the released files are retrained from older weights, and crash recovery from
auto-saves never happens.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `take_interrupted_session()` runs at construction, from `init_from_session_history()`. It recognizes an
interrupted session by its history entry still pointing at `auto_save_session_N.bin` rather than a finalized `session_N_checkpoint.bin`. Then it:
1. picks the newer (by `.config` mtime) of that auto-save and `session_N_best.bin` among those with all five files;
2. sets `current_session_id` back to N, so `cleanup_dead_sessions()` keeps both snapshots;
3. removes the interim entry, which the resumed pass recreates.

The trainer loads that snapshot, and `resume_last_session()` (every `trainer_service` pass) uses it ahead of the TD-405 rule. Pause therefore
produces a checkpoint the next pass actually continues from, and crash recovery from auto-saves works. A session with no loadable snapshot is left
to the old cleanup.

New test `IncrementalTrainerTest.InterruptedSessionResumesFromItsNewestSnapshot` uses real `save_model()` snapshots and covers both newest-snapshot
orders. Against the old code it loaded the wrong weights, moved to session 2 and deleted the auto-save.

- [x] On startup, detect an interrupted session (val loss 0 with an existing auto-save or best snapshot) and resume from its newest snapshot instead of deleting it; keep `current_session_id` aligned or look up the snapshot by the interrupted session's id.
- [x] Only treat snapshots as orphaned when no history entry references their session. (Achieved by keeping `current_session_id` at the interrupted session's id.)
- [x] Test: pause → restart resumes from the paused pass's snapshot. (Restart from a paused pass's persisted state; the pause drain itself is covered by the existing control tests.)

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`take_interrupted_session()`, `init_from_session_history()`, `resume_last_session()`, `perform_auto_save()`); the `TODO: See TD-406` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/incremental_trainer_control_test.cpp`

### TD-407: Checkpoint Deletion Leaks the Per-Layer Weight Files

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | October 13, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer` and measured. `EncoderDecoderModel::save_model()` writes
the top-level sidecars (`.config`, `.vocab`, `.encoder`, `.decoder`, `.lm_head`) plus per-layer files
(`_token_emb.bin`, `_encoder_block_<i>.bin` + `_attention.bin`/`_feedforward.bin`,
`_decoder_block_<i>.bin` + `.self_attn`/`.cross_attn`/`.ff`, `_final_norm.bin`), and the per-layer files
hold almost all the weights. `remove_model_files()` deletes only the five top-level sidecars plus
`.metrics.csv`: on a d_model 256, 4 + 4 layer checkpoint it removed **0.1 of 29.6 MB (0.2%)**. Every
retention rotation (`MAX_SESSIONS_TO_KEEP`), superseded best snapshot, broken-session cleanup and
`reset` therefore leaves almost a whole checkpoint behind. `cleanup_dead_sessions()` and
`reset_all()` scan for `*.bin` base files that `save_model()` never writes, so they only match
per-layer files by accident (partially deleting snapshots) and never the attention/FF files. Disk use
in `SESSION_DIR` grows by roughly one checkpoint per pass (plus snapshots and auto-saves) with no
bound.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** every file `save_model(base)` writes is named `base` + `.`… or `base` + `_`…, including TD-538's new encoder
files and `.metrics.csv`. The new `IncrementalTrainer::checkpoint_files(base)` lists a directory by that prefix, so it stays complete whatever
components a checkpoint has. It is used in three places:
- `remove_model_files()` deletes exactly those files.
- `cleanup_dead_sessions()` and `reset_all()` group a session directory's files by checkpoint base (`session_checkpoint_base_of()`) instead of
  scanning for bare `*.bin` files.
- `cleanup_dead_sessions()` also deletes checkpoint remnants whose `.config` is gone, which is what the old partial deletion left behind. So the
  first start after the fix reclaims existing leaked space without a separate command.

New tests, all three failing on the old code:
- `RemoveModelFilesDeletesTheWholeCheckpointOnly` (real checkpoint; `session_10` survives removing `session_1`);
- `CleanupDeadSessionsReclaimsCheckpointRemnants`;
- `CheckpointLinksLoadAndRepointCleanly` (TD-408).

`CleanupDeadSessionsRemovesOrphansAndBrokenHistory`'s stand-in auto-saves now have a `.config`, as real ones do.

- [x] Have `EncoderDecoderModel` expose (or return from `save_model()`) the list of files a checkpoint consists of, and delete exactly those in `remove_model_files()`, `cleanup_dead_sessions()` and `reset_all()`; or save each checkpoint into its own directory and remove the directory. (Done by file-name prefix, which every file `save_model()` writes follows.)
- [x] Add a test that save → remove leaves no files behind; offer a one-off cleanup command for existing session directories (ask the user to check ai-machine's `SESSION_DIR` size). (The cleanup happens automatically on the next start.)

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`checkpoint_files()`, `session_checkpoint_base_of()`, `remove_model_files()`, `cleanup_dead_sessions()`, `reset_all()`); the `TODO: See TD-407` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-408: `latest`/`best` Checkpoint Symlinks Always Dangle

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | October 13, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer`, by inspection. `create_or_update_symlink()` links
`latest_checkpoint.bin`/`best_checkpoint.bin` (in the working directory) to the **bare** checkpoint path,
which `save_model()` never creates, so the links always dangle. Loading through a link looks for
`best_checkpoint.bin.config`, which isn't a link, so neither can be used as `MODEL_PATH`. On Windows
the fallback `copy_file()` copies the same nonexistent bare file and always fails.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `create_or_update_symlink()` creates one link per checkpoint file, under the link's own base name, with an
absolute target. For example, `latest_checkpoint.bin.config` points at `…/session_3_checkpoint.bin.config`. The link name therefore loads exactly
like the checkpoint (usable as `MODEL_PATH`). On Windows the files are copied.

`remove_symlink_if_exists()` now removes every `<link>…` symlink before re-linking. On POSIX it never removes a regular file that only shares the
prefix. The same bare-path mistake is fixed in two more places:
- `cleanup_old_sessions()` re-pointed the latest link only if the bare checkpoint path existed, so it never did; it now checks the checkpoint's
  files.
- `reset_all()`'s model backup renamed the bare `MODEL_PATH`, which never exists; it now moves every file to the base `<MODEL_PATH>.bak`, which
  loads as a checkpoint.

Test: `CheckpointLinksLoadAndRepointCleanly` (loads through the link and matches the weights; re-pointing leaves no stale link).

- [x] Link a checkpoint directory (see TD-407) or create links for every sidecar; or replace the links with a small text file naming the checkpoint base path that tools read.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`create_or_update_symlink()`, `remove_symlink_if_exists()`, `cleanup_old_sessions()`, `reset_all()`); the `TODO: See TD-408` tag is now a fix comment.

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer`, by inspection. `compute_tokenized_cache_key()` hashes the
files' content checksums and segment ranges, the vocab checksum, the tokenizer mode and
`max_seq_length`, but no version of `ChatbotTrainer`'s preprocessing. A code fix that changes the cached

data for every file already cached, so the fix wouldn't take effect until the cache directory was
cleared by hand.

to bump it whenever preprocessing output changes for the same input. Version 2 covers TD-531/TD-532's JSONL decoding and TD-275's target truncation,
so every cache built before them misses and is rebuilt. Old cache files are no longer read, but they aren't deleted either; clear
`tokenized_cache_dir` to reclaim the space.

### TD-411: `resume` (Every `trainer_service` Pass) Never Downloads Over FTP

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | October 13, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool`, by inspection (definite). `trainer_service` runs
`incremental_trainer --foreground --admin-port N resume` for every pass, and `resume` calls
`IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()`. That function acquires pending files and then trains on
`resp.registry_paths()` directly, under the comment "resume_last_session runs on the same machine as
the registry … ftp_server_host is always empty here". That's only true for a local registry. With
`REGISTRY_SERVER_URL` pointing at a remote `registry_server` that delivers files over FTP (TD-040's
transport), these are the registry host's paths; the `DataTransport::fetch_all()` download that `train`
performs never happens, so the trainer can't open the files. With TD-412 the pass then "succeeds" and
marks them trained.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** the FTP-or-direct download step is now `resolve_pass_files()` in `IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`, shared by
`train`, `retrain` (its pending files) and `resume`. It keeps TD-205 segment ranges. `IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()` takes an optional
`PassFileResolver`, which the `resume` command passes, and the downloads are cleaned up after the pass. Without a resolver, a registry that hands
out an FTP host fails the pass and releases its files instead of training on paths it can't read. The pass also now releases its batch when the
resume checkpoint is missing or fails to load; before, those returns left the files claimed.

New test `ResumeTrainsOnResolvedFilesAndReleasesOnResolverFailure`: a failed resolver releases the file, and a successful one trains on the resolved
local path and marks the registry entry trained. The old code failed it.

Still open: `retrain` reads its already-trained files by registry path (only pending ones are fetched), so a full retrain against a remote FTP
registry can't read them. That needs a download path for trained files.

- [x] Factor `train`'s acquire → (FTP download) → train → mark/release → cleanup sequence into one function and use it from `resume_last_session()` (with the segment ranges). (The download step is shared; acquire/mark/release stay in each caller.)
- [x] Ask the user whether ai-machine's `trainer_service` uses a remote FTP registry; if so, audit and re-queue files marked trained since it went live. Answered October 18, 2026: the trainer always takes its data from the remote services. The affected files can't be told apart (TD-334), so re-queue everything before the retraining with `dataset_manager requeue --all --model <name>` (TD-540).
- [ ] Download already-trained files for `retrain` against a remote registry.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`resume_last_session()`), `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`resolve_pass_files()`; `train`, `retrain`, `resume` commands); the `TODO: See TD-411` tags are now fix comments except `retrain`'s trained-files one.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`

### TD-412: A Training Pass That Loads Zero Samples Marks Its Files Trained

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | October 13, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool` and verified with `IncrementalTrainer` in a scratch
program. `ChatbotTrainer::train()` has no empty-data check, and neither do `train_on_files()` or
`retrain_on_files()`. Given a nonexistent file, the pass logged `Cannot open file`, `Total samples
loaded: 0`, `Training for 2 epochs...` and `Incremental training session completed successfully`, and
`train_on_files()` **returned `true`**. Every caller then calls `mark_trained()`, so a missing,
unreadable or empty file (or every file in a TD-411 remote-FTP `resume` pass) is recorded as trained
without any training, and a zero-sample session is added to the history.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** both `train_on_files()` and `retrain_on_files()` now load through `load_training_pairs()`, which warns about each
file that yields no pairs. If nothing loaded, they return false through `fail_empty_pass()`, which logs the failure and, under the admin API, sets
the phase back to idle; the callers then release the files. `ChatbotTrainer::train()` also returns false when nothing survives tokenization.

Two related changes:
- `initialize_session()` now runs after loading and the first-run vocab bootstrap. A failed pass leaves no zero-sample session, and
  `bootstrap_vocab()`'s `load_session_history()` no longer discards the pass's own entry.
- `retrain_on_files()` no longer divides by zero when `VALIDATION_SPLIT=0`.

New test `PassThatLoadsNothingFails` covers a missing file, an empty file and a retrain over both; it fails on the old code, which returned true
three times and recorded a zero-sample session.

- [x] Treat zero loaded (or zero tokenized) samples as failure in `train_on_files()`/`retrain_on_files()` (and guard in `ChatbotTrainer::train()`), so callers release the files; log which files failed to load.
- [x] Test: a nonexistent file → `false` → released, not marked trained.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`load_training_pairs()`, `fail_empty_pass()`, `train_on_files()`, `retrain_on_files()`), `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`train()`); the `TODO: See TD-412` tags are now fix comments.

### TD-413: Standalone `train`/`retrain` Pre-Check Reads the Wrong Pending Pool

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | October 13, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool` and verified with the built binaries. Without
`REGISTRY_SERVER_URL`, `train`'s pre-fork check (and `retrain`'s count) reads
`SESSION_DIR/pending_files.txt`. But `incremental_trainer` always sets `DATASET_KIND` (TD-204), so
`LocalTransport` keeps the pool in `SESSION_DIR/<kind>/pending_files.txt` (TD-202). After `dataset_manager
--kind chatbot add d.jsonl`, `incremental_trainer train 1` printed "No pending data. Use DatasetManager to
queue training data." Queuing without `--kind` passes the check, but the child's acquire looks in the
kind pool and finds nothing. Standalone training can't start from a correctly queued pool.

- [x] Do the pre-check through `DatasetRegistry` (which applies the kind) in both modes, counting only files this model/kind can acquire.

the same kind sub-pool the pass acquires from (`SESSION_DIR/<kind>/` locally). The new `DatasetRegistry::count_acquirable()` counts only
pending entries this model may claim: unassigned ones, plus ones assigned to `MODEL_NAME`, the same rule as `acquire()`. The remote check
used to count every pending entry, including other models'. The "no pending data" message now names the pool.

Verified with the real binaries:
- `dataset_manager --kind chatbot add d.jsonl` followed by `incremental_trainer --foreground train 1` (tiny model, local registry)

deployment.

until released by hand.

### TD-421: `KVCache::append()` Has No Shape Checks

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Inference / KVCache | October 13, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `KVCache` and verified under AddressSanitizer. `KVCache::append()` never compares
`new_keys` with `new_values`, or the new columns with the cached ones:
- Appending wider rows (`Matrix(1,8)` onto a cache of width 4) writes 8 columns into 4-column rows:
  **heap-buffer-overflow WRITE**.
- Appending fewer value rows than key rows (`append(Matrix(3,4), Matrix(1,4))`) indexes `new_values` by
  `new_keys.rows`: **heap-buffer-overflow READ**.
- An inconsistent first append (`keys 3×4`, `values 1×8`) is accepted silently.

Today's callers always pass matching shapes, so this is latent, but the failure mode is memory
corruption. `DecoderKVCache::get_self_attention_cache()`/`get_cross_attention_cache()` don't
bounds-check the layer index, and `current_length()` reads only layer 0.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate shapes in `append()` (throw `invalid_argument`), bounds-check layer indices, and add a direct `KVCache` test file.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-422).** `append()` throws `invalid_argument` when keys and values differ in shape or the new rows
have a different width from the cache, and a rejected append changes nothing. `DecoderKVCache::get_*_attention_cache()` throw
`out_of_range` for a bad layer index. New `tests/kvcache_test.cpp` (`kvcacheTests`): `RejectsMismatchedShapes` (the three cases from
the description), `LayerIndicesAreChecked`, plus TD-422's tests. Clean under AddressSanitizer.

Location in code: `src/KVCache.hpp` (`append()`, `get_*_cache()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-421`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/KVCache.hpp`
- `tests/` (new KVCache test)

### TD-422: `KVCache` Copies the Whole Cache on Every Append

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Inference / KVCache | October 13, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `KVCache` and measured. `append()` allocates new `[current_length + new_rows ×
d]` matrices and copies the old contents on every call. Self-attention caches get one append per decode
step per layer, so a generation of *n* tokens does O(n²·d) copying per layer before any attention work.
Measured for one cache at d_model 512, one row per step: 128 steps 15.6 ms, 256 steps 53.8 ms, 512 steps
255 ms (quadratic), which is about 6 s of pure copying for a 24-layer decoder generating 512 tokens on the
CPU serving path. `GPUKVCache` already pre-allocates to `max_seq_length`; this one doesn't. (The old
`kvcache.md` claimed O(d²) per cached step.)

Action Items:

- [x] Pre-allocate `keys`/`values` to `max_seq_length` (or grow geometrically) and track the populated length; give `MultiHeadAttention`/`CrossAttention` a view of the populated rows instead of a full copy.
- [ ] Do this with TD-388 and TD-398, which have the same per-step copy pattern. (Not done: TD-388 is the GPU cache and TD-398 the
  hippocampal memory. Both are left open.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `append()` grows the cache in place. `Matrix` keeps one vector per row, so new rows are pushed and no
cached row is copied (amortized O(new rows × d)). Attention reads the populated matrix by reference as before. Measured for one cache
at d_model 512, one row per step (`-O2`):

| Steps | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | 19.8 ms | 0.37 ms |
| 256 | 52.7 ms | 0.42 ms |
| 512 | 219 ms | 1.03 ms |

Test `AppendDoesNotCopyCachedRows` checks that the first row's buffer survives 300 appends; the old code reallocated it.
`AppendKeepsEveryRowInOrder` checks the contents. `MultiHeadAttention::forward_with_cache()` still copies the cache into
`cached_K`/`cached_V` for a backward pass that nothing runs after cached decoding, one more O(n·d) copy per step; that remains.

Location in code: `src/KVCache.hpp` (`append()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-422`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/KVCache.hpp`
- `src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp`
- `src/CrossAttention.cpp`
