### TD-466: `ModelSerializer` Claims T5 Compatibility It Doesn't Have and Skips Input Validation

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open (decision: make it T5-faithful) | Models / ModelSerializer | October 14, 2026 | 16-24 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `ModelSerializer`, by inspection:
- **Not T5.** Tensor names and `config.json` (`architectures: T5ForConditionalGeneration`, `model_type: t5`) claim HuggingFace T5, but
  ADAI uses sinusoidal positions (T5: learned, bucketed relative attention bias, which `transformers` would initialize randomly),
  LayerNorm with bias and mean-centering (T5: weight-only RMSNorm), a GELU FFN with biases (config says `feed_forward_proj: "relu"`;
  T5 linears have no biases), 1/√d_k attention scaling (T5: none), separate encoder/decoder embeddings (T5: one shared embedding) and
  an untied, biased LM head. Exports don't load meaningfully into `transformers`; importing a real T5 checkpoint always fails because
  `require()` demands bias tensors T5 doesn't have. The header's "unknown keys ignored (e.g. T5 position biases)" case is unreachable.
  (Embeddings aren't scaled in the forward pass, which already matches T5.)
- **Validation.** `read_safetensors()` ignores `dtype` (F16/BF16 fail later as "size mismatch in from_flat"); a huge/corrupt header
  length or `data_offsets` with `end < start` become giant allocations; offsets aren't checked against the file size. Import sets
  weights as it goes, so a missing tensor leaves the model half-overwritten.
- **Hygiene.** `json_escape()` is a no-op and unused; the files are tagged `stable` with no production caller.

**Decision (October 14, 2026):** owner chose to make the format **T5-faithful** (an export loads in `transformers`'
`T5ForConditionalGeneration` and produces the same outputs; real T5 checkpoints import), rather than relabelling it as an
ADAI-specific format. Only part of the gap can be closed in the serializer; the rest is a model-architecture change:

- *Mappable at export/import, no model change:* fold the 1/√d_k attention scale into the exported `q.weight` (and unfold on
  import); `tie_word_embeddings: false` for the untied LM head; `feed_forward_proj: "gelu"` (non-gated GELU) instead of `"relu"`;
  correct special-token IDs and `d_kv`.
- *Not representable in T5, so they require a T5-style architecture variant of `EncoderDecoderModel`:* RMSNorm without bias
  (`T5LayerNorm`) instead of `LayerNorm`; bias-free Q/K/V/O, FFN and LM head; bucketed relative position bias (per head, computed in
  layer 0 and shared) instead of sinusoidal positional encoding; one embedding shared by encoder and decoder; and, if the LM head is
  tied, T5's `d_model^-0.5` rescale before it. Existing checkpoints can't be converted exactly, so this is a new variant (selected
  per model, e.g. an MNS architecture flag, since architecture is immutable) trained from scratch or imported from a real T5
  checkpoint. Optionally support T5 v1.1's gated GELU (`wi_0`/`wi_1`).
- For the current (non-T5) architecture, TD-465's fix still applies: export the decoder embedding separately. Until the variant
  exists, the current export should stop claiming `T5ForConditionalGeneration`.

Action Items:

- [ ] Implement the export-side mappings above; stop labelling non-T5 models as `T5ForConditionalGeneration`.
- [ ] Add the T5-style architecture variant (RMSNorm, bias-free linears, relative position bias, shared embedding) and its MNS/config selection.
- [ ] Map T5 tensor names both ways for the variant, including `relative_attention_bias`; import a real `t5-small` checkpoint.
- [ ] Verify against `transformers` (encoder output and logits within tolerance for the same input); add that comparison as a test or script (needs `transformers`/`torch` in the dev environment).
- [ ] Validate dtype (accept F16/BF16 with conversion), header size and offsets; load into temporaries and apply only after all tensors validate.
- [ ] Remove `json_escape()`; reconsider the `stable` tag.

Location in code: `src/ModelSerializer.{hpp,cpp}` (class comment, `config.json` writer, `read_safetensors()`, `import_safetensors()`); the model classes for the variant; tagged `TODO: See TD-466`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ModelSerializer.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/LayerNorm.*` (or a new RMSNorm), `src/MultiHeadAttention.*`, `src/CrossAttention.*`, `src/FeedForward.*`, `src/LanguageModelHead.*`, positional encoding
- `src/ModelNameService.cpp`, `src/ModelNameClient.cpp` (architecture variant flag)

Description:
Found while tracing `MultiHeadAttention` (whose per-head backward was verified correct against finite differences):

  the divisibility check that would throw. Same as TD-299 (`CrossAttention`); MNS doesn't validate architectures (TD-461).

Covered by `EncoderDecoderModelTest.EveryCheckpointFileIsCheckedOnLoad`.

### TD-468: GPU Training Round-Trips Every Gradient and Weight Through a 3× Slow CPU Optimizer

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — device-resident optimizer landed October 19, 2026 | Core / Optimizer | October 14, 2026 | 8-16 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `Optimizer`:
- **Slow update loops (verified).** `step_sgd/…/step_adamw()`, the norm and clipping loops all index through `Matrix::operator()`
  (out-of-line, bounds-checked, TD-435); an AdamW step makes about six accessor calls per parameter. On 5.24M parameters (20 × 512²,
  `-O3 -march=native`, 8 threads) `Optimizer::step()` took **45.0 ms vs 14.2 ms** for the same AdamW over raw row pointers (3.2×);
  `get_gradient_norm()` adds 6.4 ms.
- **GPU training uses it on the host (by inspection, with an estimate).** The optimizer is CPU-only, so each optimizer step in
  `ChatbotTrainer`'s GPU path does `gpu_download_grads()` (every gradient to the host), `Optimizer::step()` on the CPU, then
  `gpu_sync_weights()` (every weight back to the device). For `config.trainer.conf`'s fallback architecture (d_model 768, d_ff 3072,
  8 + 24 layers ≈ 283M parameters before embeddings; MNS's record may differ) that's an estimated ~2.4 s of CPU AdamW at the measured
  rate (~0.8 s with raw pointers) plus ~2.3 GB of host↔device copies per optimizer step (every 32 samples with
  `GRADIENT_ACCUMULATION_STEPS=32`), on a SYCL build compiled without SIMD flags (TD-436). Not yet measured on ai-machine.

Action Items:

- [ ] Rewrite the update, norm and clip loops over raw row pointers (vectorizable); re-measure.
- [ ] Measure the per-step download/step/upload time on ai-machine.
- [x] Add a GPU-resident optimizer (AdamW kernels for CUDA and SYCL) keeping weights, gradients and moments on the device, so GPU training skips the round trip; keep the CPU optimizer for CPU training.

**Fix (October 19, 2026): the device-resident optimizer.** This follows the owner's rule that GPU training does all the training math on the GPU
and moves no data without a critical reason.
- **New kernels:** `src/GPUOptimizer.{hpp,cpp}` plus two kernels in both backends (`MatrixGPU.cu`, `sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp`):
  - `matrix_sum_squares_accumulate_gpu()`: a single pass that adds into a device slot, with no temporary buffer and no host wait;
  - `optimizer_update_gpu()`: the CPU `Optimizer`'s SGD, momentum, Adam and AdamW formulas, in the same order, with a gradient scale.
- **Binding:** every layer now reports its device weight and gradient buffers (`gpu_collect_parameters()`), and `GPUOptimizer` binds the CPU
  optimizer's groups to them by host-weight identity. The moments live on the device.
- **Per step:** `ChatbotTrainer`'s GPU path reduces every group's gradient on the device and downloads **one float per group**. Those are the
  squared norms that the NaN check, the clip, the zero-gradient skip and the per-layer norm metrics need. The TD-272 window rescale and the
  clip factor are folded into the update's gradient scale. The per-step `gpu_download_grads()` and `gpu_sync_weights()` are gone.
- **While training:** the device weights are the live copy. `sync_host_from_device()` copies weights and moments back to the host only
  before a checkpoint (`save_to()`, the best snapshot, `save_training_state()`), before the per-epoch quality-metrics `clone()`, and at the end
  of `train()`. `train()` uploads the host weights when it binds, since the host copy is authoritative between passes.
- **Host groups:** groups with no device mirror are stepped on the host with no transfer. These are the two token embeddings, and the gated
  world-model/hippocampal sub-layers when attached (TD-342). The embeddings are TD-547.

Verified on the oneAPI CPU SYCL device (new opt-in `ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`, TD-394), with the real kernels and classes:
- **`gpuOptimizerTests` (6):**
  - each rule matches the CPU `Optimizer` over three scaled steps (≤ 1e-5 relative);
  - the moments round-trip through the CPU optimizer;
  - a real model's device step matches the old download-and-CPU-step path through its logits (36 device groups, 2 host).
- **Existing suites on the device path:** `chatbottrainerTests` (83), `encoderdecoderTests` (90) and `incrementaltrainerTests` (58) all pass
  with every training test on the device path. The `IncrementalTrainer` fixture now initializes the GPU, as `incremental_trainer` does.
- **Real binary:** a SYCL `incremental_trainer` trained a pass on the CPU device (validation loss 4.09 → 3.94). A second pass resumed its
  checkpoint and restored its optimizer state at global step 18.

CUDA is compile-checked only. Still to do: the first action item (the CPU loops, which now matter only for CPU training), and measuring a
step on ai-machine.

Location in code: `src/Optimizer.cpp` (update/norm/clip loops); `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`gpu_download_grads()`/`gpu_sync_weights()` around `optimizer->step()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-468`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Optimizer.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp`
- `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.{hpp,cu}`, `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.{hpp,cpp}`

**Follow-up (October 19, 2026, TD-547).** The token embeddings are now device groups too, so a model without the gated paths has no
host groups left, and GPU training no longer zeroes host gradients every window.

### TD-470: Malformed Parquet Footers Hang or Crash `registry_server`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / ParquetReader | October 14, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `ParquetReader` and verified with hand-crafted files. `skip_value()` (the Thrift compact-protocol skipper for footer and
page-header fields the reader doesn't parse) has two unbounded paths:
- **Infinite loop.** A list's size comes from a varint, and skipping a `BOOL` element (types 1/2) consumes **no bytes**: that's the
  struct-field form, but in the compact protocol each list element is one byte. A **26-byte** file whose footer holds one unknown field with
  a bool list of size ~2⁶² made `convert_to_jsonl()` spin at 100% CPU until killed (20 s timeout).
- **Unbounded recursion.** Nested structs recurse once per byte; a footer with 400,000 nested struct fields crashed with **SIGSEGV** (stack
  overflow).

`ParquetReader` runs inside `registry_server` on every HuggingFace part fetched through `POST /registry/<group>/fetch/huggingface` (and the
dashboard's fetch dialog), so a malicious or corrupt dataset part ties up a request thread forever or **kills the registry daemon** (a
segfault can't be caught). Same class as TD-309. (25,000 random mutations under ASan/UBSan found no memory errors; these needed crafted input.)

Action Items:

- [x] Consume one byte per bool element when skipping a list; reject list sizes larger than the remaining bytes.
- [x] Add a recursion depth limit (e.g. 64) to `skip_value()` and the struct parsers.
- [x] Regression tests with the two crafted footers.

Location in code: `src/ParquetReader.cpp` (`skip_value()`, `read_list_header()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-470`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ParquetReader.cpp`
- `tests/parquet_reader_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **List sizes:** `read_list_header()` rejects a size larger than the bytes left, since every compact-protocol list element takes at
  least one byte. That bounds every list loop in the reader, not just the skipper.
- **Bool elements:** a new `skip_list_element()` consumes the one byte a bool element takes inside a list. All five list loops that
  skip elements use it.
- **Nesting:** `skip_value()` takes a depth and refuses beyond 64 levels.
- **Struct parsers:** these follow the fixed schema (one function per known struct), so data can't make them recurse; only
  `skip_value()` did.

Tests (`parquet_reader_test.cpp`):
- `HugeBoolListInFooterFailsInsteadOfLooping`: a 24-byte file with a 2⁶²-element bool list in an unknown footer field.
- `DeeplyNestedFooterFailsInsteadOfCrashing`: 400,000 nested structs.

Both now return −1, and the real fixtures still parse (12/12). On the old reader, the first was still spinning when killed after 20 s,
and the second segfaulted.

### TD-471: `ParquetReader` Trusts Declared Sizes for Allocations

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / ParquetReader | October 14, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `ParquetReader`. Sizes read from the file drive allocations before being checked against the bytes actually present:
`read_page_body()`'s `compressed.resize(compressed_page_size)` (a negative `int32` becomes a huge `size_t`), Snappy's declared
uncompressed length (`out.reserve()`), a page's `dp_num_values` (`int32` → `size_t`, then `def_levels.assign()`/`reserve()`), and
`decode_column_chunk()`'s `reserve(num_rows)`.
- **Verified:** 25,000 fuzz mutations produced **62 escaped `std::length_error`s** (`vector::reserve`, `string::resize`). Nothing in
  `ParquetReader` or `DataFetcher` catches them; `httplib` converts them to HTTP 500, so `registry_server` survives, but partially
  downloaded parts aren't cleaned up (compounding TD-313).
- **By inspection:** a plausible lie is worse than an absurd one: a page claiming 2³¹ values in a `REQUIRED` column allocates and fills 8 GB
  of definition levels from a few bytes (one RLE run can expand to `num_values` entries), pushing the host toward the OOM killer.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate every declared size before allocating: non-negative, bounded by the file size / remaining bytes, page `num_values` ≤ the column chunk's remaining values, Snappy length ≤ the page's `uncompressed_page_size` (and a sane cap).
- [x] Catch exceptions in `convert_to_jsonl()` (return −1) and clean up in `DataFetcher` on failure.

Location in code: `src/ParquetReader.cpp` (`read_page_body()`, `snappy_raw_uncompress()`, `decode_column_chunk()`); `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (the `convert_to_jsonl()` call); tagged `TODO: See TD-471`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ParquetReader.cpp`
- `src/DataFetcher.cpp`
- `tests/parquet_reader_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** Each declared size is checked against what can actually be present before it sizes an allocation:
- **Page bodies:** the compressed size must be non-negative and fit in the bytes left in the file, and the uncompressed size must be
  non-negative.
- **Snappy:** the declared length must be at most the page's `uncompressed_page_size` and at most 32 bytes per compressed byte (no Snappy
  element of n ≥ 2 bytes produces more than 64).
- **Pages:** a page's value count must be non-negative and at most the values left in its column chunk.
- **Columns:** a column chunk's value count must equal its row group's row count, since a flat schema has one value or null per row. This
  is checked for every chunk before any output.
- **Row groups:** at most 2²⁴ rows (`kMaxRowsPerRowGroup`, 16× pyarrow's default row group). The reader buffers a whole row group
  (TD-472), and a constant column RLE-encodes any number of rows in a few bytes, so the file size alone can't bound this.
- **Dictionaries and PLAIN values:** the count must be non-negative and at most 8 per byte; the smallest PLAIN value is one bit.
- **Bit-packed runs:** the group count is compared before multiplying, so it can't wrap past the bounds check.

`convert_to_jsonl()` catches exceptions (−1) and now keeps the header's promise that a failure leaves the output as it was:
- **Before:** a failure in a later row group kept the earlier row groups' rows, and a replacing write had already truncated the file.
- **Now:** an append is cut back to its original size, and a replacing write goes to `<out>.tmp`, which is renamed over the target only
  on success.

`DataFetcher` deletes a part it couldn't convert.

Tests (`parquet_reader_test.cpp`, using a small Thrift writer that builds a one-column file):
- `SyntheticColumnFileConverts`: the control.
- `RowGroupDeclaringBillionsOfRowsIsRejected`
- `PageClaimingMoreValuesThanItsColumnIsRejected`: the 8 GB definition-level fill.
- `NegativeOrOversizedPageSizeIsRejected`
- `MutatedFixturesNeverThrowAndFailuresLeaveOutputUnchanged`: 9,000 deterministic byte mutations of the six fixtures, each converted
  in append and replace mode.

On the old reader under a 4 GB address-space limit, the three crafted files throw `std::bad_alloc`/`std::length_error`, and the
mutation test fails on its 13th mutated file, where a failed replacing write had wiped the output. Without the limit, the page test would fill 8 GB.

### TD-473: `Profiler` Keeps Every Timing Forever, Sorts Under Its Lock and Uses the Wall Clock

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Inference / Profiler | October 15, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PerformanceProfiler`:
- **Unbounded samples (verified).** `ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` is always wrapped in `PROFILE_SCOPE` (`--profile` only gates
  `GET /admin/profile`'s output), and `ProfileStats::timings` keeps every sample: after 2,000,000 simulated requests it held 2M entries
  (16 MB), 8 bytes per request for the life of `chatbot_api_server`.
- **Sorting under the lock (verified).** `Profiler::get_stats()` copies and sorts the vector (`compute_median()`) while holding the profiler's
  mutex, which every in-flight `generate_response()` needs for `start()`/`stop()`: 72 ms at 2M samples. `handle_profile()` then sorts two more
  copies for p95/p99 (107 ms).
- **Wall clock (verified).** `Timer` uses `std::chrono::high_resolution_clock`, which in libstdc++ is `system_clock` (`is_steady == false`); an
  NTP step or manual change during a request records a wrong or negative duration.
- **By inspection.** `ScopedTimer`, `print()`, `print_all()`, `compare()` and `Benchmark::compare()` write to `std::cout` (test-only); percentiles
  use the floor index; `compare()` divides by `optimized.mean_time` unchecked.

Action Items:

- [ ] Use `std::chrono::steady_clock`.
- [ ] Replace the unbounded vector with a fixed-size reservoir or log-bucket histogram (constant memory, no sorting), and copy only summary values under the lock.
- [ ] Guard `compare()`'s division; route output through `Logger`.

### TD-474: `PipelineInferenceEngine` Strands Queued Requests on Shutdown and Skips `model_mutex_`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open | Inference / PipelineInferenceEngine | October 16, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PipelineInferenceEngine`:
- **Stranded requests (verified).** `shutdown()` sets `running_ = false`, shuts down both `ThreadSafeQueue`s and joins the workers, which exit on
  the next loop check and leave any queued `PipelineRequest`/`EncoderOutput` (each owning its `std::promise`) inside the queues until the engine
  is destroyed. With 3 requests submitted and `shutdown()` called while the first was in the encoder stage: request 0 → `Broken promise`, requests
  1–2 **still pending 3 s later** (a probe without a timeout hung for 1.5 h). `push()` after shutdown silently drops the item (the caller's future
  fails with `Broken promise`). In `chatbot_api_server` the engine is destroyed after the HTTP server stops, so its workers drain the queue first;
  the defect bites any direct caller of `shutdown()`.
- **No `model_mutex_` (by inspection).** `ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` routes through the pipeline without `model_mutex_`, while
  `/chat/batch` runs `model_->forward()` under it, so a batch request can run concurrently with the decoder thread on layers that cache forward
  state in members. Same as TD-419.

Action Items:

- [ ] On shutdown, drain both queues and fail (or finish) every pending request explicitly; make `push()` after shutdown report failure to the caller.
- [ ] Hold `model_mutex_` around the decoder stage (or give the pipeline exclusive use of the model), consistently with TD-419's fix.
- [ ] Test: shutdown with queued requests resolves every future promptly.

Location in code: `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (`shutdown()`, workers, `ThreadSafeQueue::push()`); `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (pipeline branch of `generate_response()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-474`.

- `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`
- `tests/pipelineinferenceengine_test.cpp`

### TD-475: `PipelineInferenceEngine` Throughput Claims, Greedy Uncached Decoding and Stats

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Inference / PipelineInferenceEngine | October 16, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PipelineInferenceEngine`:
- **Throughput (verified).** The header promises "2–3× throughput", but only the encoder stage overlaps decoding. On a real model (d_model 256,
  4+4 layers, debug build) one encoder pass took 144 ms and 50 greedy decode steps 8,480 ms: a best-case pipelining speedup of **1.017×**. The
  decode loop re-runs the full decoder over all tokens so far each step (no KV cache, O(n²)), and a batch's inputs are decoded one at a time. The
  documented 1.24× (PARALLEL_OPTIMIZATIONS_QUICK_REFERENCE.md) comes from `benchmarks/PipelineBenchmark.cpp`, whose stages are `sleep()`s.
- **By inspection.** Generation is greedy only, with `BOS`/`EOS` added to encoder input (TD-364) and no repetition handling, so answers differ from
  normal `/chat` (as TD-417). `avg_throughput_rps` divides by time since construction (decays while idle); `PipelineConfig::enable_profiling` is
  never read. `ThreadSafeQueue` uses one condition variable with `notify_one()` for producers and the consumer, so a push can wake another blocked
  producer instead of the consumer (up to 50 ms extra latency). Stage errors go to `std::cerr`; only `std::exception`s are caught.

Action Items:

- [ ] Correct the header and PARALLEL_OPTIMIZATIONS_QUICK_REFERENCE.md claims; benchmark against the real model.
- [ ] Use the KV-cached decode path (or retire the engine in favour of the real-batching v2 plan, with TD-420).
- [ ] Pass the request's generation settings through; fix the throughput stat; separate not-full/not-empty condition variables; `Logger` instead of `std::cerr`.

Location in code: `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (header comment, `decoder_worker()`, `ThreadSafeQueue`, stats); tagged `TODO: See TD-475`.

### TD-476: `PortableSocket` Short Writes Truncate FTP Transfers; Unchecked Socket Setup

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Platform / PortableSocket | October 16, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PortableSocket`:
- **Short writes (verified).** A blocking `send()` returns a partial count when a signal interrupts it after queuing some data, even with
  `SA_RESTART`: sending 8 MiB over a socket pair with a slow reader and one signal mid-send returned **219,264 bytes**. `send_bytes()` passes that
  through, and `FtpDataServer`'s `RETR` loop checks only `sent < 0` before adding the full chunk to `bytes_sent`, so the transfer is silently
  truncated while the server reports success (the client then fails on size, or reuses a same-size stale file, TD-338). Control replies ignore the
  result. Needs a signal during a transfer, rare in `registry_server` today.
- **By inspection.** `WinsockGuard` ignores a failed `WSAStartup()` (and still calls `WSACleanup()`); `set_reuse_addr()`/`set_recv_timeout()` ignore
  `setsockopt()` failures; Winsock doesn't apply `SO_RCVTIMEO` to `accept()`, so the PASV wait is unbounded on Windows (Linux returns `EAGAIN` after the
  timeout, verified); `last_socket_error()` reads `errno` late; `recv_bytes()` doesn't retry `EINTR`; no tests, and the MinGW build has never been run.

Action Items:

- [ ] Add `send_all()` (loop until written, retry `EINTR`) and use it for every `FtpDataServer` send; retry `EINTR` in `recv_bytes()`.
- [ ] Check and report `WSAStartup()`/`setsockopt()` results; bound PASV `accept()` with `select()`/`poll()` so it works on both platforms.
- [ ] Unit tests (socket pairs) for short writes and timeouts.

Location in code: `src/PortableSocket.hpp` (`send_bytes()`, `recv_bytes()`, `WinsockGuard`, `set_recv_timeout()`); `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`RETR` send loop); tagged `TODO: See TD-476`.

### TD-477: Timestamp Parsing Turns Bad Input Into 1899, Ignores Offsets and Misreads Fractions

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Platform / PortableTime | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PortableTime` and verified by running `strptime_utc()` through the callers' exact logic (`TrainingMetricsAPI::parse_iso8601()`,
`SQLiteMetricsDatabase::parse_timestamp()`, `PostgresMetricsDatabase::parse_timestamp()`), which all do
`tm{}; if (strptime_utc(...)) { if (*end == '.') ms = atoi(end + 1); } return timegm_utc(&tm) + ms;`:
- **Failure isn't reported.** `not-a-date` and a date-only `2026-10-15` both became `1899-12-31T00:00:00` (the zeroed `tm`). For
  `GET …/metrics/db-history`, a bad `from` silently means "since 1899" (everything) and a bad `to` "until 1899" (nothing), with HTTP 200.
- **Offsets ignored.** `2026-10-15T12:00:00+02:00` parsed as 12:00 UTC (two hours wrong).
- **No range checks.** `2026-13-45T25:61:99` became `2027-02-15T02:02:39` (`timegm()` normalizes); `%d` also accepts whitespace and signs, and has
  undefined behaviour on overflow.
- **Fractions.** `atoi()` reads the digits as an integer: `.12` → 12 ms, `.1` → 1 ms, `.123456` → 123,456 ms (+2 min). PostgreSQL prints its
  `TIMESTAMPTZ` columns without trailing zeros (`.12`), so the Postgres backend's `recorded_at`/`created_at`/`last_update_at` read back up to ~0.9 s early.
  (SQLite stores a fixed `.mmm` and is unaffected.)

Action Items:

- [ ] Add `parse_iso8601_utc()` returning `std::optional<time_point>`: strict digits and ranges, fractional seconds by digit position, `Z`/`±HH:MM` offsets, optional date-only form.
- [ ] Replace the three callers' copies; make `db-history` return 400 for an unparsable bound.
- [ ] Unit tests for the table above.

Location in code: `src/PortableTime.hpp` (`strptime_utc()`); `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`, `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`, `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.cpp` (`parse_*`); tagged `TODO: See TD-477`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/PortableTime.hpp`
- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`, `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`, `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.cpp`

### TD-479: Postgres Backend Drops Each Session's First History Batch on Foreign-Key Violations

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Database | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PostgresMetricsDatabase` and verified on a real PostgreSQL 16 cluster through the real `TrainingMetricsService`. The Postgres schema
has `session_key REFERENCES sessions(key)` on `metrics_history`, `gradient_variance_history`, `generation_quality` and `abnormal_samples` (SQLite doesn't
enforce foreign keys, so its backend is unaffected). `TrainingMetricsService` writes the session row only in `persist_summary()`, which runs **after**
`persist_metrics()` at each periodic persist and at `end_session()`; gradient-variance rows are inserted on every optimizer step from the start. Until the
first persist, every child insert fails with `violates foreign key constraint … Key (session_key)=(…) is not present in table "sessions"`, is retried 3
times by `execute_with_retry()` (~0.5 s of sleeps, blocking the ingest handler) and is dropped. With a fresh key and `persist_every_samples = 5`, the run
ended with the session row present but **0 history rows and 0 gradient-variance rows**. At the defaults every session loses its first persist batch and every
gradient-variance row before the first persist (100 steps or 30 s), and the trainer's per-step `/metrics/advanced` pushes stall 0.5 s each meanwhile; short
sessions can lose everything. The backend's own tests always upsert the session first.

Action Items:

- [x] Upsert the session row in `TrainingMetricsService::start_session()` (and/or run `persist_summary()` before `persist_metrics()`).
- [x] Don't retry constraint violations (check the SQLSTATE class) in `execute_with_retry()`.
- [x] Add a live test that writes child rows through `TrainingMetricsService` without a prior upsert.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** `start_session()` upserts the session row as soon as a database is attached, so every child row that follows
has its parent. `execute_with_retry()` retries only when the connection is gone: a statement the server rejects on a healthy connection
(a constraint violation, a bad value) fails at once and is logged, instead of sleeping ~0.5 s in retries. Test
`FreshServiceSessionKeepsFirstRowsWithoutRetryStalls` (`postgres_metrics_database_test.cpp`, real PostgreSQL 16): a service with a fresh
key and no upsert first writes 5 samples and 5 gradient-variance rows. All of them are stored, in about 1 s. With the old code it stored
0 history rows and 0 gradient-variance rows and took 5.5 s.

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsService.cpp` (`start_session()`, `persist_metrics()`/`persist_summary()` order); `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.cpp` (child inserts, `execute_with_retry()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-479`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingMetricsService.cpp`
- `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.cpp`
- `tests/postgres_metrics_database_test.cpp`

### TD-480: `PostgresMetricsDatabase` One-Time Schema Bootstrap, Reconnects Under Lock and Unsafe Retries

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Metrics / Database | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PostgresMetricsDatabase`, by inspection:
- **One-time bootstrap.** `bootstrap_schema()` runs only in the constructor and only if `pool_[0]` connected; if PostgreSQL is down when
  `metrics_api_server` starts, later reconnects succeed but a fresh database never gets its tables, so every statement fails until restart.
- **Blocking under the lock.** `acquire_connection()` calls `ensure_connection()` (a blocking `PQconnectdb()`) while holding `pool_mutex_`, and
  `execute_with_retry()` reconnects under it too, so one slow reconnect stalls every caller; no `connect_timeout`/`statement_timeout` unless the URL sets one.
- **Unsafe retries.** An insert whose result was lost with its connection (committed but unacknowledged) is re-executed, duplicating the row; non-retryable
  errors (constraint, syntax) are retried with full back-off.
- **Archive collision.** `archive_session()` inserts under `archived_key` with plain `INSERT`; an existing row with that key aborts the transaction (unlikely:
  keys carry a millisecond timestamp and counter).

Action Items:

- [ ] Bootstrap the schema on the first successful connection (any time), not just at construction.
- [ ] Reconnect outside `pool_mutex_`; set `connect_timeout` and `statement_timeout` defaults.
- [ ] Classify errors (retry only connection failures); make inserts idempotent where retried (e.g. client-side IDs with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`).

Location in code: `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.cpp` (constructor, `acquire_connection()`, `execute_with_retry()`, `archive_session()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-480`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-481: PPO Advantages Are Normalized Within Each Response

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open (deferred with RLHF) | RLHF / PPOOptimizer | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PPOOptimizer` and verified. `compute_gae()` normalizes each trajectory's (one response's) advantages to mean 0 and unit standard
deviation, and `RLHFTrainer::apply_policy_gradient()` weights each token's log-probability gradient by those advantages. With the reward on the last
token (as `RLHFTrainer` assigns it) and value estimates of 0:
- reward +1 → advantages −1.370, −0.727, −0.043, +0.684, +1.457; reward **+100 → identical**;
- reward −1 → the same with signs flipped;
- a one-token response with reward +5 → advantage **0.000**.

So the update ignores the reward's magnitude, pushes **down** the early tokens of a well-rewarded response (and up those of a badly rewarded one), and
learns nothing from one-token responses. RLHF has no production entry point (owner, October 17, 2026: its use will be planned later).

Action Items:

- [ ] Normalize advantages across a batch of rollouts (or not at all, relying on the value baseline), not within one response.
- [ ] Test: a positive reward gives non-negative advantages for every token under a zero baseline; magnitude scales the update.

Location in code: `src/PPOOptimizer.hpp` (`compute_gae()`); `src/RLHFTrainer.cpp` (use of `compute_advantages()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-481`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/PPOOptimizer.hpp`
- `src/RLHFTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/phase5_test.cpp`, `tests/rlhftrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-482: `PPOOptimizer` Never Updates the Policy and Its Ratio Is Always 1

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open (deferred with RLHF) | RLHF / PPOOptimizer | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `PPOOptimizer`:
- **No policy update (by inspection).** `update()` computes the clipped surrogate `−min(r·A, clip(r)·A)` and an approximate KL, trains only its
  `ValueFunction`, and returns the loss; nothing differentiates it into the policy. The real update is `RLHFTrainer::apply_policy_gradient()`, an
  unclipped policy gradient.
- **Ratio always 1 (verified).** `RLHFTrainer` passes a callback returning the rollout's own old log-probs, so `r = 1` on every call: no clipping, KL ≡ 0
  (the `1.5 × kl_target` early stop never fires) and a reported loss of 0.000000 (`−mean(A)` of normalized advantages).
- **Unused configuration (by inspection).** `entropy_coef`, `value_coef`, `max_grad_norm` and the private `clip_gradients()` are never used;
  `reward_model_` is stored but never read; minibatches aren't shuffled; `ValueFunction` uses the unseeded C `rand()`.
- The header and the replaced API doc promise "stable policy updates via the clipped surrogate objective" and KL monitoring.

Action Items:

- [ ] Apply the clipped objective to the policy (compute new log-probs with the live model each PPO epoch and backpropagate the clipped loss, with KL early stopping), or rename this to what it is (value function + GAE) and make `RLHFTrainer`'s update the documented REINFORCE-with-baseline.
- [ ] Wire `entropy_coef`/`max_grad_norm`/`value_coef` or remove them; drop the unused `reward_model_`; seed/shuffle properly.

Location in code: `src/PPOOptimizer.hpp` (`update()`, `PPOConfig`); `src/RLHFTrainer.cpp` (the `log_prob_fn` callback, `apply_policy_gradient()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-482`.

### TD-483: `Quantization` Asymmetric Range, Mode-Less Files and Unpacked INT4

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open | Advanced / Quantization | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `Quantization.hpp` (no production use: tests and examples only; a quantization tool is deferred under TD-014):
- **Asymmetric range (verified).** `calibrate()` clamps `zero_point` to `[qmin, qmax]` instead of widening the calibration range to include 0. For data
  in [5, 10], `zero_point = −255` was clamped to 0, every value quantized to 255, and the round trip returned 5.000 for all of 5, 6, 7.5, 9, 10. Any all-positive
  (e.g. post-ReLU) or all-negative tensor collapses to one value.
- **Mode not saved (verified).** `QuantizedMatrix::save()` stores scale/zero point/qmin/qmax but not the mode, and `dequantize()` decides signed vs unsigned
  decoding from the caller's `Quantizer`. An `ASYMMETRIC_INT8` matrix of 0/5/15/20, reloaded and dequantized with a default `Quantizer`, gave 0, 5.02, −5.10,
  −0.08 (TD-075's corruption).
- **INT4 unpacked (verified).** One value per byte: `memory_reduction()` reported 3.98× for `SYMMETRIC_INT4`; the header and the replaced API doc promise 8×.
- **By inspection.** Per-channel quantization is described but not implemented; `CalibrationMethod::MSE` silently falls back to min/max; `load()` checks no
  reads and doesn't validate `size` against `rows × cols`; `memory_reduction()` uses `int` byte counts; `print_quantization_stats()` writes to `std::cout`.

Action Items:

- [ ] Asymmetric calibration: `min = min(min, 0)`, `max = max(max, 0)` (standard), then compute `zero_point` without clamping away the range.
- [ ] Decode from the saved `qmin`/`qmax` (or save the mode); validate `load()`.
- [ ] Pack INT4 two per byte (or correct the claims); implement or remove per-channel and MSE calibration.

### TD-484: RAG Prompt Budget Lets the Question Fall Past `max_seq_length`

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (see [RAGInference.md](../reference/source/RAGInference.md)). `truncateContext()` converts
`max_context_length` to characters at 4 per token, and only the retrieved context is budgeted: `context_prefix`, `query_prefix` and the query are added
afterwards. The shipped values are `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH=512` and `MAX_SEQ_LENGTH=512`, so even with an exact estimate the context alone fills every
position and the question lands after position 512, where the encoder adds no positional encoding (the input isn't truncated, TD-365).
- **Verified:** with a vocabulary built by this repo's `BPETokenizer` from the project's guides, a 2,048-character context of three of those documents was
  **1,150 tokens** (1.8 characters per token) and the full prompt **1,178 tokens**, 2.3× `max_seq_length`. (That vocabulary had 402 entries; a production
  one compresses better, but not to 4 characters per token for this kind of text.)
- **By inspection:** the character cut can split a UTF-8 sequence before the `...`.

Action Items:

- [x] Budget the whole prompt in real tokens (the model's tokenizer): `max_seq_length` minus the query and prefixes, the rest for context.
- [x] Truncate documents at token (or at least UTF-8 character) boundaries; prefer dropping whole lower-ranked documents first.
- [x] Clamp `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH` to the model's `max_seq_length` and document the relationship in `config.chatbot.conf`.
- [x] Test: the augmented prompt never exceeds `max_seq_length` tokens.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `RAGInference::buildBudgetedPrompt()` replaces `truncateContext()`. It counts real tokens with the
model's tokenizer and keeps the question (with its prefix) whole. The context, documents in rank order, is cut from the end at a
UTF-8 boundary (`"..."` appended) by a binary search for the longest prefix with which the context fits `max_context_length` and the
whole prompt fits the model's `max_seq_length`. Cutting from the end drops lower-ranked documents first and trims the top-ranked one
only when it alone is too long. When no context fits, or the question alone reaches `max_seq_length`, the prompt is the question alone
(the encoder keeps its last tokens, TD-365). `chatbot_api_server` caps `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH` to the model's `max_seq_length` with
a warning, and `config.chatbot.conf`/`OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md` describe the relationship. Tests (`RAGInferencePromptBudgetTest`, which
replaces the `truncateContext()` tests): a three-document context where the old rule overflowed `max_seq_length` now fits with the
question whole, the top document in and the last dropped; a fitting context is unchanged; the `max_context_length` cap; UTF-8-valid
cuts with multibyte text; question-only prompts for no budget and an over-long question.

Location in code: `src/RAGInference.cpp` (`truncateContext()`, `generateWithRetrieval()` step 3); tagged `TD-484`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RAGInference.{hpp,cpp}`
- `config.chatbot.conf`
- `tests/raginference_test.cpp`

### TD-485: RAG Session Retrieval Uses the Start of the Conversation

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (by inspection). For `/chat/session`, `ChatbotAPI` passes the whole formatted conversation
(`ConversationContext::format_for_model()`, `"User: …\nAssistant: …"`) to `generate_response()`, and the RAG branch hands that string to `RAGInference::generate()`
as the query. `DocumentStore::retrieve()` embeds it with `LLMEncoder::encode()`, which keeps only the **first** `max_seq_length` tokens, so once a
conversation is longer than that, retrieval is chosen by the system message and the oldest turns, and the latest question doesn't take part. The same
string then becomes the "Question:" after the context, compounding TD-484.

**Correction (October 27, 2026):** this was written before TD-365, which made the encoder keep the **last** `max_seq_length` tokens.
Since then the whole-conversation query does include the latest question, but mostly earlier turns, so retrieval still didn't follow
the question; the fix below doesn't depend on which end is kept.

Action Items:

- [x] Pass the latest user message to RAG as the retrieval query, separately from the conversation history.
- [x] Build the prompt as context + (budgeted) history + latest question.
- [x] Test retrieval in a multi-turn session longer than `max_seq_length`.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `handle_chat_session()` and the batch-session path capture the conversation before the new user
message (`format_for_model()`) and pass `ChatbotAPI::RagTurn{message, history}` to `generate_response()`; its RAG branch calls
`RAGInference::generate(question, history)`. Non-RAG paths still get the whole formatted conversation. Retrieval uses the question
alone. `buildBudgetedPrompt(query, context, history)` builds context + history + question within `max_seq_length`: the question
whole, the context within `max_context_length`, then as much of the history's end as fits (cut from the front at a UTF-8 boundary),
so the oldest turns go first. Tests: `RetrievalUsesTheLatestQuestionInALongSession` (a 60-turn session about one document whose
latest question is the other document's text; the fix retrieves that document with similarity 1, while the whole-conversation
query used before scores it strictly lower; which document an untrained encoder then ranks first varies, so that isn't asserted),
`HistoryKeepsItsLatestTurnsWithinTheBudget`, and `SessionTurnsGiveRagTheLatestMessageAndTheHistory` (the second turn's query is the
message alone, the history holds the first turn). These tests exposed TD-222 (the tokenizer cache leaked between tokenizers at a reused address, so token counts depended on
test order), fixed alongside; both new RAG tests also failed in the full binary on the old tokenizer.

### TD-486: RAG Path Bypasses Strategy, Reloaded Settings and GPU Generation

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (by inspection). When RAG is enabled, `ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` returns
`rag_engine_->generate(input)` before any other path, and:
- **Strategy:** `generateWithRetrieval()` always passes `strategy = ""` (the default combined sampling branch), so `STRATEGY=nucleus` (shipped) and
  `BEAM_WIDTH` have no effect. `gen_config.num_beams` stays 1, so TD-261 isn't reached from the server, but any caller setting it above 1 gets beam search.
- **Settings copied once:** `ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` copies `MAX_GEN_LENGTH`/`TEMPERATURE`/`TOP_P`/`TOP_K` into `RAGConfig::gen_config` at startup. A `SIGHUP`
  reload updates `ChatbotAPI`'s `default_config_`, which RAG bypasses, and per-request values never reach it either (TD-254).
- **CPU only:** `EncoderDecoderModel::generate_response_with_strategy()` is the CPU path, so on a GPU server enabling RAG moves every request off TD-033's GPU
  decode path.

Action Items:

- [x] Give `RAGInference` a way to build the augmented prompt only, and let `ChatbotAPI` generate from it through its normal path (strategy, config, GPU).
- [x] (Not needed: the first item covers it.) Or pass the request's `GenerationConfig` (strategy included) into `generate()`.
- [x] Test that RAG honours `strategy` and reloaded settings.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `RAGInference::buildPrompt(query, history)` does retrieval and the budgeted prompt only (steps 1–4).
`ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` asks the RAG engine for the prompt and then generates from it like any other request, so the
request's strategy and `GenerationConfig`, `SIGHUP`-reloaded settings, speculative decoding, the TD-038 engines and the GPU decode
all apply. `RAGInference::generate()`/`generateWithRetrieval()` remain for standalone use with `RAGConfig::gen_config` on the CPU;
`buildPrompt()` is the virtual test seam now (`generate()` no longer is), so `RAGInference.hpp` is version 2.0.0. Tests:
`RagHonoursTheRequestStrategyAndConfig` (greedy through RAG equals greedy from the same prompt without RAG, three times, and a
changed `max_length` reaches RAG requests) and, in GPU builds, `RagRequestsTakeTheGpuDecode` (run on the oneAPI CPU device with
`ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`). The old RAG path couldn't be run against these tests (the seam they override is new); by
inspection it called `generate_response_with_strategy()` on the CPU with an empty strategy and startup settings.

Location in code: `src/RAGInference.cpp` (`generateWithRetrieval()` step 5), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`generate_response()`'s RAG branch), `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (`rag_config` setup); tagged `TD-486`.

### TD-487: `RAGInference` Misconfiguration and Observability Gaps

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (by inspection):
- **`RAG_NUM_DOCS ≤ 0`** isn't validated; once any document is indexed, `DocumentStore::retrieve()` throws `"k must be positive"` on every request, so every
  chat request fails (an empty store returns before the check).
- **`RAG_THRESHOLD`** can remove every retrieved document silently: the prompt loses its `Context:` section and nothing is logged.
- **No retrieval logging:** nothing records which documents were used or their scores; the server calls `generate()`, discarding
  `generateWithRetrieval()`'s list.
- **`getConfig()`/`setConfig()`** are unsynchronized (no production caller of `setConfig()` today).

Action Items:

- [x] Validate `RAG_NUM_DOCS > 0` and `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH > 0` at startup (with TD-241/TD-288).
- [x] Log retrieved document IDs and scores at debug level, and warn when the threshold empties the context.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `RAGInference::validateConfig()` runs in the constructor and `setConfig()` and throws
`std::invalid_argument` for `num_retrieved_docs` or `max_context_length` below 1 (a rejected `setConfig()` keeps the old config).
`chatbot_api_server` builds the engine inside its RAG setup's `try`, so a bad `RAG_NUM_DOCS`/`RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH` is logged at
startup and the server runs without RAG, instead of failing every request. `ConfigLoader::validate()` checks both when RAG is
enabled (it still runs only on reload, TD-241). `buildPrompt()` logs each retrieved document's id and similarity at debug level, and
warns when `RAG_THRESHOLD` removes every retrieved document. `getConfig()`/`setConfig()` remain unsynchronized; nothing calls
`setConfig()` while serving. Tests: `ConfigWithNoDocumentsOrNoContextIsRejected`, `RetrievalIsLoggedAndAnEmptyingThresholdWarns`
(both fail on the old code).

Location in code: `src/RAGInference.cpp` (`generateWithRetrieval()` steps 1–2), `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (`rag_config` setup); tagged `TD-487`.

### TD-488: `registry_server` Accepts Malformed Numbers, Valueless Flags and Unknown Arguments

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open | Data / Registry Server CLI | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServerArgs.cpp` (see [RegistryServerArgs.md](../reference/source/RegistryServerArgs.md)); verified with the real
`registry_server` binary:
- **Numbers:** every numeric flag uses bare `std::stoi`. `--port abc` threw an uncaught `std::invalid_argument` (abort, core dump, exit 134); `--port 8090x`
  was accepted as 8090; `--port 99999` logged "listening on port 99999" but bound 34463. By inspection, nothing is range-checked: `--ftp-ttl 0` or negative
  issues already-expired FTP tokens, `--ftp-max-sessions 0` makes every FTP login fail with 421, `--ftp-pasv-min > --ftp-pasv-max` empties the PASV pool (425).
- **Valueless flags:** a value flag is matched only when a value follows, so a trailing one is dropped silently. A bare `--admin-enabled` left
  `PUT /admin/config` open (HTTP 200); a trailing `--ftp-secret` leaves the key random, a trailing `--port` falls back to 8082. (Unknown values such as
  `flase` fail closed, 403, unlike TD-456.)
- **Unknown arguments:** ignored without a message (`--portt 8091` started on 8082), so typos such as `--ftp-enable` leave features off. The header documents
  this as preserved legacy behaviour and a test asserts it.

Action Items:

- [ ] Parse numbers with full-string checks and ranges (ports 1–65535, TTL and sessions > 0, PASV min ≤ max); report errors and exit non-zero instead of aborting.
- [ ] Treat a value flag with no value, and any unknown argument, as an error with usage; update `UnrecognizedArgumentIsSilentlyIgnored`.
- [ ] Share the helper with TD-240/TD-438/TD-456.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServerArgs.cpp` (`parse_registry_server_args()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-488`.

### TD-490: `registry_server` Group Names Escape `data_dir`, Letting Delete Unlink Outside It

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| HIGH | Open — code fix landed October 21, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp` (see [RegistryServer.md](../reference/source/RegistryServer.md)); verified with the real binary. The route
regex captures `<group>` as `[^/]+` and every handler uses it unvalidated in `data_dir + "/" + group` (`group_dir()`, `get_group()`, `handle_delete()`'s
`group_root`). httplib accepts both `/registry/../…` and `/registry/%2e%2e/…`:
- `upload?filename=t1.jsonl` through group `..` wrote `<data_dir>/../uploads/t1.jsonl` (and a `pending_files.txt` in `data_dir`'s parent).
- **File deletion:** with `<parent>/models/checkpoint.bin` present, `pending/add` + `delete {"delete_files":true}` through group `g` refused to unlink it,
  but through group `..` the containment root became the parent and the file was **deleted** (`file_deleted:true`).
With the default relative `REGISTRY_DATA_DIR=registry_sessions`, the parent is the working directory (checkpoints, configs, binaries). The server has no
authentication (trusted-LAN design), so any LAN host, or anyone past Cloudflare Access, can delete files there with two requests. By inspection, group `.`
maps to `data_dir` itself, reaching `daemon_config.db`, `session_counters.db` and other groups' files.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate `<group>` against a strict pattern (e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`, never `.`/`..`) in every route, returning 400.
- [x] Check `group_dir()` results resolve under `data_dir` (canonicalized) before use.
- [x] Add live tests for `..`, `%2e%2e` and `.` groups.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`group_dir()`, `get_group()`, `handle_delete()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-490`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Route check:** every `/registry/<group>/…` route (all 16) checks the group with `group_ok()` before calling its handler, and
  answers 400 `invalid group name` otherwise. A valid name is one plain path component, `[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*` of at most
  128 characters, so `.` and `..` can't pass. httplib decodes the URL before routing, so `%2e%2e` is checked as `..`.
- **Defense in depth:** `group_dir()` throws for an invalid name, and `handle_delete()`'s containment root is built from it.
- **Not changed:** existing group names (`chatbot-v1`, `my-training-group`) are unaffected. MNS doesn't validate `run_group`, so an
  invalid one stored there now gets a clear 400 from the registry.

Verified against the real binary:
- **The attack:** a `checkpoint.bin` was placed in `data_dir`'s parent, then `pending/add` and `delete {"delete_files":true}` sent
  through group `..` (`curl --path-as-is`) and `%2e%2e`. All three got 400, the file survived, and no `pending_files.txt` appeared
  in the parent.
- **Live tests:** `dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`'s new `LiveRegistryGroupNames` tests:
  - `%2e%2e`, `%2E%2E`, `.`, `%2e`, `.hidden` and a kind-scoped `%2e%2e/chatbot` get 400, or no 200 for `delete`/`pending/add`;
  - ordinary names still work.
- **Suite:** 89/89 live tests pass against the fixed server.

### TD-491: Concurrent Registry Fetches Serve and Overwrite the Same Slice

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`; verified. `handle_fetch_huggingface()`/`handle_fetch_gutenberg()` read the per-(source, model) cursor, write
`…_row<offset>_training.jsonl` and write the cursor back **without holding any lock** (the group mutex is taken only to queue the result). Eight
concurrent `fetch/huggingface` requests for 1,000 pairs each, against a pre-cached 20,000-row dataset, all returned `served_from_row: 0` and
`added: true`; one file was queued and the cursor advanced to 1,000. Callers were told 8,000 pairs were added; 1,000 were, written by eight writers into the
same file at once. After a wrap-around a fetch also rewrites an earlier `_row<offset>` file that may still be pending or claimed.

Action Items:

- [x] Serialize cursor read → write → advance per cursor (a per-cursor mutex, or the group mutex around the slice step).
- [x] Make output names unique (e.g. include a sequence number) and report `added:false` when nothing new was queued.
- [x] Test concurrent fetches.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_fetch_gutenberg()`, `handle_fetch_huggingface()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-491`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `handle_fetch_huggingface()` and `handle_fetch_gutenberg()` now hold a mutex per cursor file
(`fetch_cursor_mutex()`) from reading the cursor to queuing the slice and advancing it:
- **Concurrent fetches:** for one (source, model) they run one after another, each serving the next slice. Different cursors don't wait
  for each other, and the download/cache step stays outside the lock.
- **Slice names:** `unique_slice_path()` appends `_<n>` when `…_row<offset>_training.jsonl` already exists. After a wrap-around, a fetch
  no longer rewrites an earlier slice that may be pending, claimed or trained.
- **Queuing:** `queue_fetched_slice()` uses `add_pending_path_locked()`'s result. If nothing new was queued, it removes the file, answers
  409 `{"added":false,"reason":"already_queued"}`, and doesn't advance the cursor.

Tests: the live registry suite gains `REGISTRY_SERVER_DATA_DIR`, so a test can seed a cached dataset in the server's data directory (no
network).
- `ConcurrentFetchesServeDistinctSlices`: eight concurrent fetches of 10 pairs serve rows 0–70 once each and queue eight files.
- `WrappedFetchesNeverReuseASliceFile`: six fetches over a 20-row dataset give six files and six queue entries.

On the old server, the first served only rows 0 and 10 (two files queued, eight `added:true`), and the second gave three files for six
fetches. The whole live suite passes against the fixed server (92 tests).

While testing, a stale server left on the same port took part of the traffic; that's TD-551.

### TD-492: Registry Upload Silently Replaces Pending or Claimed Files

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`; verified. `handle_upload()` truncates and rewrites `<group_dir>/uploads/<filename>` whatever its queue state.
Uploading `d.jsonl`, claiming it as run `r1`, then uploading different content under the same name returned `added: true`, replaced the bytes under the
claim, and queued nothing new (`add_pending_path_locked()` returned false; its result is ignored). A trainer then trains, or downloads over FTP, data
that is not what was queued, and a trained file's recorded checksum no longer matches.

Action Items:

- [x] Refuse (409) an upload whose target is pending, claimed or trained, unless an explicit `overwrite` is given and the entry is unclaimed.
- [x] Write to a temporary name and rename; report `added:false` when the path was already queued.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_upload()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-492`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `handle_upload()` writes the body to `<path>.upload-<n>.tmp` and decides under the group lock whether it may
replace the target:

| Target | Result |
|---|---|
| claimed by a run | 409 `"reason":"claimed"` (even with `overwrite=true`) |
| trained (in the registry) | 409 `"trained"`; with `overwrite=true`, replaced and queued again as a new version |
| queued, unclaimed, whole file | 409 `"already_queued"`; with `overwrite=true`, replaced, and its pending entry's size, checksum, entry count and `added_utc` refreshed (`{"added":false,"replaced":true}`) |
| queued as TD-205 segments | 409 `"segmented"`, since a new version would break the row ranges |
| not queued or trained | renamed into place and queued (`{"added":true}`), as before |

A refused upload leaves the existing file untouched and deletes the temporary file. `RemoteTransport::upload_file()` now logs the
server's reason with the status, so `dataset_manager add` of an already-queued file says why it failed. It used to overwrite silently;
neither it nor the Android app offers `overwrite` yet, so a deliberate replacement is a `curl` with `?overwrite=true` (adding the option to both is TD-552).

Tests (live, `dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`):
- `UploadOverAClaimedFileIsRefused`: the file's bytes are unchanged, checked with `REGISTRY_SERVER_DATA_DIR`.
- `UploadOverwriteReplacesAnUnclaimedQueuedFile`: still one queue entry, with the new size and entry count.
- `UploadOverATrainedFileNeedsOverwrite`
- `UploadDeduplicatesSamePath`: now expects 409 `already_queued`; it had asserted the old overwrite.

All four fail against the old server, and the whole live suite passes against the new one (95 tests).

### TD-493: Registry `trained` Ignores Claim Ownership and Records Each Path Once

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`; verified. `handle_trained()` adds a registry record for every listed file not already in the registry,
regardless of `run_id`; only the pending removal checks the claim. With `d.jsonl` claimed by `r1`, `trained` from run `other` returned `trained: 1` and
recorded it, while the entry stayed pending and claimed by `r1`; `r1`'s own `trained` then returned `trained: 0` (path already recorded) but removed the
pending entry, so `r1`'s sample count and `model_id` were never recorded. Because the registry is deduplicated by bare path, a file re-queued and trained
again is never recorded again either (TD-333 covers segments).

Action Items:

- [x] Record a file only when it is pending and claimed by the calling `run_id` (or an explicit force), and report rejected files.
- [x] Key registry records by (path, segment, run) or append history instead of skipping already-recorded paths.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_trained()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-493`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport` equivalent)
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** A report with a `run_id` records a unit only when that run holds the unit's claim: a pending entry for the
path, or exactly that segment in exact mode, with the same `run_id`.
- **Server (`handle_trained()`):** a unit reported by a run that doesn't hold its claim isn't recorded, and the reply lists it in a new
  `"rejected"` array (`{"trained":N,"rejected":[…]}`). The pending removal was already claim-checked and is unchanged.
- **Retraining:** a claimed unit is recorded even when an earlier pass recorded it, so a unit re-queued (or re-uploaded with
  `overwrite=true`, TD-492) and trained again keeps each pass's record and sample count. That's the "append history" option; duplicates
  within one request still collapse.
- **Forced reports:** an empty `run_id` is still an explicit force, as for `release`: it records a unit not already recorded.
- **Standalone mode:** `LocalTransport::commit_trained()` applies the same claim check under its pending lock.
- **Client:** `DatasetRegistry::build_new_versions()` no longer drops already-recorded units from run-scoped commits
  (`record_again`), so a re-trained unit is sent with its real count instead of 0. The run-less test overload keeps the old skip.
  `RemoteTransport::commit_trained()` logs a warning when the registry rejects units.
- **Requeue:** `requeue_trained()` with several records for one path re-queues it once, reports the others as `already_pending`, and
  removes all of them.

Tests:
- `RegistryTransportTests.cpp`: `CommitTrainedRecordsOnlyUnitsTheRunClaimed`, `CommitTrainedRecordsAUnitTrainedAgain`.
- Live: `TrainedFromAnotherRunIsRejected` (`trained:0`, path rejected, and then the owner's report records it with its count) and
  `ReTrainedUnitIsRecordedAgain` (two records, 5 and 7 samples). Both fail against the old server.
- `TrainedDeduplicatesInRegistry` asserted the old skip for a re-trained unit. It now checks that a forced report still skips one.

The whole live suite passes against the fixed server (97 tests).

### TD-494: `registry_server` Startup, Lease, Thread-Pool and Parsing Gaps

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`:
- **Bind failure exits 0 (verified):** with the port in use, `listen()` returns false and the server logs "registry_server stopped" and exits 0, so
  restart-on-failure never fires.
- **Compact-only JSON (verified):** `{"run_id": "r2"}` (space after the colon) gave `400 run_id required`; incoming strings aren't unescaped and
  `json_int_array()` turns bad values into 0.
- **By inspection:** SIGTERM before `listen()` is lost (as TD-464); claims have no lease, so a crashed trainer's files stay claimed until released by
  hand; fetch downloads run in the request thread and can occupy httplib's pool (8 threads on small hosts), stalling `acquire`/`trained`; upload bodies
  are unbounded and held in memory; `session/next` keys on `model_name|run_id` with `model_name` unvalidated; `/health` is ok even without
  `session_counters.db`.

Action Items:

- [x] Log and exit non-zero when `listen()` fails; handle a stop requested before `listen()`. *(October 24, 2026, with TD-551: exits 1 with the port in the log; a stop requested before `listen()` skips it, though one arriving in the last instant before `listen()` is still lost.)*
- [x] Parse request bodies with the vendored `nlohmann/json` (with TD-453).
- [x] Consider claim leases (expiry + renewal) or an explicit stale-claim report; run fetches off the request pool; cap upload size. *(October 25, 2026, owner choices: leases with renewal, a concurrent-fetch cap, a configurable 2 GiB upload cap.)*

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`main()`, JSON helpers, `handle_session_next()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-494`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`

**Partial fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **Request bodies:** parsed with the vendored nlohmann/json behind the same helper signatures, so none of the ~60 call sites changed.
  Each request thread caches its parse. As a result:
  - whitespace is accepted (`{"run_id": "r2"}` works);
  - escapes are decoded (`\u00e9` becomes `é`, `\"` becomes `"`);
  - only top-level keys match, where a key name inside a value used to match;
  - non-integers, fractions and out-of-range numbers give the default;
  - an integer array with a bad element is treated as not sent instead of carrying a silent 0, since those arrays are aligned with
    `files`;
  - a body that isn't a JSON object gives the defaults.
- **`session/next`:** rejects a `model_name` outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]*` or a `run_id` containing `|` (400), since either could make two
  (model, run) pairs share one counter.
- **`/health`:** reports `{"status":"degraded","session_counters":false}` when `session_counters.db` couldn't be opened. It stays 200,
  since everything but session numbering works and clients treat a failed `/health` as down. The bind-failure item was fixed earlier the
  same day with TD-551.

Live tests: `BodiesWithWhitespaceAreParsed`, `EscapesInBodiesAreDecoded`, `SessionKeysCantCollideThroughAPipe` and
`ReportsTheSessionCounterStore` all fail against the old server; the whole live suite passes (101 tests).

**Still open:**
- claim leases or a stale-claim report;
- running fetch downloads off httplib's request pool;
- capping upload size (the body is still held in memory unbounded);
- the narrow stop-before-`listen()` window.

**Rest of the fix (October 25, 2026).** These follow the owner's choices.
- **Claim leases.**
  - **Server:** each claim records `claimed_unix` (a new 11th column of the pending file, `PendingEntry::claimed_unix`; older files
    and older binaries ignore it). `handle_acquire()` lets another run take an entry whose claim is older than the lease (logged).
    `POST …/renew {"run_id"}` restarts a run's leases and answers `{"renewed":N}`. Acquire responses (both shapes) carry
    `claim_lease_seconds`, release clears the claim time, and the queue shows it.
  - **Setting:** `REGISTRY_CLAIM_LEASE_MINUTES` / `--claim-lease-minutes`, default 30; 0 turns leases off.
  - **Upgrade safety:** a claim with no recorded time has its lease counted from server start, so upgrading releases nothing at once.
  - **Client:** `RemoteTransport` reads the lease and implements `renew_claims()`. `DatasetRegistry::acquire_pending()` starts a
    background renewer that calls it every third of the lease (at least every 5 s), and `mark_trained()`, `release_pending()` and the
    destructor stop it. Every trainer acquire site (`train`, `retrain`, `resume` and so every `trainer_service` pass, LeJEPA) is covered
    without changes. If the claims are gone (renewed 0), it logs an error once.
  - **Result:** a crashed trainer's files return to the pool after the lease, which also helps TD-415's LeJEPA run IDs. A late report
    from the old run is rejected by TD-493's claim check.
- **Fetch concurrency:** at most `REGISTRY_MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES` / `--max-concurrent-fetches` (default 2) Gutenberg/HuggingFace
  fetches run at once (`with_fetch_slot()`). Others get 429 with `Retry-After: 30`, leaving the request threads for
  `acquire`/`trained`.
- **Upload size:** `REGISTRY_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` / `--max-upload-mb` (default 2048) sets httplib's payload limit; larger bodies get 413.

Tests:
- `registry_server_args_test.cpp`: defaults, file, CLI precedence and clamping.
- `DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`: the renewer renews during a pass and stops after `mark_trained()`, and stays off without a lease.
- Live:
  - `AcquireReportsTheClaimLease`
  - `ExpiredClaimIsTakenByAnotherRun`: a backdated claim is taken; the old run renews 0 and records nothing.
  - `RenewKeepsAClaim`
  - `ClaimWithoutATimeIsNotReleasedAtOnce`
  - `RemoteTransportReadsTheLeaseAndRenews`
  - The first three fail against the old server.
- TD-491's concurrent-fetch test now retries 429s, as clients should; the server log shows the cap refusing extra fetches.
- The whole live suite passes (106 tests). A server with `--max-upload-mb 1` answered a 2 MiB upload 413 (not stored) and a 1 KB one
  200.

**Still open:** the narrow window where a stop arriving just before `listen()` is lost.

  is also added to responses cut off at `max_response_length`) receive advantage-weighted gradient, and with TD-361 the first row trains "BOS after BOS".
  Re-tokenizing decoded text can also differ from the sampled IDs (TD-224).

- **No KL penalty** against a frozen reference (SFT) policy, the standard RLHF guard against reward hacking and drift; with TD-482's ratio ≡ 1 there is
  no step-size control at all.
- **One optimizer step per prompt** (`apply_policy_gradient()` steps inside the per-prompt loop), so updates are single-sample REINFORCE; rewards
  aren't normalized across the batch (TD-481 normalizes within a response instead).

  scoring and two forwards.
- `set_training(true)` is left on after the update; TD-341's gates aren't optimizer parameters, so they don't learn here either.

- [ ] Accumulate gradients over the batch and step once; normalize rewards/advantages across the batch (with TD-481).
- [ ] Derive value states from one encoder/decoder pass; restore the previous training mode.

### TD-502: SIGReg's Fixed Sketch Directions Leave Most Dimensions Unregularized

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 20, 2026 | World Model / SIGReg | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `SIGReg.cpp` (see [SIGReg.md](../reference/source/SIGReg.md)); verified. The `num_sketches` projection directions are drawn
once in the constructor (`std::random_device` seed) and reused for every call, so the loss only constrains their K-dimensional span: 64 of 768 dimensions
at the shipped `WORLD_MODEL_SIGREG_NUM_SKETCHES=64`. A 256-row Gaussian batch and the same batch projected onto that span (collapsed in 704 of 768
dimensions) gave identical loss (0.00265) and variance mean (1.004); through a fresh set of directions the collapsed batch showed variance 0.086 and loss
0.245. Within a pass, LeJEPA's encoder can collapse outside the sketched subspace with no penalty and nothing in the logged metrics. New directions each
process partly mask this across `trainer_service` passes but make runs irreproducible.

Action Items:

- [x] Resample the directions on every `compute_loss()`/`backward()` pair (share one draw between the two within a step), from a seedable RNG.
- [x] Add a test that a subspace-collapsed batch is penalized.

Location in code: `src/SIGReg.cpp` (constructor), `src/SIGReg.hpp` (`directions_`); tagged `TODO: See TD-502`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SIGReg.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp`
- `tests/sigreg_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Per-step directions:** `SIGReg::resample_directions()` draws new unit directions, and `LeJEPAEncoder::train_step()` calls it
  once per step. That step's `compute_loss()`, `compute_variance_stats()` and `backward()` then share the draw.
- **Seeding:** the RNG is a member `std::mt19937`, seeded from `std::random_device` at construction. `set_seed()` reseeds it and
  redraws, for reproducible runs and tests. `get_directions()` exposes the current draw.

Tests (`sigreg_test.cpp`):
- `RedrawnDirectionsPenalizeCollapseOutsideOneDrawsSpan`: a 512-row Gaussian batch projected onto one draw's 8-direction span
  (collapsed in 56 of 64 dimensions) scores the same as the full batch under that draw. Over 20 redraws it averages above 0.05,
  more than 10× the Gaussian batch.
- `SetSeedMakesTheDirectionsReproducible`.

### TD-503: SIGReg Loss Has a Sequence-Length-Dependent Floor

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 20, 2026 | World Model / SIGReg | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `SIGReg.cpp`; verified. The squared characteristic-function gap is a biased estimator with an expected floor ∝ 1/n, and
`LeJEPAEncoder::train_step()` applies SIGReg to one text's token embeddings (n = token count). A true N(0, I) set scores 0.0785 at n = 8, 0.0331 at 20,
0.0225 at 32, 0.0057 at 128 and 0.0003 at 2,048; fully collapsed is 0.343. Short texts are pushed away from a target they already meet (the small-n
minimizer isn't Gaussian), and the logged `sigreg_loss` mostly reflects text length, so it can't be compared across datasets or over training. (The paper
applies SIGReg across a batch of samples; per-sequence application is a deliberate deviation that makes the bias matter.)

Action Items:

- [x] Use the unbiased estimator of |φ̂(t) − φ(t)|² (remove the (1 − |φ̂|²)/n-style self-term), or scale and document the n-dependence.
- [x] Consider applying SIGReg across a batch of sequences' pooled embeddings, as the paper does.

Location in code: `src/SIGReg.cpp` (`compute_loss()`, `backward()`), `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp` (`train_step()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-503`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SIGReg.cpp`
- `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp`
- `tests/sigreg_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Unbiased estimator:** `compute_loss()` adds the bias correction `(|φ̂|² − 1)/(n − 1)` to each squared gap, which replaces
  `|φ̂|²` with its unbiased U-statistic `(n|φ̂|² − 1)/(n − 1)`, and `backward()` is its exact gradient. Its expectation is 0 for an
  N(0, I) sample of any size, so a single value can be slightly negative. Fewer than two rows return 0, with a zero gradient.
- **Measured on the real class:** mean over 300 N(0, I) samples with fresh directions:

  | n | Old | New |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8 | 0.0865 | 0.0019 |
  | 32 | 0.0211 | 0.0002 |
  | 128 | 0.0054 | 0.0001 |

  A collapsed batch still scores above 0.2 at n = 8.
- **Metrics ingest:** `metrics_api_server` recorded LeJEPA epoch metrics only when `sigreg_loss >= 0`, which would have dropped
  real epochs. It now gates on `predictor_loss` alone; the two always arrive together.

Tests:
- `sigreg_test.cpp`: `UnbiasedLossDoesNotDependOnSequenceLength` and `FewerThanTwoRowsScoreZeroWithZeroGradient`.
  `LossNearZeroForIsotropicGaussianBatch` now allows small negative values. The existing finite-difference gradient check passes
  against the new gradient.
- `training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`: `NegativeSigregLossIsStillRecorded`.

**Batch application (October 20–21, 2026, the second action item, requested by the owner).**
- **`LeJEPAEncoder::train_batch(texts)`:**
  - Phase 1 encodes every text's target view and mean-pools it to one row per text, then takes SIGReg's loss and gradient over
    that `[batch, d_model]` matrix.
  - Phase 2 trains each text as `train_step()` does. Its pooled row's SIGReg gradient, scaled by `sigreg_lambda` and the batch
    size, is spread evenly over its tokens.
  - The batch-size factor keeps the paper's balance: in the batch objective each sample gets `(1/B)·∂predictor_b + λ·∂SIGReg/∂pooled_b`
    in one step, but here each text takes its own step with its full predictor gradient. Unscaled, the SIGReg term was B times
    weaker: at λ = 3 it barely held the embeddings.
  - Texts that fail to tokenize or give fewer than 2 tokens are skipped rather than failing the batch, and a batch with fewer
    than 2 usable texts contributes no SIGReg.
- **`train_step(text)`:** unchanged, the per-sequence form. Both share a private `train_tokens()`.
- **The pass:** `incremental_trainer --objective=lejepa` trains in batches of the new `WORLD_MODEL_SIGREG_BATCH_SIZE` (default 32,
  2–4096; `config.trainer.conf`). It still pushes per-sample predictor-loss metrics and checks auto-save per sample, and the
  batch SIGReg loss and diagnostics count once per trained text in the epoch averages.

Tests (`lejepaencoder_test.cpp`):
- `TrainBatchSkipsUnusableTextsAndReportsTheTrainedOnes` and `TrainBatchOfOneHasNoSigregLoss`.
- `TrainBatchSigregPullsPooledEmbeddingsTowardGaussian`: two encoders from the same weights, 30 batches of 16 texts, λ = 1 vs
  λ = 0. The pooled embeddings' gap from N(0, I) ended at 0.25–0.36 with SIGReg against 0.56–0.59 without, from a 0.27–0.31 start.
- The config key's parsing, env override and validation are tested in `config_test.cpp`.
