### TD-506: CPU Chat Generation Is Off by One Because `model_fn` Uses the Training Forward

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| HIGH | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Inference / Serving / API | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `SpeculativeDecoding.hpp` (see [SpeculativeDecoding.md](../reference/source/SpeculativeDecoding.md)); verified.
`EncoderDecoderModel::forward(input, targets)` is the training forward: it feeds `[BOS] + targets[:-1]` to the decoder, so its last logits row predicts
`targets.back()`, the last token already in the context. `TextGenerator` (and `SpeculativeDecoder`) read the last row as the next-token prediction.
`ChatbotAPI` builds every CPU generation `model_fn` as `model_->forward(input_tokens, decoder_tokens)`: the plain path (the default on a server without a
GPU), speculative decoding, `--batched-inference` and `/chat/batch`.

Reproduced with a tiny `EncoderDecoderModel` trained on the CPU (`forward()`, loss ≈ 0) to echo 12 five-token sequences: greedy generation through
`ChatbotAPI`'s `model_fn` got **0/12** exactly right (`2 2 15 24 31 30 26 3` for `15 31 24 30 4`); with an aligned `model_fn` (decoder input =
the generated tokens) **12/12**; speculative decoding likewise 0/12 vs 12/12. So a correctly trained model answers wrongly on a CPU
`chatbot_api_server`. The GPU path, `generate_response()`'s cached path, and the RAG, pipeline and integrated engines are aligned and unaffected.

Action Items:

- [x] Add an inference forward that takes the decoder input directly (e.g. `forward_decoder(input_tokens, decoder_input)`) and use it in all four `ChatbotAPI` `model_fn`s.
- [x] Add a regression test: a model trained on an echo task must generate it exactly through `ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` on the CPU.
- [x] Have that forward project only the last decoder row (TD-424's `ChatbotAPI` part; `EncoderDecoderModel`'s beam callbacks already do, October 26, 2026).

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `EncoderDecoderModel::next_token_logits(input_tokens, decoder_tokens)` is the inference forward. Its decoder
input is the generated sequence as given: `TextGenerator` starts it with BOS, and a BOS is put in front when it is missing (as from
`SpeculativeDecoder`'s empty context). It returns the logits of the last decoder row only. It shares `run_decoder()` with `forward()`:
the encoder (tail-truncated, TD-365), world-model and hippocampal reads are the same, and nothing is committed to the hippocampal memory.
All four `ChatbotAPI` CPU callbacks use it: plain, speculative (draft and target), batched and `/chat/batch`. `forward()` keeps the
training shift and the full projection.

Tests (`ChatbotAPIEchoTest`): the fixture trains a tiny model on the CPU to echo four phrases (mean loss below 0.01; a fresh model is
tried when an unseeded run doesn't converge, TD-368). Then every path must reproduce each phrase exactly:
- `PlainCpuGenerationEchoesExactly` (greedy) and `PlainCpuBeamSearchEchoesExactly`;
- `BatchEndpointEchoesExactly` (`generate_batch_responses()`);
- `SpeculativeDecodingEchoesExactly` (the model as its own draft);
- `BatchedInferenceEchoesExactly` (temperature 0, TD-214).

With the old callbacks, the four plain, beam and batch tests fail with every token doubled: "hheelloo w wororlldd" for "hello world".
`NextTokenLogitsIsTheLastRowOfTheAlignedForward` checks the logits against the training forward's last row (within 1e-4) and checks that
a missing BOS is added.

Not changed: these CPU paths still re-run the encoder every step with no KV cache, don't commit hippocampal steps, and don't cap
generation at `max_seq_length` the way `generate_response_with_strategy()` does (TD-347). That is part of TD-362's CPU/GPU differences.
(TD-362, October 26, 2026: the plain CPU path now uses `generate_response_with_strategy()`; the speculative, batched and `/chat/batch`
paths still use `next_token_logits()`.)

### TD-507: Speculative Decoding Isn't Target-Distributed, Greedy or Faster

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Inference / SpeculativeDecoding | October 17, 2026 | 4-8 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`; verified with toy fixed-distribution `TextGenerator`s:
- **Wrong residual:** on rejection it samples from `max(0, p_target − p_draft)` with `p_draft` non-zero only for the rejected token. With target
  (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) and draft (0.2, 0.3, 0.5), 40,000 first tokens were (0.40, 0.40, 0.20), not the target distribution the header promises.
- **Greedy isn't greedy:** acceptance stays random (`p_t/p_d`), so 41% of "greedy" first tokens were the draft's argmax rather than the target's.
- **Never faster:** each candidate gets its own target `get_next_token_probs()` call (no parallel verification, no bonus token): 41 tokens took 41 target
  passes plus draft passes; `generate_tokens(…, 40)` returned 41 tokens. `chatbot_api_server` builds the draft with the target's own architecture, so
  even a correct algorithm couldn't save time.
- **By inspection:** candidates are sampled from the temperature-scaled draft distribution but accepted with unscaled draft/target probabilities.

Action Items:

- [x] Verify all K candidates in one target forward (logits for every position), use the full draft distribution in the residual `max(0, p − q)`, sample a bonus token when all K are accepted, and cap output at `max_new_tokens`.
- [x] Greedy mode: accept iff the candidate equals the target argmax.
- [x] Apply temperature consistently to both distributions; allow a smaller draft architecture (`DRAFT_*` config) in `chatbot_api_server`. (The draft's architecture comes from its own checkpoint instead of `DRAFT_*` keys.)
- [x] Test the output distribution and greedy equivalence.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `SpeculativeDecoder` (`SpeculativeDecoding.hpp` 2.0.0) is rewritten as standard speculative sampling.
Each round works as follows:
1. The draft samples up to K tokens from q = softmax(draft logits / T).
2. One target pass over the context plus the proposals gives K + 1 rows (`TextGenerator::get_logits()`).
3. Each proposal is accepted with probability min(1, p/q), where p = softmax(target logits / T), the same temperature for both models.
4. The first rejection is replaced by a sample from norm(max(0, p − q)), using the whole draft distribution.
5. When all K are accepted, a bonus token is sampled from the target's next row.

Greedy mode (`use_greedy`, or T ≤ 0 as in TD-515) accepts a proposal only when it is the target's argmax, so the output equals the
target's greedy output. A round never drafts more than the remaining budget, and the output is cut at `max_new_tokens`. A target that
returns only its last row still works: the decoder calls it once per prefix it needs and remembers the mode.

Model side:
- `EncoderDecoderModel::next_token_logits(…, last_rows)` returns the last K + 1 rows, and `ChatbotAPI`'s target callback asks for
  them.
- `chatbot_api_server` builds the draft from `EncoderDecoderModel::read_checkpoint_architecture(DRAFT_MODEL_PATH)`. The draft can now
  be smaller than the target, but its vocabulary must match the tokenizer's. `num_candidates < 1` throws.

Measured on the old code with the same mocks:
- first-token distribution (0.391, 0.411, 0.197) instead of (0.5, 0.3, 0.2);
- (0.396, 0.341, 0.264) at T = 0.5 instead of (0.658, 0.237, 0.105);
- greedy output equal to the target's greedy output in 0 of 10 runs;
- 20 target calls for 20 tokens.

New tests (`SpeculativeDecodingTD507Test`):
- `FirstTokenFollowsTheTargetDistribution` and `TemperatureAppliesToBothModels` (20,000 draws each, within 0.015);
- `GreedyOutputEqualsTheTargetsGreedyOutput` (10 draft/target pairs);
- `OneTargetPassPerRoundAndABonusToken`: 4 target passes for 20 tokens at K = 4;
- `OutputNeverExceedsMaxNewTokens`;
- `LastRowOnlyTargetGivesTheSameGreedyOutput`.

Supporting tests:
- `ChatbotAPIEchoTest.NextTokenLogitsLastRowsMatchTheAlignedForward`;
- `EncoderDecoderModelTest.ReadCheckpointArchitectureMatchesTheSavedModel`;
- `ChatbotAPIEchoTest.SpeculativeDecodingEchoesExactly`, which now uses the one-pass target.

Location in code: `src/SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`, `src/TextGenerator.{hpp,cpp}` (`get_logits()`), `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`
(`next_token_logits()` `last_rows`, `read_checkpoint_architecture()`), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`, `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`
- `tests/speculativedecoding_test.cpp`

### TD-508: Speculative Decoding Speedup Statistic and Hygiene

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | Inference / SpeculativeDecoding | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`: `get_speedup()`/`calculate_theoretical_speedup()` return `K·α/(K+1)`, which is below 1 for every
acceptance rate (verified: 0.6 at 80% acceptance, 0.8 at 100%) and isn't a speedup (expected tokens per target pass is `(1 − α^(K+1))/(1 − α)`, before
costs); the tests assert this formula and the replaced doc promised "2–3×". By inspection: `acceptance_threshold` is never read; `print_stats()`/
`print_speedup_table()` use `std::cout`; `generate()` uses `goto`; the RNG is unseeded (TD-368's class).

Action Items:

- [x] Report tokens per target pass (and measured time if available) instead; update the tests.
- [x] Remove or implement `acceptance_threshold`; route output through `Logger`; seedable RNG.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-507).**
- **Statistics.** `get_speedup()` is replaced by `get_tokens_per_target_pass()`, with pass and token counters
  (`get_target_passes()`, `get_draft_passes()`, `get_generated_tokens()`). `calculate_theoretical_speedup()` is replaced by
  `expected_tokens_per_target_pass(K, α)` = (1 − α^(K+1))/(1 − α), which is K + 1 at α = 1. Timing isn't measured, since it depends
  on the draft-to-target cost ratio.
- **Removed:** `acceptance_threshold`, `print_speedup_table()` and the `goto`.
- **Output.** `print_stats()` is now `log_stats()`, through `Logger`.
- **RNG.** The constructor takes a seed (default `std::random_device`).
- **Tests.** The speedup tests became `ExpectedTokensPerTargetPassTest`, and `SpeculativeDecodingTD508Test.SameSeedSameOutput` is new.

Location in code: `src/SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`.

### TD-509: `SQLiteMetricsDatabase::get_session()` Blocks WAL Checkpoints

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / SQLite Database | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp` (see [SQLiteMetricsDatabase.md](../reference/source/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.md)); verified.
`get_session()` steps its prepared statement and returns on `SQLITE_ROW` without `sqlite3_reset()`, so the statement keeps a read snapshot open until
the next `get_session()` call. In WAL mode that stops checkpoints: 20,000 `insert_metrics_record()` calls after one found `get_session()` left a
**254 MB WAL and a 4 KB main database** (all data only in the WAL), against a 4 MB WAL and 2.1 MB database without it. In production,
`TrainingMetricsService::restore_from_summary()` calls it at service construction; for an existing key (`0-default` after a restart, or a trainer
re-registering after a `metrics_api_server` restart mid-pass) the snapshot stays open until a service with a new key is constructed, while every write
(including one gradient-variance row per optimizer step) grows the WAL.

Action Items:

- [x] `sqlite3_reset()` the statement after copying the row (and on every return path), e.g. with a scope guard.
- [x] Test that the WAL stays bounded after a found `get_session()`.

Location in code: `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp` (`get_session()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-509`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`
- `tests/MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** `get_session()` resets its prepared statement on every return path with a scope guard, so a found row no
longer holds a read snapshot. Test `FoundGetSessionDoesNotBlockWalCheckpoints` (`MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`): a found `get_session()`,
then 4,000 inserts of a few KB each. The WAL stays under 16 MB and the rows reach the main database. With the old code the WAL grew to
86 MB.

### TD-511: `SQLiteMetricsDatabase` Busy Timeout, Transactions and Setup Gaps

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / SQLite Database | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`:
- **No busy timeout (verified):** with another connection holding a write transaction, an insert threw `database is locked` after 0.3 ms; callers log
  and drop the row (as TD-304 for `DaemonConfigStore`).
- **Missing directory (verified):** the default `training_sessions/metrics.db` fails to open (`unable to open database file`) if the directory doesn't
  exist.
- **By inspection:** every write is its own autocommit transaction (many tiny transactions for per-step rows); `PRAGMA` and `ALTER TABLE` migration
  errors are ignored; `schema_version` is written but never read.

Action Items:

- [x] `sqlite3_busy_timeout()` (a few seconds); create the parent directory; check PRAGMA/migration results.
- [x] Batch per-step inserts in transactions; use or drop `schema_version`.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Opening the database.** The constructor creates the parent directory and sets a 5 s busy timeout. A failed `PRAGMA` is logged.
  WAL is a performance setting, so a missing WAL isn't fatal.
- **Migrations.** These are now table-driven, through one `has_column()` probe instead of four copy-pasted blocks. A failed
  `ALTER TABLE` throws and names the statement, where it used to be ignored and left a store missing columns.
- **`schema_version`.** It was dropped, since it was written but never read and the column probes are what decide. Existing
  databases keep the table.
- **Batching.** One autocommit per row measured 316 µs against 4.7 µs batched (WAL, `synchronous=NORMAL`). `IMetricsDatabase` gained
  `insert_metrics_records()` and `insert_gradient_variance_samples()`, one transaction each, all or nothing, and both throw when not
  stored. Both backends implement them. `TrainingMetricsService` writes each persist's history rows as one batch (TD-529's marker
  moves only on success). It buffers the per-step gradient-variance rows and writes them at each persist or every 256 rows. Past
  100,000 pending rows while the DB is down, the oldest are dropped.
- **Flushing.** Buffered rows are flushed before a session is archived and before `set_database()` switches keys, so they never land
  under a key without a session row.

Tests:
- SQLite (`MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`): `CreatesMissingParentDirectory`, `WriteWaitsForAnotherConnectionsTransaction` (another
  connection holds a write for 300 ms), `BatchInsertsAreAllOrNothing` (a trigger rejects one row and the whole batch rolls back),
  `ServiceBatchesGradientVarianceRows`, `NewDatabaseHasNoUnusedSchemaVersionTable`, `FailedMigrationFailsTheOpen`.
- Postgres, live: `BatchInsertsAreAllOrNothing`.

Five of the SQLite tests failed against the old behavior: unable to open, `database is locked`, a partly stored batch, a
`schema_version` table, and an open that succeeded silently with a column missing. `SchemaBootstrap` no longer expects
`schema_version`. The failing-DB test (TD-529) now fails the batch method.

Location in code: `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp` (constructor, `bootstrap_schema()`, insert methods); tagged `TODO: See TD-511`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`

### TD-512: Startup Sweep Deletes Every Download Because the Pending List Is Never Loaded

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| HIGH | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / StartupSweep | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `StartupSweep.hpp` (see [StartupSweep.md](../reference/source/StartupSweep.md)); verified with the real classes.
`startup_sweep()` classifies `DOWNLOAD_DIR` files against `reg.pending_files()`, which returns `DatasetRegistry`'s in-memory `pending_` filled only by
`load_pending_list()`. All three call sites in `IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`train`, `retrain`, `--objective=lejepa`) construct a fresh
`DatasetRegistry`, call **only `load_registry()`**, then sweep. Reproducing that sequence with two queued files (one partially, one fully downloaded) and
an operator's `notes.txt` in `downloads/`: the sweep saw 0 pending files and deleted all three as "orphaned" (condition G); with `load_pending_list()`
both downloads were kept. So conditions A/B/C never run: every pass deletes every completed and partial download (re-downloaded in full; resume never
happens) and anything else in `DOWNLOAD_DIR`. By inspection, a registry that can't be reached gives the same empty state and the same wipe. The tests
populate the pending list on the instance they sweep, so they pass.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `startup_sweep()` now loads the pending list and the trained registry itself.
- **Pending list can't be loaded** (unreachable registry, or no pending list yet): it skips the sweep entirely, because without that list every
  file would look orphaned.
- **Trained registry can't be loaded:** it continues with an empty trained set, so nothing is deleted as already trained on missing information.

The `resume` command (every `trainer_service` pass, which downloads since TD-411) now runs the sweep too. New tests:
- `FreshRegistryKeepsQueuedDownloads`: production's call sequence, with a partial and a complete queued download kept;
- `UnreadablePendingListDeletesNothing`.

Both fail with the old sweep. The condition D/G tests now create an empty pending list, so "nothing pending" is actually known.

- [x] Call `reg.load_pending_list()` before `startup_sweep()` at all three call sites (or have `startup_sweep()` load it).
- [x] Skip all deletion when either load fails. (Skipped entirely when the pending list fails; a failed trained-registry load only disables condition D.)
- [x] Add a test that sweeps a freshly constructed registry, as production does.

Location in code: `src/StartupSweep.hpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (call sites, plus the new one in `resume`); the `TODO: See TD-512` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `src/StartupSweep.hpp`
- `tests/StartupSweepTests.cpp`

the caller then takes the argmax (`generate()`, `generate_sampling()`). `generate_top_k()` and `generate_nucleus()` sample instead, at an effective

- `generate_sampling()` and `generate()` treat a negative temperature like 0 (they used to test `== 0` and sample a negative temperature at 1).

### TD-516: `TextGenerator` Ignored `min_length`/`early_stopping`, Silent NaN Output and Config Semantics

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 26, 2026 | NLP / TextGenerator | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TextGenerator.{hpp,cpp}`:
- **Verified:** `min_length` is never read (with `min_length = 4` and an EOS-preferring model, greedy and `generate()` stopped after one token: an empty
  response); all-NaN logits pick token 0 (PAD, a stop token), so a broken model (e.g. TD-423) silently returns an empty response
  (`std::discrete_distribution` over NaN is also undefined); `max_length` counts the starting BOS and prompt (`max_length = 6` → 5 new tokens).
- **By inspection:** `early_stopping` has no effect (both branches break only when no beams remain) and beam search never stops once the best finished
  beam is unbeatable; the repetition penalty runs after top-k/top-p, so penalized tokens stay in the nucleus; `top_p <= 0` disables filtering; beam search
  calls the model once per beam per step; seed 0 means random.

Action Items:

- [x] Implement `min_length` (mask EOS/PAD until reached) and real early stopping, or remove both fields. (Owner chose to implement both, October 26, 2026.)
- [x] Detect non-finite logits and report an error; define `max_length` as new tokens; apply the penalty before filtering; treat `top_p <= 0` as top-1. (Owner chose new tokens.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** Every strategy now takes its next-token logits from one helper, `next_logits()`.
- **Non-finite logits.** A NaN or +inf logit, or a row with no finite value, throws `std::runtime_error`. A broken model no longer
  silently returns an empty response.
- **`min_length`.** EOS and PAD are masked to −inf until `min_length` new tokens exist. This applies in greedy, sampling, top-k,
  nucleus, `generate()` and beam search.
- **`max_length` counts new tokens.** The BOS and prompt are no longer counted, so `max_length = 6` gives up to 6 new tokens, not 5.
  `ChatbotAPI`'s and `MAX_GEN_LENGTH`'s "maximum response tokens" now mean what they say. `EncoderDecoderModel`'s TD-347 cap
  (`capped_generation_length()`) becomes `max_seq_length − 1` new tokens, so the sequence with BOS still fits in `max_seq_length`.
- **Early stopping.** With `early_stopping` (the default), beam search stops once no running beam can still win. A running beam's
  raw score can only fall, since log-probabilities are clamped at 0. Its best possible final score is therefore its current score
  divided by the largest length penalty it can still get (the current or the final length, whichever penalty is larger). When the
  best finished beam is at least that for every running beam, the search ends. The result is identical to the full search.
- **Filter order.** The repetition penalty runs before temperature and the top-k/top-p filters, in every strategy. Temperature
  commutes with the penalty, since the penalty keeps each logit's sign.
- **`top_p <= 0`** keeps only the top token (top-1).

Not changed (by inspection, LOW):
- beam search still calls the model once per beam per step;
- seed 0 still means a random seed.

Tests (`TextGeneratorTD516Test`, all failing on the old code):
- `MinLengthKeepsStopTokensOutUntilReached`: five strategies, with an EOS-preferring model;

### TD-517: Token Embeddings Aren't Scaled by sqrt(d_model), So Position Swamps Content

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| HIGH | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 | Layers / TokenEmbedding | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TokenEmbedding.cpp` (see [TokenEmbedding.md](../reference/source/TokenEmbedding.md)); verified with the real `TokenEmbedding`
and `PositionalEncoding`. Embeddings are initialized N(0, 1/d_model), so each row has norm ≈ 1 (0.97 measured at `d_model = 768`), while each
sinusoidal positional row has norm √(d_model/2) (19.6 measured). `LLMEncoder`, `LLMDecoder` (full, cached and GPU paths) and `LeJEPAEncoder` add the two
directly; nothing multiplies the embedding by √d_model as the original Transformer does. At initialization, two **different** tokens at the same position
had cosine similarity **0.997**, higher than the **same** token at adjacent positions (0.973): the model input is dominated by position, and the network
must first grow every embedding row ~20×, against the global weight decay that also applies to embeddings (TD-469). Every forward path goes through
`TokenEmbedding::forward()`, so the fix can live in one place.

**Owner decision (October 17, 2026): must fix.** It changes the input scale of every checkpoint, so it lands with the planned retraining (TD-358).

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** chose the second option. The table is initialized from N(0, 1) (`TokenEmbedding::kInitStd`, used by the
constructor and `reinitialize()`), and `forward()`/`backward()` stay unscaled (the T5 convention).
- Rows now have norm ≈ 27.7 at `d_model = 768`, against 19.6 for positional rows.
- At initialization, different tokens at one position measure 0.334 cosine and the same token at adjacent positions 0.991 (before: 0.997 and 0.973).
- New test `TokenEmbeddingConstructorTest.TokenIdentityNotSwampedByPositionAtInit` fails with the old init; the variance test now expects 1.

Why not the √d_model multiply: it would change what every saved table means. Old checkpoints would load silently rescaled (hence the version bump
this entry proposed), and SafeTensors exports would stop matching T5 (TD-466). With the init change, saved files and their meaning are unchanged, so
no format bump is needed: pre-fix checkpoints behave exactly as before and are retired by the TD-358 retraining.

TD-371 revisited: with token rows around norm 34 after adding position (they were about 20), the residual stream starts larger. Each Pre-LN
sublayer reads a normalized input, so its output is relatively smaller against that stream, which moves away from the residual-growth risk rather
than towards it. No residual scaling is added in this change; TD-371 stays an owner decision, best judged from the first retraining's per-layer
residual norms. TD-469 (weight decay on embeddings) applies proportionally at either scale and stays separate.

Action Items:

- [x] Scale the embedding output by √d_model in `TokenEmbedding::forward()` (and the gradient by the same factor in `backward()`), or equivalently initialize with standard deviation 1 and keep the lookup unscaled; pick one and document it.
- [x] ~~Bump the checkpoint format/version so pre-fix checkpoints aren't silently loaded with the new scaling (they need retraining anyway, TD-358).~~ Not needed with the init-based fix: loading isn't rescaled.
- [x] Add a test that token identity isn't swamped at initialization (e.g. cross-token cosine at one position well below same-token adjacent-position cosine).
- [x] Revisit TD-371 (residual-branch scaling) in the same change. Revisited; no change, see above.

Location in code: `src/TokenEmbedding.cpp` (constructor and `reinitialize()`), `src/TokenEmbedding.hpp` (`kInitStd`); the `TODO: See TD-517` tags are now `TD-517:` fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TokenEmbedding.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ModelSerializer.cpp` (format version)
- `tests/tokenembedding_test.cpp`

### TD-519: Trainer Admin PUT Reads a Spaced `true` as False and Disables Auto-Save

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Training / Admin API | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerAdminAPI.cpp` (see [TrainerAdminAPI.md](../reference/source/TrainerAdminAPI.md)); verified against the real server.
`json_bool()` compares the four characters immediately after `"auto_save_enabled":` with `true`, so a space after the colon reads as false.
`PUT /admin/config {"auto_save_enabled": true}` (Python `json.dumps`' default formatting, and common in hand-typed `curl` bodies) answered
`"auto_save_enabled":false` and persisted that to `daemon_config.db`, so every later pass runs without auto-save; the compact form works.
`TrainerServiceProxy::handle_put_config_idle()` copies the same helper, so the request has the same effect when no child is running. (The integer keys
work: `stoi` skips leading whitespace. The Android dashboard sends compact JSON.)

Action Items:

- [x] Parse request bodies with the vendored `nlohmann/json` (with TD-453), rejecting non-boolean values with 400.
- [x] Test whitespace and pretty-printed bodies, in both handlers.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** Both handlers now call one shared parser, `parse_trainer_admin_config()` (`src/TrainerAdminConfig.{hpp,cpp}`, in
`adai_core`), which reads the body with the vendored `nlohmann/json`.
- Any valid JSON spacing works. `auto_save_enabled` must be a JSON boolean, and the three counts must be integers in range.
- These are rejected with 400: malformed JSON, a body that isn't an object, the immutable keys, and a body with no mutable key.
- The whole body is validated before anything is applied or persisted, which also fixes TD-305's validate-first half for this endpoint.
- The old substring helpers (`json_int()`, `json_bool()`, `json_has_key()`) are removed from both files.

Verified:
- **Against the old handlers:** the new HTTP tests failed in both suites.
  - The live API with `"auto_save_enabled": true` left auto-save off.
  - A body rejected on its third key had already applied the first two.
  - The idle proxy wrote `false` for a spaced `true`.
- **With the fix:** they pass, along with `TrainerAdminConfigTests` (3 cases), `TrainerAdminAPITests` (16) and `TrainerServiceProxyTests` (18).

Location in code: `src/TrainerAdminAPI.cpp` (`json_bool()`, `handle_put_config()`), `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp` (`json_bool()`, `handle_put_config_idle()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-519`.

### TD-523: `trainer_service` Can't Tell a Failing Pass From an Idle One

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerServiceMain.cpp` (see [TrainerServiceMain.md](../reference/source/TrainerServiceMain.md)); verified with the real binary and a
stub `incremental_trainer` that printed an error and exited 1. The supervisor treats exit 0 as "did work" and every other code as "nothing to do",
counting only codes other than 0/1 as crashes. `incremental_trainer resume` returns 1 when `resume_last_session()` returns false, which covers an empty
queue **and** a missing checkpoint, a failed `load_model()` and a failed `train_on_files()`. With the stub, `/admin/status` showed `"phase":"idle"`,
`"total_passes_crashed":0`, `"last_exit_code":1` (identical to a healthy idle service) and nothing reached `trainer_service`'s log. A corrupt checkpoint
or unreadable dataset therefore becomes a silent retry every 45 s: each attempt claims the pending files, fails and releases them (TD-333 leaves segments
stuck), indefinitely, while the dashboard shows an idle trainer.

Action Items:

- [x] Give `resume` distinct exit codes (e.g. 0 did work, 3 nothing pending, 1 failed) and have the supervisor count failures separately, log them, expose a `total_passes_failed`/`last_failure` field in `/admin/status`, and back off on consecutive failures.
- [x] Test the supervisor's handling of each exit code with a stub child.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Distinct results:** `IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()` now returns `ResumeResult::Trained`, `NothingPending` or `Failed`.
  `resume` exits 0, 3 or 1 to match (`kResumeExit*` in `IncrementalTrainerArgs.hpp`).
- **Unreachable registry:** an unreachable registry (or a local lock failure) now sets a new `AcquireResponse::failed` flag. So a registry
  outage is a failure, not "nothing pending".
- **Supervisor:** `trainer_service` classifies each exit with `classify_pass_exit()`:
  - 0 trained; 3 idle; 128 and up crashed (a signal death);
  - anything else failed, including 127 for an exec failure.
- **On a failure or crash** it:
  - logs an error with the exit code;
  - counts it;
  - waits `failure_backoff_seconds()`: the 45 s poll interval, doubled for each consecutive failure up to 15 minutes. `POST /admin/resume`
    still wakes it at once.
- **`/admin/status`** gains `total_passes_failed`, `consecutive_failures` and `last_failure_unix`. `total_passes_crashed` now counts only
  signal deaths.

Verified:
- **Unit tests:** `ResumeReportsNothingPendingSeparatelyFromFailure` (empty local queue, then an unreachable registry), the exit-code
  classification and backoff tests.
- **Real `trainer_service` with a stub `incremental_trainer`:**
  - **exit 1:** `total_passes_failed: 1`, `consecutive_failures: 1`, `last_failure_unix` set, and a "training pass failed with exit code 1"
    error in its log;
  - **exit 3:** idle, with no failure recorded.

Location in code: `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp` (exit-code handling), `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`resume`'s `return 1`); tagged `TODO: See TD-523`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `src/TrainerServiceControlState.hpp`
- `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp`

  `DOWNLOAD_DIR=downloads` under `WorkingDirectory=/opt/adai`), so FTP downloads would fail read-only under the shipped unit; the empty-`LOG_FILE_PATH`
  fallback log in the working directory likewise (TD-431).

Action Items:

- [ ] Exponential backoff on consecutive crashes/failures (done for failed and crashed passes with TD-523; launch failures remain); add the download directory to `ReadWritePaths` (and set `LOG_FILE_PATH` in the shipped config).

### TD-526: Metrics API Accepts Cross-Origin Writes and Reads From Any Web Page

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Metrics / API | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (see [TrainingMetricsAPI.md](../reference/source/TrainingMetricsAPI.md)); verified against the real
`metrics_api_server`. A post-routing handler adds `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` to every response, there is no authentication, and push/control
routes parse any body regardless of `Content-Type`. A `POST` with `Content-Type: text/plain` is a CORS simple request that browsers send without a
preflight. With `Origin: http://evil.example`: `POST /api/sessions/{key}/control/clear` → 200 "Metrics history cleared"; `POST …/metrics/sample`
`{"sample":5,"loss":99.0}` → 200, recorded. Any web page opened in a browser on the LAN (or by a Cloudflare-Access-authenticated operator for
`metrics.kerfbit.dev`) can therefore clear histories, inject fake metrics or end sessions (`PUT /admin/config` needs a preflight and is blocked), and, because the wildcard
origin permits reading responses, read every endpoint, including `metrics/abnormal`'s raw `input_text`/`target_text`. TRAINING_METRICS_API.md's
"add a reverse proxy" advice doesn't help against a browser already inside it.

Action Items:

- [x] Replace the wildcard with a configured allow-list of dashboard origins (or no CORS for write routes).
- [x] Reject write/control requests whose `Content-Type` isn't `application/json` (forcing a preflight); consider a shared token for writes.
- [x] Update TRAINING_METRICS_API.md's security notes; check `mns_server`/`registry_server` for the same exposure.

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (post-routing CORS handler, `OPTIONS` route, push/control routes); tagged `TODO: See TD-526`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`
- `docs/development/TRAINING_METRICS_API.md`
- `tests/training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `TrainingMetricsAPI` takes an allow-list of browser origins: `METRICS_API_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in
`config.metrics.conf` or the environment, or `--cors-allowed-origins`. **Owner decision: empty by default.** Browsers always send
`Origin` on cross-origin requests and on POSTs; the trainer, the Android app and `curl` don't, and are unaffected.
- **Writes** (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE): refused with 403 if they carry an `Origin` that isn't explicitly listed, and with 415 if their
  `Content-Type` is one a browser may send without a preflight (`text/plain`, form-encoded, multipart). This runs in a pre-routing
  handler, so no write route runs.
- **Responses:** carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` only for a listed origin. A `*` entry lets any origin read, never write.
  `Vary: Origin` is set whenever an `Origin` came in.
- **Preflights:** answered (204, methods GET/POST/PUT) only for a listed origin; otherwise 403 with no CORS headers.
- **Tizen app:** it reads with `fetch(…, {mode: 'cors'})`. If its runtime enforces CORS, its origin must be listed. Its exact `Origin`
  header can't be checked without the device.

Tests (`training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`, against the real HTTP server):
- `CrossOriginTextPlainWriteIsRefusedAndNotApplied`: the verified attack; the injected sample isn't recorded.
- `SimpleContentTypeWriteIsRefusedWithoutOrigin`
- `NonBrowserJsonWriteStillWorks`: the trainer's path.
- `DefaultGrantsNoCrossOriginReadsOrPreflights`
- `ListedOriginReadsAndWrites`
- `WildcardGrantsReadsButNotWrites`

**Same exposure elsewhere:** the other daemons send no CORS headers, so responses can't be read, but `registry_server` executed a
cross-origin `text/plain` `pending/add` (verified). Filed as TD-550.

### TD-527: `TrainingMetricsAPI` Per-Poll Logging, Parsing and Unbounded History Queries

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / API | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`:
- **Verified:** `GET /api/sessions/{key}/metrics/current` logs `[metrics/current] matched key='…' len=…` at INFO on every request (five polls, five
  lines); dashboards poll it continuously, so it crowds the log and speeds rotation (TD-430/TD-431).
- **By inspection:** pushes find keys by substring and parse with `stoi`/`stof` (malformed numbers → 400 with the bare exception text, `stof`);
  `GET …/metrics/history?max_records=N` is uncapped; history timestamps are whole seconds; `handle_session_status()` switches the stream to fixed
  precision part-way, rounding `samples_per_second` to 2 decimals; every route repeats the same try/catch boilerplate (2,760 lines, TD-039).

Action Items:

- [x] Drop the per-request log line (or make it DEBUG); cap `max_records`; emit millisecond timestamps.
- [ ] Parse bodies with `nlohmann/json` (TD-453) and return field-specific errors; factor the per-route boilerplate. (Parsing and
  errors done; the per-route try/catch boilerplate is unchanged.)

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Logging.** `metrics/current` logs at debug.
- **History.** `max_records` is capped at 10,000, the in-memory history size. Records gain `timestamp_ms`; `timestamp` keeps its
  seconds string, which the dashboards read.
- **Status.** In `handle_session_status()` only `progress_percent` is rounded to 2 decimals.
- **Push bodies.** Every push handler (session start, epoch start/end, sample, validation, best, abnormal, generation quality,
  advanced, layer gradients) reads its body through one `PushBody` helper on nlohmann/json:
  - absent fields take defaults, and `null` in a number field is NaN (TD-443);
  - a wrong type is a 400 naming the field, and invalid JSON is a 400;
  - a key inside a nested object or a string can no longer be read as a top-level field;
  - string escapes are decoded, and `config` is re-serialized, with `model_id` folded in as a JSON field.

  The two substring parsers are gone (cpp net −387 lines).

The per-route try/catch boilerplate (TD-039) is unchanged.

Tests (`training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`):
- `PushBodiesParseAsJsonWithFieldErrors`: `config` with its own `session_id` sent first; an escaped label; a string where a number
  belongs; truncated JSON; null and 1e-7 values.
- `HistoryHasMillisecondTimestampsAndCappedMaxRecords`.

Against the old code both fail: `session_id` came out 99 from inside `config`, the label was cut to `say \`, errors had no field
name, and there was no `timestamp_ms`.

### TD-528: `metrics_api_server` Stop/Start Race, Stale Help Text and Default-Session Slot

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Server CLI | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp` (see [TrainingMetricsAPIServer.md](../reference/source/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.md)); by inspection
(40 SIGTERMs sent 0–90 ms after start all exited, so the race below wasn't reproduced):
- **Stop/start race:** `TrainingMetricsAPI::stop()` returns early unless `running_` is set, which `start()` does on the server thread; a SIGTERM after the
  handlers are installed but before `start()` runs makes `stop()` a no-op and the shutdown `join()` waits for a server that then runs forever (the
  `mns_server` TD-464 race).
- **Help/banner drift:** `--help` lists `--max-disk-records` (unenforced, TD-440); both endpoint lists (help and startup banner) show the legacy flat
  routes and omit most session-scoped, compare, export, db-history, LeJEPA and admin routes.
- **Default-session slot:** the `0-default` session created at startup counts toward `max_live_sessions`, so trainers get one fewer slot than configured
  (relevant to TD-445).

Action Items:

- [x] Make `stop()` effective before `listen()` (e.g. set `running_` before spawning the thread, or have `start()` check a stop flag first).
- [x] Generate or trim the endpoint lists (point to TRAINING_METRICS_API.md). (`--max-disk-records` is enforced since TD-440's fix, October 25, 2026.)
- [x] Exempt `0-default` from the live-session cap (or stop creating it when no legacy client uses it).

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Stop/start.** `TrainingMetricsAPI::start()` binds, then calls `listen_after_bind()`. It marks itself starting before it checks a
  stop-requested flag. `stop()` sets that flag first, then waits up to 5 s for a start in progress to be listening, the point where
  httplib's `stop()` works. So whichever comes second sees the other, and a stop can no longer be lost. `metrics_api_server` doesn't
  report "failed to start" when the start gave way to a shutdown.
- **Endpoint lists.** `--help` and the startup banner share one short list of the main routes and point to TRAINING_METRICS_API.md.
- **`0-default`.** It doesn't count toward `max_live_sessions` (`counted_sessions_locked()`) and isn't an eviction candidate.

Tests:
- `TrainingMetricsAPIStartStop.StopBeforeStartIsNotLost`;
- `StopRacingStartAlwaysEndsIt`: 50 starts, each stopped at once;
- `MetricsSessionRegistry.DefaultSessionDoesNotTakeALiveSlot`.

All three fail against the old code: start() kept serving, the stop was lost on the first iteration, and `0-default` took a slot.
`NeverStartedPlaceholderIsNotEvicted` and `SessionStartReturns503WhenRegistryIsFull` had pinned `0-default` taking a slot; each now
uses a cap of 1 with one trainer session.

End to end: 30 real `metrics_api_server` starts got a SIGTERM 0–90 ms in. None hung: 15 exited 0 through the handler, and 15 were
ended by SIGTERM's default action before the handler was installed (143).

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp` (`print_usage()`, startup banner, shutdown sequence, `0-default` creation); tagged `TODO: See TD-528`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`
- `src/MetricsSessionRegistry.hpp`

### TD-529: Metrics Service Re-Inserts DB Rows When the JSONL File Can't Be Written

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Service | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingMetricsService.cpp` (see [TrainingMetricsService.md](../reference/source/TrainingMetricsService.md)); verified with
the real SQLite backend. `persist_metrics()` inserts the records after `persisted_up_to_` into the database, then opens the JSONL file; if the open fails
it logs a warning and returns **before** advancing `persisted_up_to_`, so the next persist inserts the same rows again plus the new ones. With the JSONL
path in a read-only directory, 30 samples at `persist_every_samples = 10` (3 history records) left 9 rows in `metrics_history` (1 + 2 + 3 + 3): duplicates
grow quadratically while the file is unwritable, and `db-history`, compare and export all return them. (The converse, a DB exception mid-loop advancing
the marker past rows that never reached the DB, is TD-479's drop.)

Action Items:

- [x] Track DB and file progress separately (two markers), advancing each only after its own write succeeds.
- [x] Test persistence with an unwritable JSONL path and with a failing DB.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** `persist_metrics()` keeps a DB marker (`db_persisted_up_to_`) next to the file marker, and each advances only
past rows its own write accepted: the DB marker one row at a time, so a DB exception leaves the failed row for the next persist, and the
file marker only after the JSONL write and close succeed. `clear_history()` and `trim_history()` adjust both markers. Tests
(`MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`):
- `UnwritableMetricsFileDoesNotDuplicateDbRows`: with the JSONL path unopenable, 10 samples give 10 DB rows. The old code left 75.
- `FailingDbRowsAreInsertedOnceWhenItRecovers`: rows whose inserts threw are inserted once, by the first persist after the DB recovers.
  The old code dropped them.

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsService.cpp` (`persist_metrics()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-529`.

- `tests/MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`

### TD-531: JSONL Training Reader Doesn't Decode `\uXXXX`, Corrupting Non-ASCII Text

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| HIGH | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 (dataset scan remains) | Data / JSONL Format | October 17, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingSampleMeta.hpp` (see [TrainingSampleMeta.md](../reference/source/TrainingSampleMeta.md)); verified. `tsm_detail::json_str()`,
used by `parse_jsonl_sample()` for every training pair (`ChatbotTrainer::load_conversation_data()`, `DatasetRegistry::count_pairs()`/segments,
`VocabBuilderHelpers::load_pairs_format()`), decodes only `\n`, `\t`, `\r`; every other escape becomes the character after the backslash. JSON writers
escape non-ASCII by default (Python `json.dumps` `ensure_ascii=True`, pandas `to_json` `force_ascii=True`): `"Caf\u00e9 au lait?"` parsed as
`Cafu00e9 au lait?` and `"Oui \u2014 tr\u00e8s bon \ud83d\ude00"` as `Oui u2014 tru00e8s bon ud83dude00`. Any dataset prepared with standard tooling
and queued through `dataset_manager add`/upload therefore trains (and builds vocabularies) on garbage wherever it has an accented letter, curly
apostrophe (`don’t` → `donu2019t`), dash or emoji, silently. `\b`, `\f`, `\/` are mis-decoded too. (DataFetcher's own output is raw UTF-8; its
HuggingFace input scanner has the same gap, TD-314.)

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** `parse_jsonl_sample()` now uses `tsm_detail::parse_object_members()`, a small top-level JSON object reader. It
decodes every escape, including `\uXXXX` and surrogate pairs (unpaired surrogates become U+FFFD), and also fixes TD-532.

It is hand-written rather than `nlohmann/json`. `nlohmann` would reject lines `sample_to_jsonl()` itself writes (raw control characters, TD-533),
silently dropping those pairs, and the header reaches many files through `ChatbotTrainer.hpp`. Correctness is checked against `nlohmann` instead.

Tests (`training_sample_meta_test.cpp`, 20 → 32):
- `\u` escapes, surrogate pairs, every standard escape, nested keys, raw control characters, repeated keys and malformed lines;
- `MatchesNlohmannOnEscapedUnicode`, 500 random lines written by `nlohmann` with `ensure_ascii`, which must decode identically;
- 9 of the new tests fail against the old reader.

The local TinyStories training file (2,119,719 lines, 0 with `\u` escapes) parses identically with the old and new readers.

Action Items:

- [x] Parse JSONL lines with full escape and surrogate-pair handling. Done with a hand-written top-level reader, cross-checked against `nlohmann/json`, for the reasons above; TD-314 and TD-453 remain open.
- [x] Add tests with `\u` escapes, surrogate pairs and every standard escape.
- [ ] Scan queued datasets for `\u` before retraining, and drop tokenized caches built from affected files so they re-tokenize. A pending file needs nothing else; re-reading it decodes correctly. Check with: `grep -lE '\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}' <registry data dir>/**/*.jsonl`. The local TinyStories copy has none.

Location in code: `src/TrainingSampleMeta.hpp` (`tsm_detail::parse_object_members()`, `parse_jsonl_sample()`); the `TODO: See TD-531` tag is now a fix comment.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingSampleMeta.hpp`
- `tests/training_sample_meta_test.cpp`

### TD-534: `vocab_builder` Defaults to Plain Text, Turning JSONL Syntax Into Vocabulary

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 17, 2026 | Tooling / vocab_builder | October 17, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while tracing `VocabBuilder.cpp` (see [VocabBuilder.md](../reference/source/VocabBuilder.md)); verified. Training data is JSONL, but `--format`
defaults to `plain`, which takes each line as raw text; the help describes `pairs` (the loader that actually parses JSONL, by a leading `{`) only as
"INPUT/RESPONSE format". On a small JSONL corpus, `--format plain` produced JSON-syntax tokens (`{`, `{"`, `input`, `response`: 6 of 99 entries) that
never appear in the text the trainer tokenizes (it parses the JSONL first); `--format pairs` produced none. On real data the wasted merges grow with
escapes and key names.

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** `--format` defaults to `auto`. `detect_input_format()` in `VocabBuilderHelpers.hpp` picks `pairs` for a file whose
first non-blank line starts with `{` or `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:` (a UTF-8 BOM is skipped), `json` for `[`, and `plain` otherwise. The help describes
`pairs` as JSONL or `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:` training data, and an explicit `--format plain` on such a file prints a warning.

On 300 TinyStories JSONL lines at `--vocab-size 400`:
- `auto` learned no `{`, `input` or `response` tokens (the 5 quote tokens left come from dialogue in the stories);
- `plain` learned 18 JSON-ish tokens.

5 new `DetectInputFormatTest` cases. OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md §4 is rewritten from `--help`.

Action Items:

- [x] Default to (or auto-detect) JSONL; describe `pairs` as "JSONL or INPUT:/RESPONSE: training files" in the help.
- [x] Warn when `plain` input looks like JSONL.

Location in code: `src/VocabBuilder.cpp` (`main()` format default, `print_usage()`), `src/VocabBuilderHelpers.hpp` (`detect_input_format()`); the `TODO: See TD-534` tag is now a fix comment.

### TD-538: Encoder Token Embedding and Final Norm Are Overwritten in Every Checkpoint

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Transformer / LLMEncoder | October 18, 2026 | 1-2 hours (plus retraining) |

Description:
Found while fixing TD-405; verified. `EncoderDecoderModel::save_model(path)` saves the encoder as `<path>.encoder` and the decoder as
`<path>.decoder`. `LLMEncoder` and `LLMDecoder` both derive their component file names by stripping the last extension, so both use the base
`<path>`. Both then wrote `<path>_token_emb.bin` and `<path>_final_norm.bin`. The decoder saves second, so the encoder's embedding and final
LayerNorm were overwritten in every checkpoint, and every load gave the encoder the decoder's copies.

Verified: a save/load round trip changed the logits by up to 1.54, and the reloaded encoder embedding differed by up to 5.08 while the decoder's
embedding and the LM head matched exactly. Every resumed training pass, every `clone()` (TD-363) and every `chatbot_api_server` that loads
`MODEL_PATH` ran its encoder on the decoder's embedding and norm.

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `LLMEncoder` now writes `<path>_encoder_token_emb.bin` and `<path>_encoder_final_norm.bin`; the decoder keeps
the old names. On load, if the encoder-specific files are missing (any checkpoint saved before the fix), the encoder falls back to the old shared
files with a warning. That is exactly what old checkpoints always loaded, so they load unchanged.

New tests: `EncoderDecoderModelTest.SaveLoadRoundTripReproducesLogits` (failed with a 1.54 logit difference before the fix) and
`LegacyCheckpointWithoutEncoderSpecificFilesStillLoads`.

Action Items:

- [x] Give the encoder's embedding and final norm their own file names, with a fallback for old checkpoints.
- [x] Test that a round trip reproduces the logits exactly.
- [ ] Retrain rather than continuing from an existing checkpoint: none has the encoder's own embedding or norm (with TD-358).
- [x] `IncrementalTrainer::remove_model_files()` (TD-407) should delete the new file names too. (Done: TD-407's prefix-based removal covers them.)

Location in code: `src/LLMEncoder.cpp` (`save_weights()`, `load_weights()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`
- `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp`

### TD-539: `IncrementalTrainer` Constructors Never Load a Checkpoint

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| **HIGH** | Open — code fix landed October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | October 18, 2026 | 1 hour |

Description:
Found while fixing TD-405; verified. All three `IncrementalTrainer` constructors chose a checkpoint from session history and then loaded it only
`if (fs::exists(best_checkpoint_path))`. That tests the bare checkpoint path, which `EncoderDecoderModel::save_model()` never writes (only
`<path>.config`, `.vocab`, `.encoder`, `.decoder`, `.lm_head`; see TD-408). So with real checkpoints the constructors never loaded anything.

`resume_last_session()` checks `<path>.config` and does load, so `trainer_service` passes resumed (from the best-ever checkpoint, TD-405). But
`incremental_trainer train`/`retrain` call `train_on_files()`, which doesn't load either, so every such pass trained from freshly initialized
weights. The existing tests didn't notice because their stand-in checkpoints also create the bare file.

Verified with the real class and real `save_model()` checkpoints: a trainer constructed over two sessions matched neither checkpoint's weights.

**Fix landed October 18, 2026 (with TD-405):** the constructors share `init_from_session_history()`, which loads `select_resume_checkpoint()`.
That only returns sessions whose sidecars all exist (`is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()`). The new test
`IncrementalTrainerTest.ResumesFromMostRecentSessionNotLowestValidationLoss` uses real checkpoints, which have no bare file.

Action Items:

- [x] Load checkpoints in the constructors using the sidecar files, not the bare path.
- [x] Test with real `save_model()` checkpoints.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (constructors, `init_from_session_history()`).

Description:
Found while reviewing the TD-411 fix against the owner's rule (October 18, 2026) that the trainer always takes its data files and configuration
from the remote services (`registry_server`, MNS) first, with local files only as fallback. `IncrementalTrainer::reset_all(keep_data_registry=true)`,
used by `incremental_trainer reset --keep-data`, re-queued trained files in two steps:
1. delete `<SESSION_DIR>/data_registry.txt`;
2. re-add each trained path with `DatasetRegistry::add_files()`, which checks that the file exists locally.

Against a remote `registry_server`, that changed nothing on the server, so no trained file was re-queued. There was also no operator command for
re-queuing at all. That's needed now: every existing checkpoint has to be retrained from scratch (TD-358, TD-538), and files a pre-TD-411/412
`resume` pass marked trained without training them can't be told apart (TD-334).

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** a server-side re-queue across every layer.
- **Transport:** `RegistryTransport::requeue_trained(paths, all, model_name)`. `LocalTransport` does it under the pending lock; `RemoteTransport`
  calls `POST /registry/<group>[/<kind>]/requeue`, which `registry_server` serves through the group's `LocalTransport`.
- **Registry:** `DatasetRegistry::requeue_trained()`.
- **CLI:** `dataset_manager requeue (--all | <file> ...) [--model <name>]`.
- **Trainer:** `reset_all()`'s keep-data branch now uses it, assigning the files to `MODEL_NAME`.

Trained entries come back as whole-file pending entries with their source, added time and checksum. A path that is already pending only loses its
trained record.

Tests: `DatasetRegistryTest.RequeueTrained*`, `LocalTransportRequeueTest`, `DatasetManagerArgsTest.RequeueArgs`. It was also checked end to end
against a real `registry_server`: two trained files were re-queued as unclaimed and assigned, the trained registry was emptied, and an empty request
got 400.

Action Items:

- [x] Re-queue through the registry transport so it works against `registry_server`; add an operator command.
- [ ] Before the TD-358 retraining: `dataset_manager requeue --all --model <name>` on the deployment (covers TD-411's audit item).
- [ ] Add re-queue to the Android ops dashboard's Registry tab, which aims for CLI parity (TD-205).
- [x] Segment ranges aren't restored on re-queue, because the trained registry has no segment concept (TD-333). (Fixed with TD-333, October 19, 2026: records carry their segment, and re-queue restores it.)

Location in code: `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_requeue()`), `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/DatasetManagerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`reset_all()`).

Files to Modify:

- (as above)
- `tests/DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`, `tests/dataset_manager_args_test.cpp`

### TD-541: A Pass Without Validation Data Has Its Checkpoint Discarded

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | October 19, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while testing TD-269 (a one-pair pass's checkpoint wasn't resumed from). `ChatbotTrainer` reports a validation loss of 0 when there is no
validation data, which happens with `VALIDATION_SPLIT=0` or when a pass has fewer pairs than the split ratio (fewer than 10 at the default).
`IncrementalTrainer::is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()` rejects any `final_validation_loss <= 0` as "never measured". So that session is never
resumed from (TD-405's rule skips it), and `cleanup_dead_sessions()` removes it from the history and deletes its checkpoint at the next start. Its
training is lost, while its files are already marked trained.

Action Items:

- [x] Record "no validation" explicitly (for example NaN or a flag in the session record) instead of 0, and treat such a session as resumable
  under the most-recent rule; keep excluding it only from lowest-loss selection.
- [x] Test: a pass with no validation split is resumed by the next pass and survives cleanup.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** A completed pass whose `ChatbotTrainer` recorded no validation loss now stores `TrainingSession::kNoValidationLoss`
(-1) instead of 0. The value round-trips through `session_history.txt` unchanged. 0 still means an in-progress session, and NaN still means a
diverged one.
- `is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()` accepts -1, so the session is resumed under the most-recent rule and survives `cleanup_dead_sessions()`.
- `has_validation_loss()` keeps it out of every lowest-loss choice: `RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT`, the best checkpoint picked at startup and
  after cleanup, and `update_best_checkpoint()`. That last one now takes an unmeasured pass as "best" only when no best exists yet, and never
  records -1 as the loss to beat.
- Other changes:
  - the MNS candidate summary leaves out `final_val_loss` for such a pass;
  - `history` and the trainer summary show "n/a" instead of a loss.

Verified: the new `PassWithoutValidationIsResumedAndSurvivesCleanup` test, a 2-pair pass, failed against the old code. Its validation loss was
0, and the next trainer's history was empty. With the fix it passes, and with `RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT=true` the session is still not
picked.

Not changed: the per-epoch callback still records 0 for the validation loss of an epoch without validation data, in the per-epoch arrays and
the MNS progress `best_loss`. These are reporting values only; they don't affect checkpoint selection.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()`, `finalize_session()`), `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (validation
loss with no validation data).

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/incrementaltrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-542: `dataset_manager segment` Keeps a Queued Whole-File Entry, So Its Pairs Train Twice

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | October 19, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while checking TD-326's fix with the real binary: `dataset_manager add f.jsonl` then `dataset_manager segment f.jsonl --count 3` left four
pending entries, the whole file plus three segments. Training that pool trains every pair twice. `segment` neither removes the whole-file entry nor
warns about it. Segmenting a file that isn't queued yet (the documented flow) is fine. The Android dashboard's "Create segments" dialog mirrors the
command's sequencing (`RegistryRepository.createSegments()`), so it likely has the same gap.

Action Items:

- [x] Owner decision (October 19, 2026): the segments replace an unclaimed whole-file entry.
- [x] Apply the same rule in the Android `createSegments()`; refuse when the whole-file entry is claimed by a run.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** `dataset_manager segment` and the Android `RegistryRepository.createSegments()` now follow the same steps:
- They look for a whole-file pending entry of the path first. If a run has claimed it, or the path already has trained records (the whole-path
  delete would erase them), they refuse before queuing anything.
- After adding the segments, they delete the unclaimed whole entry (`force=false`, so a claim taken in between makes the delete fail) and give
  the segments its model assignment.
- If that delete doesn't remove exactly one entry, the new segments are deleted again, so the file is never left queued both ways.

`createSegments()` now returns a `SegmentsResult` (`created`, `replacedWhole`, `error`), and the confirm dialog shows the extra delete call.

Verified with the real binaries, locally and against a `registry_server`. A whole entry assigned to `m1` became two or three segments assigned to
`m1`, with no whole entry left. An entry claimed by `run-01` was refused, and nothing was queued. Five Android repository tests cover the plain
path, the replacement, both refusals and the rollback. All 126 opsdashboard unit tests pass. The command still has no unit tests of its own
(TD-331).

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`segment`), `android/opsdashboard/…/RegistryRepository.kt` (`createSegments()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`
- `android/opsdashboard/src/main/java/com/adai/ops/data/registry/RegistryRepository.kt`

### TD-544: `EncoderDecoderModel::clone()` Leaves Its Temp Checkpoint Files Behind

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Model / EncoderDecoderModel | October 19, 2026 | 1 hour |

Description:
Found while rechecking `EncoderDecoderModel` after TD-358/361/538. `clone()` saves the model to a temp checkpoint in the system temp directory and
loads it back. It then removed only the five top-level files (`.config`, `.vocab`, `.encoder`, `.decoder`, `.lm_head`), but `save_model()` also
writes a component file per embedding, block and norm. So every clone left a copy of the model's weights behind. `ChatbotTrainer` clones once per
epoch for the async BLEU/ROUGE metrics, so a long run with quality metrics on fills the temp directory with full-size weight copies. This machine's
`/tmp` held 115 clones' worth (4.6 MB) from test runs alone.

Action Items:

- [x] Remove every file of the temp checkpoint (`<tmp>.…` and `<tmp>_…`), as `IncrementalTrainer::checkpoint_files()` does.
- [x] Test: a clone leaves no files in the temp directory.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** `clone()`'s cleanup removes every file in the temp directory whose name starts with the temp checkpoint's name followed
by `.` or `_`. Another clone's files can't match, since their names differ before that character. `CloneLeavesNoTempFiles` points `TMPDIR` at a
fresh folder and clones a one-layer model. The old code left 11 files and the new one none. Existing leftovers (`/tmp/adai_clone_*`) can be deleted by
hand.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`clone()`).

|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | October 19, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while rechecking `IncrementalTrainer` after TD-413 (the same root cause). `reset_all()` removed `SESSION_DIR/pending_files.txt` and
`SESSION_DIR/data_registry.txt`, the legacy root pool's files. But `incremental_trainer` always sets `DATASET_KIND` (TD-204), so its local pool is
`SESSION_DIR/<kind>/` (TD-202). So, with a local registry:
- `reset` without `--keep-data` deleted the legacy pool's queue, which isn't the trainer's, and left the trainer's own trained records in place, so
  those files stayed marked trained after a reset;
- `--keep-data` also removed the pending queue before re-queuing the trained entries. Once pointed at the right pool, that would have thrown away
  every queued but untrained file.

- [x] Keep the queue with `--keep-data`; clear it only on a full reset.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**

  `registry_server` nothing local is touched.
- **Queue kept with `--keep-data`:** the queue is removed only without `--keep-data`.
- **Fresh weights forget the old state:** `reset_model_for_config()` also clears the loaded checkpoint's training-state path (TD-269), since fresh
  weights shouldn't inherit old optimizer moments.
- **Test:** `ResetWorksOnTheTrainersOwnPoolAndKeepDataKeepsTheQueue` failed three ways on the old code: the legacy queue was deleted, the full reset
  left the kind pool's queue, and the legacy file was gone again.

### TD-547: GPU Training Does the Token Embeddings on the Host

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 19, 2026 | GPU / Training | October 19, 2026 | 4-8 hours |

Description:
Found while building TD-468's device-resident optimizer. `TokenEmbedding` has no device mirror, so GPU training still does all of this on the host:
- **Each sample:**
  - the encoder and decoder embedding lookup plus positional encoding (`LLMEncoder::gpu_encode()`, `LLMDecoder::gpu_decode()`), with the result
    uploaded;
  - the embedding backward: the gradient downloaded (`Matrix::from_gpu`) and accumulated into the host table.
- **Each accumulation window:** `model->zero_grad()` zeroes both `vocab × d_model` host gradient tables (TD-518's full-matrix zeroing).
- **Each optimizer step:** `GPUOptimizer` steps the two embedding groups on the host, a full AdamW over `vocab × d_model` parameters twice:
  - ~49M parameters at 32k × 768;
  - likely the largest remaining CPU cost of a GPU pass.

That breaks the owner's rule that GPU training does the training math on the GPU and moves no data without a critical reason.

Action Items:

- [x] Give `TokenEmbedding` a device table and gradient, a gather kernel (lookup + positional-encoding add, with a device positional table),
  and a scatter-add backward (atomic adds for repeated tokens), in both backends.
- [x] Report them from `gpu_collect_parameters()` so `GPUOptimizer` steps them on the device; leave only the token IDs and scalars crossing.
- [ ] Verify on the oneAPI CPU device against the host path, as for TD-468; measure on ai-machine. (CPU device done; ai-machine open.)

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Device table:** `TokenEmbedding` has a device table and gradient (`gpu_upload_weights()`, `gpu_download_weights()`,
  `gpu_zero_grads()`, `gpu_collect_parameters()`).
  - `gpu_forward(ids, pe, pe_rows, pos_offset)` uploads only the token IDs and runs `embedding_gather_add_pe_gpu()`: the lookup plus
    positional row `pos_offset + i`, with none past the table, as `PositionalEncoding::forward()`.
  - `gpu_backward(dout)` runs `embedding_scatter_add_gpu()`, with atomic adds, since a token can repeat.
  - Both kernels exist in CUDA and SYCL.
- **Encoder and decoder:** `LLMEncoder`/`LLMDecoder` keep a device copy of their positional table and use the device embedding in
  `gpu_encode()`, `gpu_decode()`, their `gpu_backward()`s, and the KV-cached `gpu_decode_step()`. Generation therefore reads the live device
  table during training too.
- **Optimizer:** the embeddings are now device groups, so `GPUOptimizer` steps nothing on the host for a model without the gated
  world-model/hippocampal paths: 38 device groups, 0 host groups.
- **Zeroing:** in GPU mode `ChatbotTrainer` no longer calls `model->zero_grad()` at each window start, NaN skip or failed backward. That
  zeroed every host gradient, including both `vocab × d_model` tables. It now calls `GPUOptimizer::zero_host_grads()` (host groups only)
  plus `gpu_zero_grads()`.
- **Behavior change:** `gpu_decode_step()` used to compute positional rows inline, including past `max_seq_length`, where the full forward
  adds none (TD-347). It now uses the same table rows as `gpu_decode()`.

Verified on the oneAPI CPU device (`ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`):
- **New test `DeviceEmbeddingMatchesTheHostLookupAndBackward`:**
  - the lookup equals `forward()` + `PositionalEncoding::forward()`;
  - the offset path adds rows 6–7 and nothing past the 8-row table;
  - the backward equals `backward()` with a repeated token;
  - an out-of-range ID throws.
- **`ModelStepMatchesTheDownloadAndCpuStepPath`:** now 38 device groups and 0 host, still equal to the old path.
- **Suites:** `chatbottrainerTests` (83), `encoderdecoderTests` (90) and `incrementaltrainerTests` (58) pass.
- **Real binary:** two SYCL `incremental_trainer` passes trained and resumed (global step 18 restored).

CUDA is compile-checked only.

Still crossing per sample: the token IDs and target IDs (inputs), the scalar loss, and the decoder's causal mask (`tgt²` floats built on the
host, small). The per-sample `gpu_synchronize()` (TD-390) also remains.

Location in code: `src/TokenEmbedding.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/LLMEncoder.cpp` (`gpu_encode()`, `gpu_backward()`), `src/Decoder.cpp` (`gpu_decode()`,
`gpu_backward()`), `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu`, `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp`.

### TD-548: Standalone World-Model Pool and Checkpoint Share One Directory

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| MEDIUM | Open — code fix landed October 21, 2026 | Training / World model | October 20, 2026 | 1-2 hours |

Description:
Found while verifying TD-342 end to end, and reproduced with the real binaries on the oneAPI CPU device.
- **The collision:** in standalone mode (no `REGISTRY_SERVER_URL`), `LocalTransport` keeps each kind's queue in
  `<SESSION_DIR>/<kind>/` (TD-202). `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model/` is also the default world-model checkpoint directory.
- **LeJEPA pass:** `dataset_manager --kind world_model add` creates that directory. `incremental_trainer --objective=lejepa`
  then finds it, tries to load a checkpoint from it (`Failed to open file for reading: …/world_model/config.bin`), and the
  pass exits 1.
- **Chatbot pass:** `IncrementalTrainer::maybe_attach_world_model()` sees the same directory, fails to load, and continues
  without the world model.
- **Who is affected:** `--objective=lejepa` always uses `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model` (it ignores `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH`),
  so standalone world-model training can't be configured around this. Against `registry_server` the queue lives server-side,
  so ai-machine isn't affected.

Workaround: queue the LeJEPA data under another kind and pass `--dataset-kind` (e.g. `--dataset-kind chatbot`).

Action Items:

- [x] Put the world-model checkpoint in its own directory (e.g. `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model_checkpoint`), with a fallback that
  reads an old-layout checkpoint, or move the standalone pools under `<SESSION_DIR>/pools/<kind>/` with a migration.
- [x] Have `--objective=lejepa` honor `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH`, like the chatbot attach.
- [x] Test a standalone LeJEPA pass, then a chatbot pass that attaches its world model.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (the `lejepa` world-model directory), `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
(`maybe_attach_world_model()`), `src/DatasetRegistry.cpp` (`local_pool_dir()`).

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Shared rule:** three new static helpers on `LeJEPAEncoder`, used by the LeJEPA pass, `IncrementalTrainer::maybe_attach_world_model()`
  and `chatbot_api_server`:
  - `default_checkpoint_dir()` is `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model_checkpoint`.
  - `has_checkpoint()` requires the checkpoint's `config.bin`, so a dataset pool in the same directory no longer counts.
  - `resolve_checkpoint_dir()` picks `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH` (or MNS's artifact path) when set, else the new default, else a
    pre-fix `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model` checkpoint.
- **The LeJEPA pass:** saves to `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH` when set (it used to ignore it) or the new default. A checkpoint resumed
  from the old directory moves to the new one on the next save.
- **Metrics label:** kept as `world_model`.

Verified:
- **Test:** `lejepaencoder_test.cpp`'s `CheckpointDirectoryResolution`.
- **Real binaries** (SYCL build, oneAPI CPU device):
  - the original sequence (`dataset_manager --kind world_model add`, a LeJEPA pass, then a chatbot pass) now trains and attaches the
    world model without the `--dataset-kind` workaround;
  - a session with only an old-layout checkpoint resumes it and saves to `world_model_checkpoint`.

### TD-549: FTPS Data Channel Doesn't Require TLS Session Reuse

| Priority | Status | Component | Created | Effort Estimate |
|----------|--------|-----------|---------|------------------|
| LOW | Open — code fix landed October 24, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | October 21, 2026 | 2-4 hours |

Description:
Filed while fixing TD-372. The data connection is now accepted only from the control connection's client IP, but under `PROT P`
any TLS client from that address still passes the data-channel handshake. A process on the same host as the trainer (or behind the
same NAT) could still race for the file. vsftpd's `require_ssl_reuse` closes this by requiring the data channel to resume the
control channel's TLS session. It was left out of TD-372 because session reuse interacts badly with some TLS 1.3 clients (session
tickets), and libcurl, the trainer's client, would need verifying on both sides first.

Action Items:

- [x] Enable the server session cache with a session-id context. After the data-channel `SSL_accept()`, require
  `SSL_session_reused()` and the control channel's session; refuse with 425/522 otherwise.
- [x] Verify libcurl (`CURLOPT_SSL_SESSIONID_CACHE`, on by default) still downloads under TLS 1.2 and 1.3.

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`cmd_retr()`).

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** A `PROT P` data connection must resume its own control connection's TLS session, or `RETR` answers 522
and sends nothing.
- **Why a token:** checking `SSL_session_reused()` alone isn't enough, because another client on the same host could resume a session
  from its own control connection.
- **The token:** each control connection gets a random 16-byte token, set as the SSL object's app data before its handshake.
- **Where it's carried:** `SSL_CTX_set_session_ticket_cb()` writes the token into every session ticket the server issues
  (`SSL_SESSION_set1_ticket_appdata()`), for both TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 tickets. It's also set on the control session itself, for TLS 1.2
  session-ID resumption from the server cache (`SSL_CTX_set_session_id_context()` + `SSL_SESS_CACHE_SERVER`).
- **The check:** after the data channel's `SSL_accept()`, `data_session_matches()` requires a resumed session whose ticket appdata equals
  the control connection's token (constant-time compare). The data connection issues no tickets of its own.
- **Compatibility:** OpenSSL ≥ 1.1.1 (the ticket appdata API).

Tests (`FtpDataServerTests.cpp`, an OpenSSL client against a real server, under both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3):
- `ResumingTheControlSessionDownloads`
- `FreshTlsSessionOnTheDataConnectionIsRefused`
- `AnotherControlConnectionsSessionIsRefused`: the TD-549 threat.

On the old server the two refusal tests fail under both versions; the file was delivered.

libcurl, the trainer's client, still works. `DataTransportFtpsTests` (TLS 1.3) pass. `curl --tlsv1.2 --tls-max 1.2` and `--tlsv1.3`
against a real FTPS `registry_server` (token from `acquire`) both downloaded the file byte for byte, with no refusal logged.
